subject.name: Physics
subject.syllabusDetails:
{"modules":[{"title":"MODULE - I: Relativistic Mechanics & Interference","topics":"Frame of reference, Galilean transformation, Inertial and Non-inertial frames, Postulates of special theory of relativity, Michelson-Morley experiment, Lorentz transformation of space and time, Length contraction, Time dilation, Addition of velocities, Variation of mass with velocity, Equivalence of mass and energy, Momentum-energy transformation equations.
Interference: Theory of interference of light, Conditions for sustained interference, Classification of interference, Fresnel's Biprism experiment, displacement of fringes, Interference in thin films- wedge shaped film and Newton's rings."},{"title":"MODULE - II: Diffraction & Polarization","topics":"Diffraction: Single, Double & N-slit Diffraction, Diffraction grating, Grating spectra, Rayleigh's criterion and resolving power of grating.
Polarization: Phenomena of double refraction, Doubly refracting crystals, Quarter wave plate & Half wave plate, Nicol prism, Production and analysis of plane, circular and elliptical polarized light, Optically active substance, Fresnel's theory of optical activity, Specific rotation and Polarimeters."},{"title":"MODULE - III: Laser, Holography & Fiber Optics","topics":"Laser and Holography: Spontaneous and stimulated emission of radiation, Einstein's coefficients, construction and working of Ruby, He-Ne lasers and laser applications. Basic Principle of Holography, Construction and reconstruction of Image on hologram and applications of holography.
Fiber Optics: Fundamental ideas about optical fiber, Types of fibers, Acceptance angle and cone, Numerical aperture, Propagation mechanism and communication in optical fiber, Attenuation, Signal loss in optical fiber and dispersion."}],"referenceBooks":["Aurthur Beiser, 'Concepts of Modern Physics' - (Mc-GrawHill)","Robert Resnick - 'Introduction to Special theory of Relativity' - Wiley","Ajoy Ghatak, 'Optics' - (TMH) Brijlal & Subramanian (S. Chand)","Anuradha De., 'Optical Fibre & Laser' - (New Age)"]}

Linked List: Singly linked lists: Representation in memory, Algorithms of several operations: Traversing, Searching, Insertion into, Deletion from linked list; Linked representation of Stack and Queue, Header nodes, Doubly linked list: operations on it and algorithmic analysis; Circular Linked Lists: all operations their algorithms and the complexity analysis. Development Management, Team models, Requirements process, Configuration, management, Software metrics, Programming languages & tools, Managing conflict and motivating, MS-Project: Assigning Resources."},{"title":"MODULE III: Project Control, System Test Process & Final Phases","topics":"Project Control, Status reporting, Project metrics, Earned value analysis, Communications Techniques, Process Improvement, MS Project: (a) Resource leveling (b) Other views
System Test Process, Test specifications, Black box and white box testing, Test scripts, Unit and integration testing, Acceptance test specifications, Test tools, MS Project:(a) Reporting.
Final Phases & Other Issues, Project Recovery, Documentation, Cutover/Migration Post Project Reviews, Closing, MS Project: (a) Advanced features."}],"textBooks":["S. McConnell, "Software Project Survival Guide" (1997)","W. Royce, "Software Project Management: A Unified Framework", (1998)"],"referenceBooks":["S. McConnell, "Software Project Survival Guide" (1997)","S. Berkun, "The Art of Project Management", (2005)","C. Larman, "Agile and Iterative Development: A Manager's Guide", (2003)","W. Royce, "Software Project Management: A Unified Framework", (1998)","J. Highsmith, "Agile Project Management: Creating Innovative Products", (2004)","T. DeMarco, "The Deadline: A Novel About Project Management", (1997)","T. DeMarco, "Peopleware: Productive Projects and Teams", (1999)","E. Bennatan, "On Time Within Budget: Software Project Management Practices and Techniques", (2000)"]}

subject.name: Networking Protocols
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To study network design principles, OSI and TCP/IP protocol suites, ATM cell transport, client-server socket programming, and next-generation IPv6 routing architectures.","outcomes":"Scholars will master protocol implementations, socket-level network engineering, multicast routing, and internet security.","modules":[{"title":"MODULE I: Networks & Services, OSI Reference Model & IP Routing","topics":"Networks and Services, Approaches to Network Design, The OSI Reference Model; Overview of TCP/IP Architecture, Application Protocols and TCP/IP Utilities, Internet Architecture Interconnection through IP Routers, Internet Protocol (IP), User datagram protocol (UDP)."},{"title":"MODULE II: Routing Cores, Multicast, ATM Networks & Internet Services","topics":"Routing Cores - peers Algorithms Autonomous Systems Exterior Gateway Protocol Multicast Address. Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) and Implementation. TCP/IP over ATM networks: ATM cell Transport, Adaptation Layer, IP Address Building in an ATM network Logical IP subnet Concept ATMARP packet format. Domain name system, Remote Login (Telnet, Rlogin) File Transfer and Access (FTP, TFTP, NFS), Electronic mail (SMTP, MIME) Internet Management (SNMP, SNMPV2) Internet Security and Firewall Design Post Office Protocol (POP) Network News Transfer Protocol (NNTP)."},{"title":"MODULE III: TCP/IP Transport Layer, Socket API & Client-Server Systems","topics":"TCP/IP over view- The Transport Layer: TCP and UDP. Elementary TCP Sockets. TCP Client-Server Example. I/O Multiplexing: The select and poll Functions. Socket Options. Elementary UDP Sockets. Elementary Name and Address Conversions. The Client Server Model and Software Design, Concurrent Processing in Client-Server Software, Iterative, Connectionless Servers (UDP), Iterative, Connection-Oriented Servers (TCP), Concurrent, Connection-Oriented Servers (TCP). Single-Process, Concurrent Servers (TCP). Multiprotocol Servers (TCP, UDP), Multiservice Servers (TCP, UDP). Uniform, Efficient Management of server. Concurrency in clients. TCP/IP Architecture, The Internet Protocol, Limitations of IPv4 and Introduction to IPv6, User Datagram Protocol, Transmission Control Protocol, DHCP, Introduction to Internet Routing Protocols"}],"textBooks":["A. Leon-Garcia, Indra Widjaja, \"Communication Networks\", Tata McGraw Hill, 2000","William Stallings, \"Data and Computer Communications\", Pearson Education, 7th Edition."],"referenceBooks":["A. Leon-Garcia, Indra Widjaja, \"Communication Networks\", Tata McGraw Hill, 2000","William Stallings, \"Data and Computer Communications\", Pearson Education, 7th Edition.","Andrew S. Tanenbaum, \"Computer Networks\", Prentice Hall India, 4th Edition, 2003","W.Richard Stevens: TCP/IP Illustrated vol 1: The Protocols, Pearson Edun. Asia, 2000.","Douglas Comer: Internetworking with TCP/IP vol.1: Principles, Protocols and Architecture, Prentice Hall, 4th edition, 2000"]}

subject.name: Real Time Systems
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To analyze real-time computing constraints, task models, periodic and aperiodic scheduling algorithms, resource contention control, and multi-processor validation.","outcomes":"Scholars will be able to design predictable real-time embedded systems, verify schedulability bounds, and implement priority ceiling protocols.","modules":[{"title":"MODULE I: Issues in Real Time Computing, Task Models & Scheduling","topics":"Time System, Issues in real time computing, Performance measures of Real Time System, Issues in Real Time Computing, Performance measures of Real time Systems, Real Time Application.Task Assignment and Scheduling: Different task model, Scheduling hierarchy, offline vs Online Scheduling, Clock Drives. Model of Real Time System: Processor, resources, temporal parameter, Periodic Task Model, Sporadic Task Model, Precedence Constraints and Data Dependencies, Scheduling hierarchy Scheduling of Periodic Task: Assumptions, fixed versus dynamic priority algorithms, schedulability test for fixed priority task with arbitrary deadlines."},{"title":"MODULE II: Scheduling of Aperiodic & Sporadic Tasks","topics":"Scheduling of Aperiodic and Sporadic Tasks: Assumptions and approaches, deferrable, sporadic servers, slack stealing in deadline driven and fixed priority systems. Two level scheme for integrated scheduling, Scheduling for applications having flexible constrains."},{"title":"MODULE III: Resources Access Control & Real Time Protocols","topics":"Resources and Resource Access Control: Assumptions on resources and their usage, resource contention, resource access control(Priority Ceiling Protocol, Priority Inheritance protocol, Slack Based Priority Ceiling Protocol, Peremption Ceiling Protocol). Multi Processor Scheduling: Model of multi processor and distributed systems, Scheduling algorithms for end to end periodic tasks in homogeneous/heterogeneous systems, Predictability and validation of dynamic multiprocessor system. Real time Communication: Model of real time Communication, Priority base service For switched network, Weighted Round Robin Service, Medium access Control Protocol, Real Time Protocol."}],"textBooks":["Jane .W. S. Liu Real Time Systems Pearson Education.","Krishna .C.M Real Time Systems Mc-Graw Hill Publication"],"referenceBooks":["Jane .W. S. Liu Real Time Systems Pearson Education.","Krishna .C.M Real Time Systems Mc-Graw Hill Publication"]}

subject.name: Research Methodology
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"Foundational compulsory doctoral paper covering systematic research design, scientific investigation, statistical analysis, hypothesis testing, literature synthesis, and scholarly writing.","outcomes":"Scholars will formulate research hypotheses, execute statistical tests, conduct systematic literature reviews, and author peer-reviewed manuscripts.","modules":[{"title":"Unit I: Foundations & Objectives of Research","topics":"Meaning, objectives, and motivation of scientific and engineering research. Types of research: Descriptive vs. Analytical, Applied vs. Fundamental, Quantitative vs. Qualitative, Conceptual vs. Empirical. Criteria of good scientific research and ethical imperatives."},{"title":"Unit II: Research Problem Formulation & Literature Survey","topics":"Identifying, delineating, and formulating engineering research problems. Systematic literature review methodologies (PRISMA framework and synthesis matrices). Formulation of null and alternate hypotheses (H0 vs. H1). Sampling methods and measurement errors."},{"title":"Unit III: Data Analysis, Statistical Inference & Software Tools","topics":"Quantitative data processing: descriptive statistics, dispersion, and central tendencies. Inferential statistics: parametric vs. non-parametric hypothesis tests (t-test, z-test, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, Chi-square). Regression analysis and statistical computing environments (R and Python)."},{"title":"Unit IV: Scholarly Dissemination, Technical Writing & Reference Management","topics":"Structure of an academic engineering paper (IMRaD framework). Reference management tools: Zotero, Mendeley, and BibTeX. Overleaf and LaTeX typesetting for conference and journal manuscripts."},{"title":"Unit V: Intellectual Property Rights & Academic Integrity","topics":"Intellectual Property Rights: Patents, Copyrights, Trademarks, and Trade Secrets. Patent filing procedure in India and internationally (PCT). Plagiarism metrics, Turnitin/Urkund verification."}],"textBooks":["C. R. Kothari, \"Research Methodology: Methods and Techniques\", New Age International","Wayne Goddard, Stuart Melville, \"Research Methodology: An Introduction\", Juta & Co"],"referenceBooks":["Donald H. McBurney, \"Research Methods\", Thomson Learning"]}

subject.name: Research and Publication Ethics
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"UGC-mandated course covering moral philosophy, scientific misconduct, publication ethics, predatory publishing awareness, and database metrics.","outcomes":"Scholars will identify predatory publishers, avoid publication misconduct, and adhere to COPE ethics guidelines.","modules":[{"title":"Module 1: Philosophy, Ethics & Scientific Misconduct","topics":"Moral philosophy, nature of moral judgments and reactions, professional ethics. Scientific misconduct: Fabrication, Falsification, and Plagiarism (FFP). Redundant and duplicate publications, salami slicing."},{"title":"Module 2: Publication Ethics, Predatory Publishing & Metrics","topics":"Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) guidelines. Predatory journals and publishers: Identifying fake metrics, deceptive conferences (Think-Check-Submit). Indexing and citation databases: Web of Science (SCIE), Scopus, PubMed. Research metrics: Impact Factor, CiteScore, h-index, g-index."}],"textBooks":["P. Chaddah, \"Ethics in Competitive Research: Do not get scooped; do not get plagiarized\", ISBN: 978-9387480865","National Academy of Sciences, \"On Being a Scientist: A Guide to Responsible Conduct in Research\", The National Academies Press"],"referenceBooks":["COPE guidelines: https://publicationethics.org"]}

subject.name: Doctoral Seminar & Research Literature Survey
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"Critical literature survey paper presented before the Departmental Research Committee (DRC) focusing on candidate's chosen research domain, identifying key gaps, and formulating the initial research proposal.","outcomes":"Scholars will produce a publishable state-of-the-art survey and defend their doctoral research direction.","modules":[{"title":"Literature Survey & Seminar Defense","topics":"Comprehensive review of minimum 30–50 high-impact peer-reviewed papers in the domain. Preparation of a state-of-the-art survey document with comparative taxonomy. Oral defense and presentation before the Research Advisory Committee (RAC)."}],"textBooks":[],"referenceBooks":[]}

subject.name: Mathematics-I
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To provide foundational knowledge of series, determinants, vectors, trigonometry, and single-variable differential calculus required for polytechnic engineering disciplines.","outcomes":["Students will be able to solve arithmetic/geometric progressions, calculate determinants using Cramer's rule, apply vector algebra, manipulate complex numbers, and compute derivatives of standard algebraic, trigonometric, and exponential functions."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit I (Series & Progressions)","topics":"Arithmetic Progression (A.P.) and Geometric Progression (G.P.): nth term, sum to n terms, Arithmetic Mean and Geometric Mean. Binomial theorem for positive, negative and fractional index (without proof). Practical applications of Binomial theorem."},{"title":"Unit II (Determinants & Vector Algebra)","topics":"Determinants: Elementary properties of determinants of order 2 and 3, multiplication system of algebraic equations, consistency of linear equations, Cramer's rule.\nVector Algebra: Dot and cross product of two vectors, scalar and vector triple products, work done and moment of a force."},{"title":"Unit III (Trigonometry & Complex Numbers)","topics":"De Moivre's theorem and its applications, roots of complex numbers, Euler's formula, expansion of sin(nθ) and cos(nθ), circular and hyperbolic functions, inverse hyperbolic functions."},{"title":"Unit IV (Differential Calculus - I)","topics":"Concept of function, domain and range, limits, standard limits, continuity of a function, differentiability, derivative of simple algebraic, trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, and inverse functions. Successive differentiation, Leibnitz's theorem."}],"textBooks":["H.K. Dass, \"Applied Mathematics for Polytechnics\", S. Chand & Company Ltd.","B.S. Grewal, \"Higher Engineering Mathematics\", Khanna Publishers."],"referenceBooks":["Erwin Kreyszig, \"Advanced Engineering Mathematics\", John Wiley & Sons.","R.S. Aggarwal, \"Senior Secondary School Mathematics\", Bharati Bhavan."]}

subject.name: Applied Physics
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To establish fundamental physical concepts in mechanics, properties of matter, heat, electrostatics, and modern optics essential for engineering students.","outcomes":["Scholars will understand vector resolution, laws of motion, friction, elasticity, fluid dynamics, thermodynamic principles, electric fields, and basic laser applications."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit I (Vector & Motion)","topics":"Scalar and vector quantities, Cartesian components, scalar and vector products. Parabolic motion, projectiles thrown horizontally and at an angle, time of flight, horizontal range, maximum height. Circular motion, angular velocity, angular acceleration, centripetal and centrifugal forces."},{"title":"Unit II (Work, Power, Energy & Friction)","topics":"Work done by constant and variable forces, potential and kinetic energy, conservation of mechanical energy. Friction: Static and dynamic friction, laws of friction, angle of friction, angle of repose, rolling friction, lubrication."},{"title":"Unit III (Properties of Matter & Fluid Statics)","topics":"Elasticity, Hooke's law, Young's, bulk and rigidity modulus. Surface tension, surface energy, capillary action. Viscosity, streamline and turbulent flow, Stokes' law, terminal velocity, Poiseuille's formula, Bernoulli's theorem and applications."},{"title":"Unit IV (Heat & Thermodynamics)","topics":"Modes of heat transfer: Conduction, convection, radiation. Thermal conductivity, Fourier's law. Laws of thermodynamics: Zeroth, First, and Second laws, isothermal and adiabatic processes, specific heat of gases."},{"title":"Unit V (Electrostatics & Modern Physics)","topics":"Coulomb's law, electric field, electric potential, Gauss's law and applications. Capacitors, capacitance in series and parallel combinations. Photoelectric effect, Einstein's photoelectric equation. Lasers: Spontaneous and stimulated emission, population inversion, optical fibers."}],"textBooks":["Arthur Beiser, \"Applied Physics\", McGraw-Hill.","R.K. Gaur & S.L. Gupta, \"Engineering Physics\", Dhanpat Rai Publications."],"referenceBooks":["Resnick, Halliday & Walker, \"Fundamentals of Physics\", Wiley.","Pradeep's Fundamental Physics, Pradeep Publications."]}

subject.name: Fundamentals of Electrical & Electronics Engineering
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To provide foundational concepts of DC circuits, AC circuits, magnetic systems, electrical machines, and basic semiconductor devices.","outcomes":["Students will analyze DC circuits using Ohm's and Kirchhoff's laws, compute AC quantities, understand transformer principles, and comprehend diode and transistor operations."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Basic Electrical Terminology & DC Circuits)","topics":"Current, EMF, potential difference, resistance, resistivity, conductors and insulators, insulation resistance of cables. Temperature coefficient of resistance. Electrical power, energy and SI units, heating effect of electric current. Ohm's law, Kirchhoff's laws (KCL, KVL) and simple circuit problems."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Network Theorems)","topics":"Star-delta and delta-star conversions. Superposition theorem, Thevenin's theorem, Norton's theorem, Maximum power transfer theorem applied to direct current networks."},{"title":"Unit 3 (AC Fundamentals)","topics":"Generation of alternating voltage and current, sinusoidal waveforms, cycle, frequency, time period, amplitude, instantaneous value, average and RMS values, form factor, peak factor. Phasor representation. Behavior of pure R, L, C, series R-L, R-C, and R-L-C circuits, power factor and resonance."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Magnetic Circuits & Transformers)","topics":"Magnetic field, flux, flux density, magnetic field strength, reluctance, permeability, comparison of electric and magnetic circuits. Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction, Lenz's law. Single-phase transformer: Principle, construction, EMF equation, turn ratio, losses and efficiency."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Semiconductor Devices)","topics":"Conductors, insulators, and semiconductors. Intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors, P-type and N-type. P-N junction diode: Forward and reverse biasing, V-I characteristics. Half-wave and full-wave rectifiers, Zener diode. Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT): NPN, PNP, CE, CB, CC configurations."}],"textBooks":["V.N. Mittle & Arvind Mittal, \"Basic Electrical Engineering\", McGraw-Hill.","Albert Malvino & David Bates, \"Electronic Principles\", McGraw-Hill."],"referenceBooks":["B.L. Theraja & A.K. Theraja, \"A Textbook of Electrical Technology\", S. Chand.","Boylestad & Nashelsky, \"Electronic Devices and Circuit Theory\", Pearson."]}

subject.name: Fundamentals of Computer
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To introduce computer architecture, operating system interfaces, binary data representation, office productivity applications, and internet networking basics.","outcomes":["Students will identify hardware components, navigate desktop operating systems, convert number systems, produce documents/worksheets, and utilize internet tools securely."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit-I (Introduction to Computer)","topics":"Characteristics of computers, what computers can do and cannot do, classification of digital computer systems, anatomy of digital computer. Usage of computer systems in office, publication, reservation, banking. Components of PC: Mouse, keyboard, CPU, monitor, printers, scanners, modem, memory, sound cards, USB pen drives."},{"title":"Unit-II (Operating System Concepts - Windows)","topics":"Working with Windows desktop, icons, taskbar, start menu, My Documents, My Computer, Control Panel, Recycle bin. Concepts of drives, folders, files. Windows accessories: Notepad, WordPad, Paint, clock, calendar, calculator."},{"title":"Unit-III (Data Representation & Multimedia)","topics":"Data representation, ASCII code, EBCDIC code, decimal, binary, octal, hexadecimal number systems and interconversions. Multimedia basics: Digital images, analog to digital conversion, digital audio and digital video."},{"title":"Unit-IV (GUI-Based Software - MS Office)","topics":"MS-Word: Menus, toolbars, creating, formatting, tables, clipboard. MS-Excel: Working with workbooks, rows, columns, formulas, functions, charts and types. MS-PowerPoint: Slides, presentations, layout, graphs, animation effects, slide sorter, reading view."},{"title":"Unit-V (Internet & Algorithms)","topics":"History of Internet, equipment required for Internet connection, browsers (Internet Explorer, Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome). Search engines, emails. Algorithms: Introduction, basic operations, pseudocode and flowcharts. VDU and printers, raster scanning, display terminals."}],"textBooks":["P.K. Sinha & Priti Sinha, \"Computer Fundamentals\", BPB Publications.","V. Rajaraman, \"Fundamentals of Computers\", Prentice Hall of India."],"referenceBooks":["Peter Norton, \"Introduction to Computers\", McGraw-Hill.","ITL Education Solutions, \"Introduction to Information Technology\", Pearson."]}

subject.name: Applied Physics Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To verify physical laws and measurement principles through laboratory experiments.","outcomes":["Students gain practical mastery of precision measuring instruments, mechanics apparatus, and optics experiments."],"labExperiments":["Measurement of dimensions of a cylinder and sphere using Vernier Calipers.","Measurement of wire diameter and thickness of metal sheets using Screw Gauge.","Determination of radius of curvature of a spherical surface using a Spherometer.","Determination of acceleration due to gravity (g) using a Simple Pendulum.","Verification of Parallelogram Law of Forces.","Determination of coefficient of viscosity of a liquid using Stokes' Method.","Determination of focal length of a convex lens using u-v method.","Measurement of surface tension of water using capillary rise method.","Determination of refractive index of glass prism using spectrometer."]}

subject.name: Electrical & Electronics Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To provide hands-on experience in circuit assembly, measuring electrical quantities, and characterizing semiconductor diodes.","outcomes":["Students will be able to construct basic circuits, use multimeters and oscilloscopes, verify circuit laws, and measure rectifier performance."],"labExperiments":["Verification of Ohm's Law and calculation of resistance.","Verification of Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) and Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL).","Measurement of voltage, current, and power in DC series and parallel circuits.","Calibration of ammeter and voltmeter using standard meters.","Plotting V-I characteristics of a P-N junction diode under forward and reverse bias.","Measurement of ripple factor and efficiency of Half-Wave and Full-Wave Rectifiers.","Testing and study of Zener diode voltage regulation characteristics."]}

subject.name: Computer Concept Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To provide practical fluency in PC hardware identification, operating system navigation, document creation, data analysis, and presentations.","outcomes":["Students will configure PC systems, format documents, write Excel formulas, build presentation slide decks, and execute internet operations."],"labExperiments":["Demonstration and identification of internal PC hardware components (CPU, RAM, HDD/SSD, SMPS, motherboard expansion slots).","Operating System navigation: File management, folder structures, file attributes, Control Panel settings, and accessories.","MS-Word: Creation of professional resume and technical report with headers, footers, tables, and borders.","MS-Excel: Creating student marksheets, calculating total, percentage, grade using IF conditions and SUM/AVERAGE functions.","MS-Excel: Data visualization using bar charts, pie charts, line graphs, and conditional formatting.","MS-PowerPoint: Developing a 10-slide technical presentation incorporating slide transitions, animations, and graphics.","Internet utilities: Web search techniques, email account configuration, attachments, and cloud storage backup."]}

subject.name: Engineering Drawing - I
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To develop spatial visualization skills and introduce standards of engineering graphics, projection techniques, and dimensioning.","outcomes":["Students will produce technical drawings adhering to Indian Standard (IS) conventions, construct scales, and project orthographic views."],"labExperiments":["Drawing instruments, sheet layout, borders, title block, and IS code conventions.","Lettering techniques: Vertical and inclined single-stroke letters and numerals (Sheet 1).","Dimensioning rules and practice of aligned and unidirectional dimensioning systems (Sheet 2).","Construction of Plain Scales and Diagonal Scales (Sheet 3).","Orthographic projections of points situated in all four quadrants (Sheet 4).","Orthographic projections of straight lines parallel, inclined to one or both reference planes (Sheet 5).","Projections of simple regular planes (triangle, square, hexagon, circle) (Sheet 6)."]}

subject.name: General Proficiency
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To assess and develop student conduct, discipline, punctuality, institutional engagement, and extracurricular participation.","outcomes":["Demonstrated professional etiquette, active team collaboration, disciplined academic presence, and co-curricular contribution."]}

subject.name: Mathematics-II
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To provide advanced mathematical tools in set theory, differential calculus, integral calculus, and first-order ordinary differential equations.","outcomes":["Students will apply set relations and mappings, evaluate higher-order derivatives, compute definite and indefinite integrals, calculate areas and volumes, and solve first-order differential equations."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit I (Set Theory & Relations)","topics":"Set theory: Sets, subsets, relations, equivalence relations, equivalence classes. Functions and mappings: Injective, surjective, bijective mappings, composition of functions, inverse mapping."},{"title":"Unit II (Differential Calculus - II)","topics":"Higher order derivatives, Taylor's and Maclaurin's series for single variable functions. Partial differentiation, Euler's theorem for homogeneous functions. Tangents and normals, maxima and minima of single variable functions."},{"title":"Unit III (Integral Calculus)","topics":"Integration: Concept of integration as anti-derivatives. Integration of elementary functions, integration by substitution, integration by parts, integration by partial fractions. Definite integrals: Definition, properties, evaluation of simple definite integrals."},{"title":"Unit IV (Applications of Integration)","topics":"Applications of definite integrals: Finding areas bounded by plane curves, length of plane curves. Volumes and surface areas of solids of revolution. Numerical integration: Trapezoidal rule and Simpson's 1/3rd rule."},{"title":"Unit V (Differential Equations)","topics":"Differential equations: Definition, order and degree of a differential equation. Formation of differential equations. Solution of first order and first degree differential equations: Separation of variables, homogeneous equations, linear differential equations, Bernoulli's equation."}],"textBooks":["H.K. Dass, \"Applied Mathematics-II for Polytechnics\", S. Chand & Company Ltd.","B.S. Grewal, \"Higher Engineering Mathematics\", Khanna Publishers."],"referenceBooks":["Erwin Kreyszig, \"Advanced Engineering Mathematics\", John Wiley & Sons.","N.P. Bali & Manish Goyal, \"A Textbook of Engineering Mathematics\", Laxmi Publications."]}

subject.name: Applied Chemistry
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To impart essential chemical concepts covering atomic structure, water treatment, fuels, corrosion, and modern polymers relevant to engineering applications.","outcomes":["Students will understand atomic orbital principles, analyze water hardness and softening techniques, evaluate fuels, understand corrosion mechanisms, and identify engineering polymers."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit I (Atomic Structure & Chemical Bonding)","topics":"Basic concept of atomic structure, de-Broglie wave equation, quantum numbers, Heisenberg's uncertainty principle, shapes of s, p, and d orbitals. Chemical bonding: Ionic, covalent, coordinate bonds. Molecular Orbital Theory (MOT) applied to homonuclear and heteronuclear diatomic molecules, hydrogen bonding."},{"title":"Unit II (Water Technology)","topics":"Hardness of water: Types of hardness (temporary and permanent), units of hardness. Estimation of hardness by EDTA method. Boiler troubles: Scale and sludge formation, priming and foaming, caustic embrittlement. Water softening methods: Lime-soda process, Zeolite process, Ion-exchange demineralization."},{"title":"Unit III (Fuels & Combustion)","topics":"Classification of fuels, calorific value, gross and net calorific value (GCV and NCV), determination of calorific value by Bomb Calorimeter. Solid fuels: Proximate and ultimate analysis of coal. Liquid fuels: Petroleum refining, knocking, octane number, cetane number."},{"title":"Unit IV (Corrosion & Lubrication)","topics":"Corrosion: Definition, dry and wet (electrochemical) corrosion, galvanic series, factors affecting corrosion rate, prevention methods (cathodic protection, sacrificial anode, metallic coatings). Lubricants: Functions, mechanism of lubrication, properties (viscosity, flash and fire point, cloud and pour point)."},{"title":"Unit V (Polymers & Engineering Materials)","topics":"Polymers: Classification, addition and condensation polymerization. Preparation, properties, and applications of polyethylene, PVC, Teflon, Bakelite, and Nylon-6,6. Brief introduction to composites, refractory materials, and Portland cement."}],"textBooks":["P.C. Jain & Monika Jain, \"Engineering Chemistry\", Dhanpat Rai Publishing Company.","S.S. Dara, \"A Textbook of Engineering Chemistry\", S. Chand & Company."],"referenceBooks":["Shashi Chawla, \"A Textbook of Engineering Chemistry\", Dhanpat Rai Publications.","Gopi K. Nayak, \"Applied Chemistry for Polytechnics\", Foundation Books."]}

subject.name: Fundamentals of Mechanical & Civil Engineering
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To provide an integrated understanding of thermal/fluid systems, prime movers, building materials, construction practices, and land surveying.","outcomes":["Students will describe energy sources and boilers, explain IC engine mechanisms, identify construction materials, and understand surveying principles."],"modules":[{"title":"Part A - Unit 1 (Sources of Energy & Fuels)","topics":"Sources of energy: Conventional and non-conventional forms - thermal, hydel, tidal, wind, solar, biomass, nuclear energy. Common fuels: Solid, liquid, gaseous fuels, higher and lower calorific values, combustion equations."},{"title":"Part A - Unit 2 (Steam Generators & Prime Movers)","topics":"Steam generators: Classification of boilers, Cochran boiler, Babcock and Wilcox boiler, boiler mountings (safety valve, water level indicator, pressure gauge) and accessories (economizer, superheater, air preheater). Internal Combustion (IC) engines: 2-stroke and 4-stroke petrol and diesel engines, working cycles."},{"title":"Part A - Unit 3 (Power Transmission)","topics":"Elements of power transmission: Belt drives, rope drives, chain drives, gear drives. Comparison of belt, chain, and gear drives, velocity ratio, slip, creep, and types of gears."},{"title":"Part B - Unit 4 (Civil Engineering Building Materials)","topics":"Building materials: Bricks (characteristics of good brick, classification), stones (quarrying, dressing), cement (types and setting properties), sand, aggregate, mortar, plain and reinforced cement concrete (PCC and RCC), timber (types, seasoning)."},{"title":"Part B - Unit 5 (Building Construction & Surveying)","topics":"Foundations: Types of shallow and deep foundations. Masonry construction: Brick masonry bonds (English and Flemish bonds). Surveying: Chain surveying, instruments, chaining, ranging, prismatic compass surveying, concept of leveling, bench marks, and reduced levels."}],"textBooks":["Pravin Kumar, \"Basic Mechanical Engineering\", Pearson Education.","B.C. Punmia, \"Basic Civil Engineering\", Laxmi Publications."],"referenceBooks":["R.K. Rajput, \"Basic Mechanical Engineering\", Laxmi Publications.","S. Ramamrutham, \"Basic Civil Engineering\", Dhanpat Rai Publications."]}

subject.name: Fundamentals of Mechanics
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To develop problem-solving capability in static equilibrium, coplanar force systems, centroids, friction, and mechanics of materials.","outcomes":["Students will calculate force resultants, solve equilibrium problems using Lami's theorem, locate centroids, determine mechanical advantage, and calculate stress-strain relationships."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Introduction & Force Systems)","topics":"Mechanics and its utility. Concept of scalar and vector quantities, effect of a force, tension and compression, rigid body. Principle of physical independence of forces, principle of transmissibility of forces. Coplanar and non-coplanar forces, concurrent, parallel, and non-concurrent force systems."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Equilibrium & Moments)","topics":"Resultant of forces: Parallelogram law of forces, triangle law of forces, polygon law of forces. Resolution and composition of forces. Moments and couples: Varignon's theorem, conditions of equilibrium for concurrent and coplanar forces, Lami's theorem."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Center of Gravity & Centroid)","topics":"Concept of center of gravity and centroid. Centroids of plane figures: Rectangle, triangle, circle, semi-circle. Centroids of composite sections: T-section, I-section, L-section, channel section."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Friction & Simple Machines)","topics":"Friction: Types of friction, laws of static friction, limiting friction, coefficient of friction, angle of friction, angle of repose. Simple machines: Mechanical advantage (MA), velocity ratio (VR), efficiency, law of machine, reversible and self-locking machines, simple screw jack, wheel and axle."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Stresses, Strains & Thin Shells)","topics":"Concept of stress and strain, tensile, compressive, and shear stress, Hooke's law, modulus of elasticity, Poisson's ratio, stress-strain curve for mild steel. Introduction to thin cylindrical and spherical shells subjected to internal pressure, longitudinal and circumferential stresses."}],"textBooks":["R.K. Bansal, \"A Textbook of Engineering Mechanics\", Laxmi Publications.","R.S. Khurmi, \"Applied Mechanics\", S. Chand & Company."],"referenceBooks":["D.S. Kumar, \"Engineering Mechanics\", S.K. Kataria & Sons.","S.S. Bhavikatti, \"Engineering Mechanics\", New Age International."]}

subject.name: Applied Chemistry Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To perform quantitative chemical analysis including water quality testing, fuel proximate analysis, and lubricant characterization.","outcomes":["Students will determine water hardness, measure pH, quantify moisture and ash in coal, and measure oil flash point and viscosity."],"labExperiments":["Determination of temporary and permanent hardness of water sample using standard EDTA solution.","Determination of total alkalinity of water sample using phenolphthalein and methyl orange indicators.","Measurement of pH of various chemical solutions using digital pH meter and pH paper.","Determination of moisture, volatile matter, and ash content in a coal sample (Proximate Analysis).","Determination of Flash Point and Fire Point of lubricating oils using Pensky-Martens apparatus.","Measurement of kinematic viscosity of lubricating oils using Redwood Viscometer.","Preparation of a urea-formaldehyde / phenol-formaldehyde resin in the laboratory."]}

subject.name: Civil & Mechanical Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To conduct experimental testing on construction materials, mechanical engines, and basic land survey operations.","outcomes":["Students will determine compressive strength of bricks, test steel tensile limits on UTM, inspect engine components, and execute chain and compass survey."],"labExperiments":["Determination of compressive strength of common building bricks using Compression Testing Machine.","Tensile testing of mild steel specimen on Universal Testing Machine (UTM) and plotting stress-strain graph.","Study and performance demonstration of two-stroke and four-stroke petrol engine cut models.","Study and performance demonstration of two-stroke and four-stroke diesel engine cut models.","Study of high-pressure and low-pressure boiler models (Babcock & Wilcox and Lancashire Boilers).","Chain surveying: Measuring distance between stations, chaining, ranging, and setting perpendicular offsets.","Prismatic compass surveying: Measurement of fore and back bearings of a closed traverse."]}

subject.name: Workshop Practice
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To impart fundamental manufacturing skills across carpentry, fitting, welding, sheet metal, and plumbing shops.","outcomes":["Students will produce timber joints, perform manual metal filing, execute electric arc welding, fabricate sheet metal utensils, and thread plumbing pipes."],"labExperiments":["Carpentry Shop: Identification of carpentry tools; preparation of Half-Lap Joint and Mortise & Tenon Joint.","Fitting Shop: Filing, sawing, marking, drilling, and preparation of a square or V-groove fitting job from mild steel plate.","Welding Shop: Demonstration of Arc and Gas welding equipment; preparation of Lap Joint and Butt Joint using manual metal arc welding.","Sheet Metal Shop: Development of patterns and fabrication of a rectangular sheet metal tray with wired edges.","Plumbing Shop: Cutting, threading, and assembling G.I. pipes with elbows, tees, unions, and gate valves."]}

subject.name: Engineering Drawing - II
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To advance technical drawing skills into isometric projections, sections of solids, surface developments, and fasteners.","outcomes":["Students will construct isometric views, draw section planes through solids, develop lateral surfaces, and render mechanical fasteners."],"labExperiments":["Projections of regular solids: Prisms, pyramids, cylinders, and cones inclined to reference planes (Sheet 1).","Sections of solids: Section plane parallel and inclined to reference planes, true shape of sections (Sheet 2).","Development of lateral surfaces of right prisms, cylinders, pyramids, and truncated cones (Sheet 3).","Isometric projections of plane figures, prisms, cylinders, and composite solids (Sheet 4).","Thread profiles: Metric, Whitworth, square, acme, and knuckle threads (Sheet 5).","Drawings of hexagonal and square head bolts, nuts, washers, studs, and foundation bolts (Sheet 6)."]}

subject.name: General Proficiency
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To evaluate discipline, professional growth, institutional activities, and semester conduct.","outcomes":["Demonstrated adherence to code of conduct, teamwork, attendance compliance, and active participation in engineering exhibitions."]}

subject.name: Digital Electronics
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To understand number systems, Boolean logic simplification, combinational circuit design, flip-flops, and sequential circuit architectures.","outcomes":["Students will be able to minimize Boolean functions, design adders, decoders, multiplexers, build synchronous/asynchronous counters, and analyze shift registers."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Number Systems & Codes)","topics":"Review of number systems: Binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal. Inter-conversions. Complements: 1's and 2's complements, binary subtraction. Binary codes: BCD, Excess-3, Gray code, parity bits, Hamming code for error detection and correction."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Boolean Algebra & Logic Gates)","topics":"Logic gates: AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR. Universal logic gates. Boolean algebra laws, De Morgan's theorems. Standard representation of logic functions: SOP and POS forms. Karnaugh Maps (K-Map) up to 4 variables, don't care conditions. Quine-McCluskey tabular minimization."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Combinational Logic Circuits)","topics":"Arithmetic circuits: Half adder, full adder, half subtractor, full subtractor, 4-bit parallel binary adder/subtractor, look-ahead carry adder. Data processing circuits: Multiplexers (2:1, 4:1, 8:1, 16:1), Demultiplexers/Decoders (1:4, 1:8, 3:8 decoder), Encoders, Priority encoders, BCD to 7-segment decoders/drivers, Magnitude comparators."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Sequential Logic Circuits)","topics":"Flip-Flops: Comparison of combinational and sequential circuits, latches vs flip-flops. RS latch, clocked RS flip-flop, D flip-flop, JK flip-flop, Master-Slave JK flip-flop, T flip-flop. Triggering of flip-flops (edge and level). Excitation tables, flip-flop conversions."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Registers & Counters)","topics":"Registers: Shift registers, modes of operation - SISO, SIPO, PISO, PIPO, universal shift register, bidirectional shift registers. Counters: Asynchronous (ripple) counters, mod-N ripple counters, synchronous counters, up/down counters, Ring counter, Johnson counter. Semiconductor memories: ROM, PROM, EPROM, EEPROM, RAM."}],"textBooks":["R.P. Jain, \"Modern Digital Electronics\", Tata McGraw-Hill.","M. Morris Mano, \"Digital Logic and Computer Design\", Prentice Hall of India."],"referenceBooks":["I.J. Nagrath, \"Electronics Analog and Digital\", Prentice Hall of India Ltd.","Malvino & Leach, \"Digital Principles and Applications\", McGraw-Hill."]}

subject.name: Operating Systems
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To provide an understanding of OS design principles, process management, scheduling algorithms, memory virtualization, deadlocks, and storage systems.","outcomes":["Students will analyze operating system structures, evaluate CPU scheduling algorithms, solve concurrency problems using semaphores, manage deadlocks, and analyze virtual memory paging."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Operating System Overview)","topics":"Introduction to operating systems, evolution of OS: Batch processing, multiprogramming, multitasking, time-sharing, real-time operating systems, distributed systems. Operating system services, system calls, system programs, operating system structure: Monolithic, layered, microkernel, and modular architectures."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Process Management & CPU Scheduling)","topics":"Process concept, process states, Process Control Block (PCB), process scheduling queues, context switching, inter-process communication (IPC). Threads: User-level and kernel-level threads. CPU scheduling: Scheduling criteria, algorithms - First-Come First-Served (FCFS), Shortest Job First (SJF), Priority scheduling, Round Robin (RR), Multilevel Queue scheduling."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Process Synchronization & Deadlocks)","topics":"Inter-process synchronization: Critical section problem, Peterson's solution, hardware synchronization, semaphores, classic synchronization problems (Producer-Consumer, Dining Philosophers, Readers-Writers). Deadlocks: Characterization, resource allocation graphs, deadlock prevention, deadlock avoidance (Banker's algorithm), deadlock detection and recovery."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Memory Management)","topics":"Logical vs physical address space, swapping, contiguous memory allocation (First-fit, Best-fit, Worst-fit), fragmentation (internal and external), paging, page table structure, segmentation. Virtual memory: Demand paging, page fault handling, page replacement algorithms (FIFO, Optimal, LRU), thrashing."},{"title":"Unit 5 (File Systems & Secondary Storage)","topics":"File concept, file access methods (sequential, direct), directory structures (single-level, two-level, tree-structured), file allocation methods (contiguous, linked, indexed), free-space management. Secondary storage: Disk structure, disk scheduling algorithms (FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK), RAID levels."}],"textBooks":["Abraham Silberschatz, Peter B. Galvin & Greg Gagne, \"Operating System Concepts\", John Wiley & Sons.","William Stallings, \"Operating Systems: Internals and Design Principles\", Pearson."],"referenceBooks":["Harvey M. Deitel, \"An Introduction to Operating Systems\", Addison Wesley.","Milan Milenkovic, \"Operating Systems: Concepts and Design\", McGraw-Hill."]}

subject.name: Programming in 'C'
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To develop procedural programming competence, structured algorithm design, pointer arithmetic, memory management, and file handling in C.","outcomes":["Students will write robust C programs utilizing arrays, user-defined functions, recursion, dynamic memory allocation, complex structures, and persistent file input/output."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Introduction to C Programming)","topics":"History and features of C, structure of a C program, compilation and execution. Character set, tokens, identifiers, keywords, data types, qualifiers, variables, constants. Operators: Arithmetic, relational, logical, assignment, increment/decrement, conditional, bitwise, sizeof. Operator precedence and associativity, type conversion and casting."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Control Flow & Loops)","topics":"Decision making: if statement, if-else statement, nested if-else, else-if ladder, switch-case statement. Iterative statements: while loop, do-while loop, for loop, nested loops. Jump statements: break, continue, goto, exit."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Arrays, Strings & Functions)","topics":"Arrays: Declaration, initialization, 1D and 2D arrays, matrix operations (addition, multiplication, transpose). Strings: Character arrays, string literals, string input/output (gets, puts, scanf, printf), string manipulation functions (strlen, strcpy, strcat, strcmp, strrev). Functions: Prototyping, definition, function calls, pass by value, pass by reference, recursion."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Pointers & Dynamic Memory Allocation)","topics":"Pointers: Concept, pointer variables, address-of (&) and dereferencing (*) operators, pointer arithmetic, pointer to pointer, pointers and arrays, array of pointers, pointers as function arguments, returning pointers. Dynamic memory allocation: malloc, calloc, realloc, free, memory leak handling."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Structures, Unions & File Handling)","topics":"Structures: Declaration, initialization, accessing structure members, array of structures, nested structures, structures and functions, structure pointers. Unions: Definition and comparison with structures, bit fields, typedef. File management: File streams, file opening modes (r, w, a, r+, w+, a+), file I/O functions (fgetc, fputc, fgets, fputs, fscanf, fprintf, fread, fwrite), file position pointers (fseek, ftell, rewind)."}],"textBooks":["E. Balagurusamy, \"Programming in ANSI C\", Tata McGraw-Hill.","Yashavant Kanetkar, \"Let Us C\", BPB Publications."],"referenceBooks":["Brian W. Kernighan & Dennis M. Ritchie, \"The C Programming Language\", Prentice Hall.","Byron Gottfried, \"Programming with C\", Schaum's Outlines, McGraw-Hill."]}

subject.name: Discrete Structures
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To introduce mathematical foundations of computer science including set theory, logic, algebraic structures, combinatorics, and graph algorithms.","outcomes":["Students will construct formal mathematical proofs, manipulate propositional statements, analyze partially ordered sets, solve recurrence relations, and apply graph theory models."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Sets, Relations & Functions)","topics":"Sets and operations: Union, intersection, complement, Cartesian product, power sets. Relations: Reflexive, symmetric, transitive, anti-symmetric relations, equivalence relations, equivalence classes. Partial order relations, Posets, Hasse diagrams, maximal, minimal, greatest and least elements, Lattices. Functions: Injective, surjective, bijective, composition, inverse functions."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Propositional & Predicate Logic)","topics":"Propositions, logical connectives (negation, conjunction, disjunction, implication, biconditional), truth tables, tautologies, contradictions, logical equivalences. Rules of inference, valid arguments. Predicate logic: Predicates, quantifiers (universal and existential), negation of quantified statements, methods of proof: Direct proof, indirect proof, proof by contradiction, mathematical induction."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Algebraic Structures)","topics":"Binary operations and their properties. Algebraic systems: Semigroups, monoids, groups, abelian groups, subgroups, cyclic groups, cosets, Lagrange's theorem, homomorphism and isomorphism of groups. Introduction to rings, integral domains, and fields."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Combinatorics & Recurrence Relations)","topics":"Counting techniques: Fundamental principles of counting, permutations and combinations, Pigeonhole principle, Inclusion-Exclusion principle. Recurrence relations: Formulating recurrence relations, solving linear recurrence relations with constant coefficients (homogeneous and non-homogeneous), generating functions."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Graph Theory & Trees)","topics":"Graphs: Basic definitions, vertices, edges, degree of a vertex, handshaking theorem, simple graphs, multigraphs, directed and undirected graphs. Graph representations: Adjacency matrix, incidence matrix. Paths, cycles, Eulerian and Hamiltonian paths and circuits, planar graphs, Kuratowski's theorem, graph coloring, chromatic number. Trees: Definition, properties, binary trees, spanning trees, minimum spanning tree (Prim's and Kruskal's algorithms)."}],"textBooks":["Kenneth H. Rosen, \"Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications\", Tata McGraw-Hill.","B. Kolman, R.C. Busby & S.C. Ross, \"Discrete Mathematical Structures\", Pearson."],"referenceBooks":["C.L. Liu, \"Elements of Discrete Mathematics\", Tata McGraw-Hill.","J.P. Tremblay & R. Manohar, \"Discrete Mathematical Structures with Applications to Computer Science\", McGraw-Hill."]}

subject.name: IT Infrastructure
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To provide knowledge of enterprise IT infrastructure components, data center architecture, enterprise storage solutions, virtualization, and network security policies.","outcomes":["Students will be able to describe IT infrastructure layers, configure enterprise storage (DAS, NAS, SAN, RAID), evaluate hypervisors, and formulate security incident response plans."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Introduction to IT Infrastructure)","topics":"Definitions, components of IT infrastructure, evolution from mainframe to cloud, client-server computing. Data center architecture: Tiers, power, cooling, cabling, rack management, server types (rack, tower, blade servers). ITIL framework overview and service lifecycle."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Storage Management Technologies)","topics":"Storage architectures: Direct-Attached Storage (DAS), Network-Attached Storage (NAS), Storage Area Network (SAN). Fiber Channel and iSCSI protocols. RAID levels (RAID 0, 1, 5, 6, 10). Backup and recovery strategies, snapshot management, disaster recovery planning and Business Continuity (BCP)."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Networking & Server Administration)","topics":"Network infrastructure: Managed switches, routers, firewalls, VLANs, structured cabling, patch panels. Server roles: Domain Controller, Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, print and file servers. Operating system deployment and configuration management."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Virtualization Technologies)","topics":"Virtualization concepts: Hypervisors (Type-1 bare metal, Type-2 hosted). VMware ESXi, Microsoft Hyper-V, KVM, VirtualBox. Server consolidation, virtual networking, virtual storage, live migration, high availability clusters. Containerization basics: Docker vs virtual machines."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Information Security & Cyber Ethics)","topics":"Information security principles: CIA triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability). Cyber threats, malware, ransomware, social engineering, denial of service (DoS/DDoS). Security measures: Antivirus, intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDS/IPS), patch management, access control lists, cyber ethics and IT compliance."}],"textBooks":["Sjaak Laan, \"IT Infrastructure Architecture: Infrastructure Building Blocks and Concepts\", Lulu.com.","Manoj Kumar Chouhan, \"IT Infrastructure and Its Management\", Dreamtech Press."],"referenceBooks":["Kathy Schwalbe, \"Information Technology Project Management\", Cengage Learning.","Mark Burgess, \"Principles of Network and System Administration\", John Wiley & Sons."]}

subject.name: Digital Electronics Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To construct, verify, and debug digital logic circuits on breadboards and digital trainers.","outcomes":["Students will build truth tables for logic gates, verify universal gate implementations, assemble combinational circuits, and test flip-flops and counters."],"labExperiments":["Verification of truth tables of basic logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR) using TTL ICs.","Implementation of basic logic gates using universal gates (NAND and NOR gates).","Breadboard design and verification of Half Adder and Full Adder circuits using basic gates.","Design and verification of Half Subtractor and Full Subtractor circuits.","Implementation of 4-bit parallel binary adder and subtractor using IC 7483.","Study and verification of Multiplexer (IC 74151) and Demultiplexer/Decoder (IC 74138).","Breadboard implementation and verification of RS, D, JK, and T Flip-Flops.","Design and verification of 4-bit Asynchronous (Ripple) Counter and Synchronous Counter using JK Flip-Flops."]}

subject.name: Operating Systems Lab (UNIX/LINUX)
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To develop command-line proficiency in UNIX/Linux environments, write shell scripts, and implement OS scheduling algorithms.","outcomes":["Students will execute file/process management commands, write shell programs with conditional and loop constructs, and simulate CPU scheduling algorithms."],"labExperiments":["Familiarization with Linux command line interface: Directory operations (pwd, cd, mkdir, rmdir, ls -la).","File handling commands: cat, cp, mv, rm, touch, head, tail, grep, find, wc, chmod, chown.","Process monitoring and management commands: ps, top, kill, nice, pstree, background (&), foreground (fg).","Shell programming - Part I: Variables, arithmetic operators, user input, conditional execution (if-else, case).","Shell programming - Part II: Loops (for, while, until), string comparisons, writing administrative backup scripts.","Implementation of CPU Scheduling algorithm in C: First-Come First-Served (FCFS).","Implementation of CPU Scheduling algorithm in C: Shortest Job First (SJF) and Round Robin (RR).","Implementation of Page Replacement algorithms in C: First-In First-Out (FIFO) and Least Recently Used (LRU)."]}

subject.name: Programming in 'C' Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To implement structured C programs solving numerical, mathematical, and real-world computational problems.","outcomes":["Students will write, compile, test, and debug programs incorporating multidimensional arrays, string libraries, pointers, recursion, and file manipulation."],"labExperiments":["Programs on decision making and branching: Quadratic equation roots, leap year verification, grade calculation.","Programs on loops: Prime number generation, Fibonacci series, Armstrong numbers, Pascal's triangle.","Programs on 1D arrays: Linear search, binary search, finding minimum/maximum elements, bubble sort.","Programs on 2D arrays: Matrix addition, matrix subtraction, matrix multiplication, and transpose calculation.","Programs on strings: String length, copy, concatenate, reverse, and palindrome check without using string library functions.","Programs on functions and recursion: Factorial, GCD using Euclidean algorithm, Tower of Hanoi problem.","Programs on pointers: Swapping two numbers using pointers, array element traversal using pointer arithmetic.","Programs on structures and files: Student record management system storing and reading data from text files."]}

subject.name: IT Infrastructure Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To acquire hands-on mastery of computer hardware maintenance, local area network cabling, operating system installation, and hypervisor management.","outcomes":["Students will assemble PC systems, crimp Ethernet cables, configure TCP/IP networks, set up virtual machines, and administer backup operations."],"labExperiments":["Disassembly and re-assembly of desktop computer system, identifying processor socket, RAM slots, chipsets, and peripheral interfaces.","BIOS/UEFI setup: Boot sequence configuration, system time, CPU overclocking settings, and security passwords.","Operating System installation: Partitioning hard drives, clean installation of Windows and Ubuntu Linux.","Network cabling: Preparing straight-through and crossover UTP cables using RJ-45 connectors, crimping tool, and cable tester.","Local Area Network (LAN) setup: IP address allocation (static vs dynamic), subnet masking, ping test, and file/printer sharing.","Hypervisor installation and virtual machine deployment using VMware Workstation / VirtualBox.","Data backup and restoration: Creating system restore points, disk cloning using cloning software, and scheduled automated backups."]}

subject.name: Discipline & General Proficiency
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To foster professional discipline, teamwork, communication skills, technical society involvement, and institutional ethics.","outcomes":["Demonstrated professional conduct, punctual academic performance, team engagement, and participation in co-curricular workshops."]}

subject.name: Data Structures with 'C'
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To understand abstract data types (ADTs), algorithm complexity, linear data structures (arrays, stacks, queues, linked lists), and non-linear data structures (trees, graphs).","outcomes":["Students will analyze time/space complexity, implement stack and queue applications, manipulate linked lists, execute tree traversals, and apply sorting/searching algorithms."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Introduction & Arrays)","topics":"Concept of data structures, classification: Primitive and non-primitive, linear and non-linear data structures. Abstract Data Types (ADT). Algorithm analysis: Time complexity, space complexity, Big-O, Omega, Theta notations. Arrays: Single and multidimensional arrays, address calculation in row-major and column-major order, sparse matrices."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Stacks & Queues)","topics":"Stacks: Definition, array implementation of stack, operations (push, pop, peek), overflow and underflow conditions. Applications of stack: Infix to postfix conversion, evaluation of postfix expressions, recursion simulation. Queues: Definition, array implementation, operations (enqueue, dequeue), circular queue, priority queue, double-ended queue (deque)."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Linked Lists)","topics":"Linked lists: Dynamic memory vs static allocation, Singly linked list: Traversal, searching, insertion (at beginning, at end, after given node), deletion (from beginning, from end, specific node). Circular linked list, Doubly linked list. Linked implementation of stacks and queues. Polynomial representation and addition using linked lists."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Trees & Graphs)","topics":"Trees: Basic terminology (root, leaf, height, depth, degree), binary trees, complete binary tree, strictly binary tree. Tree traversals: Pre-order, in-order, post-order (recursive and non-recursive). Binary Search Tree (BST): Searching, insertion, deletion. Introduction to AVL trees and B-Trees. Graphs: Terminology, adjacency matrix and adjacency list representations, graph traversals - Breadth-First Search (BFS) and Depth-First Search (DFS)."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Searching & Sorting Algorithms)","topics":"Searching algorithms: Linear search, binary search (iterative and recursive), complexity analysis. Sorting algorithms: Bubble sort, selection sort, insertion sort, quick sort (divide and conquer), merge sort, heap sort. Comparison of sorting algorithms in best, average, and worst-case performance."}],"textBooks":["Ellis Horowitz, Sartaj Sahni & Susan Anderson-Freed, \"Fundamentals of Data Structures in C\", Silicon Press / Universities Press.","Aaron M. Tenenbaum, Yedidyah Langsam & Moshe J. Augenstein, \"Data Structures Using C and C++\", Prentice Hall of India."],"referenceBooks":["Robert L. Kruse, Bruce P. Leung & Clovis L. Tondo, \"Data Structures and Program Design in C\", Pearson.","Seymour Lipschutz, \"Data Structures with C\", Schaum's Outline Series, McGraw-Hill."]}

subject.name: OOP's with C++
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To learn object-oriented programming paradigms, class architecture, encapsulation, inheritance, operator overloading, polymorphism, templates, and exception handling in C++.","outcomes":["Students will build object-oriented software utilizing classes, manage object lifecycle with constructors, implement inheritance hierarchies, resolve dynamic binding, and write template code."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Introduction to Object-Oriented Programming & C++)","topics":"Comparison of procedural programming and object-oriented programming (OOP). Key concepts: Objects, classes, data abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, dynamic binding, message passing. C++ tokens, variables, constants, reference variables, scope resolution operator (::), cin, cout, inline functions, default arguments, function overloading."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Classes & Objects)","topics":"Class declaration, defining member functions inside and outside the class, private, public, protected access specifiers. Memory allocation for objects, array of objects, arrays as class member data, static data members and static member functions. Friend functions and friend classes, returning objects."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Constructors, Destructors & Operator Overloading)","topics":"Constructors: Purpose, default constructor, parameterized constructor, copy constructor, dynamic constructor, constructor overloading. Destructors. Operator overloading: Overloading unary operators, overloading binary operators (using member function and friend function), overloading << and >> stream operators, data type conversions (basic to class, class to basic, class to class)."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Inheritance, Pointers & Polymorphism)","topics":"Inheritance: Base and derived classes, visibility modes (public, private, protected), types of inheritance: Single, multilevel, multiple, hierarchical, hybrid inheritance. Ambiguity resolution, virtual base classes, constructors in derived classes. Pointers to objects, this pointer, pointers to derived classes, virtual functions, pure virtual functions, abstract classes."},{"title":"Unit 5 (File Streams, Templates & Exception Handling)","topics":"C++ I/O streams, stream classes hierarchy, unformatted and formatted I/O, file stream classes (ifstream, ofstream, fstream), opening and closing files, reading and writing objects. Templates: Function templates, class templates, templates with multiple arguments. Exception handling: try, catch, throw blocks, rethrowing exceptions."}],"textBooks":["E. Balagurusamy, \"Object Oriented Programming with C++\", Tata McGraw-Hill.","Robert Lafore, \"Object-Oriented Programming in C++\", Pearson."],"referenceBooks":["Bjarne Stroustrup, \"The C++ Programming Language\", Addison-Wesley.","Herbert Schildt, \"C++: The Complete Reference\", McGraw-Hill."]}

subject.name: Computer Organization
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To understand register transfer logic, basic computer instruction cycles, CPU microarchitecture, arithmetic algorithms, memory hierarchies, and I/O bus systems.","outcomes":["Students will analyze computer micro-operations, design control units, explain RISC/CISC paradigms, execute Booth's multiplication, analyze cache mapping, and evaluate DMA transfers."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Register Transfer & Micro-operations)","topics":"Register transfer language (RTL), bus and memory transfers, three-state bus buffers. Arithmetic micro-operations: Binary adder, binary adder-subtractor, arithmetic circuit. Logic micro-operations, shift micro-operations (logical, circular, arithmetic shifts). Arithmetic Logic Shift Unit (ALSU)."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Basic Computer Organization & Instruction Cycle)","topics":"Instruction codes, computer registers (AR, PC, DR, AC, IR, TR, INPR, OUTR), common bus system. Computer instructions: Memory-reference, register-reference, and input-output instructions. Timing and control signals, instruction cycle: Fetch, decode, execute, memory-reference execution, interrupt cycle."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Central Processing Unit (CPU))","topics":"General register organization, stack organization (register stack, memory stack), reverse Polish notation. Instruction formats: Three-address, two-address, one-address, zero-address instructions. Addressing modes: Direct, indirect, register, register indirect, immediate, displacement, relative, indexed addressing. RISC vs CISC architecture characteristics."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Computer Arithmetic)","topics":"Addition and subtraction with signed-magnitude data, 2's complement representation. Multiplication algorithms: Hardware multiplier, Booth's multiplication algorithm for signed 2's complement integers. Division algorithms: Restoring and non-restoring division algorithms. Floating-point arithmetic operations."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Memory Hierarchy & Input-Output Organization)","topics":"Memory hierarchy, main memory (RAM, ROM chips, memory address map), auxiliary memory (magnetic disks, SSDs), associative memory. Cache memory: Cache hit/miss, mapping functions (direct, associative, set-associative mapping), cache write policies. Virtual memory: Address translation, paging. Input-Output interface, asynchronous data transfer (strobe, handshaking), programmed I/O, interrupt-driven I/O, Direct Memory Access (DMA)."}],"textBooks":["M. Morris Mano, \"Computer System Architecture\", Prentice Hall of India.","Carl Hamacher, Zvonko Vranesic & Safwat Zaky, \"Computer Organization\", McGraw-Hill."],"referenceBooks":["William Stallings, \"Computer Organization and Architecture\", Pearson.","John P. Hayes, \"Computer Architecture and Organization\", McGraw-Hill."]}

subject.name: E-Commerce
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To study electronic commerce models, web technologies, digital payment infrastructures, cyber security threats, encryption, and legal frameworks.","outcomes":["Students will differentiate e-business models, describe online payment mechanisms, analyze security vulnerabilities, explain digital signatures, and navigate the IT Act 2000."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Introduction to E-Commerce & Business Models)","topics":"Definition, origin, and development of E-Commerce. Comparison of traditional commerce and electronic commerce, advantages and disadvantages of E-Commerce. Business models: Business-to-Consumer (B2C), Business-to-Business (B2B), Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C), Consumer-to-Business (C2B), Government-to-Citizen (G2C). Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) and supply chain integration."},{"title":"Unit 2 (E-Commerce Infrastructure & Technologies)","topics":"Internet, Intranet, and Extranet. World Wide Web (WWW) architecture, domain name system (DNS), web servers, application servers, database servers. Mobile Commerce (M-Commerce): Features, mobile payment applications, wireless technologies (4G/5G, Wi-Fi)."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Electronic Payment Systems)","topics":"Overview of electronic payment systems, electronic cash, credit cards, debit cards, smart cards, electronic wallets (e-wallets), net banking, Unified Payments Interface (UPI). Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT), Automated Clearing House (ACH). Payment gateways, risks involved in online payments, fraud detection."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Security in E-Commerce)","topics":"Security threats in e-commerce: Malicious code, phishing, credit card fraud, sniffing, spoofing, denial of service attacks. Security tools: Encryption (symmetric and asymmetric cryptography, DES, RSA), Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), digital signatures, digital certificates, Secure Socket Layer (SSL/TLS), firewalls."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Online Marketing & Legal Environment)","topics":"Internet marketing concepts: Search Engine Optimization (SEO), Search Engine Marketing (SEM), email marketing, social media marketing, affiliate marketing. Legal and regulatory issues: Information Technology Act 2000 (IT Act), cyber crimes, intellectual property rights (patents, copyrights, trademarks), privacy issues and consumer protection."}],"textBooks":["Kenneth C. Laudon & Carol Guercio Traver, \"E-Commerce: Business, Technology, Society\", Pearson Education.","Gary P. Schneider, \"Electronic Commerce\", Cengage Learning."],"referenceBooks":["K.K. Bajaj & Debjani Nag, \"E-Commerce: The Cutting Edge of Business\", Tata McGraw-Hill.","P.T. Joseph, \"E-Commerce: An Indian Perspective\", Prentice Hall of India."]}

subject.name: Industrial Management
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To teach management principles, organizational behavior, industrial relations, operations management, quality assurance, and factory regulations.","outcomes":["Students will apply management functions, evaluate organizational structures, analyze production scheduling, calculate Economic Order Quantity, and understand workplace safety laws."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Principles of Management)","topics":"Definition, nature, scope, and significance of management. Evolution of management thought: Taylor's Scientific Management, Fayol's 14 Principles of Administrative Management, Hawthorne studies. Functions of management: Planning, organizing, staffing, directing, controlling. Decision making process."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Forms of Business Organization & Structures)","topics":"Ownership forms: Sole proprietorship, partnership, joint-stock company (private and public limited), cooperative societies, public sector enterprises. Organizational structure: Line organization, functional organization, line and staff organization, matrix organization. Authority, responsibility, delegation, and decentralization."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Human Resource Management & Industrial Relations)","topics":"Recruitment, selection process, induction, training and development methods. Performance appraisal, job evaluation, merit rating. Wage and incentive schemes: Time rate, piece rate, Taylor's differential piece rate, Halsey and Rowan incentive plans. Industrial relations: Causes of industrial disputes, trade unions, collective bargaining, settlement mechanisms."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Production Planning & Inventory Control)","topics":"Plant location factors, plant layout types (product, process, fixed position layout). Production planning and control (PPC): Routing, scheduling, dispatching, expediting. Inventory management: Purpose of inventory, ABC analysis, Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) formula, safety stock, lead time."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Quality Management & Industrial Legislation)","topics":"Total Quality Management (TQM), Quality Circles, ISO 9000 quality standards, statistical quality control (control charts for variables and attributes). Industrial safety: Causes of industrial accidents, safety precautions, Factories Act 1948 provisions regarding health, safety, and welfare of workers, Workmen's Compensation Act."}],"textBooks":["L.M. Prasad, \"Principles and Practice of Management\", Sultan Chand & Sons.","O.P. Khanna, \"Industrial Engineering and Management\", Dhanpat Rai Publications."],"referenceBooks":["T.N. Chhabra, \"Principles and Practice of Management\", Dhanpat Rai & Sons.","Harold Koontz & Heinz Weihrich, \"Essentials of Management\", Tata McGraw-Hill."]}

subject.name: Data Structures Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To develop practical algorithmic programs implementing core data structures and sorting algorithms in C.","outcomes":["Students will program array algorithms, stacks, queues, linked lists, trees, and benchmark various sorting techniques."],"labExperiments":["Array implementation of Stack ADT: Push, Pop, Peek, and display operations.","Application of Stack: Conversion of Infix arithmetic expression to Postfix expression.","Application of Stack: Evaluation of Postfix expression using stack.","Array implementation of Linear Queue ADT: Enqueue, Dequeue, and display operations.","Implementation of Circular Queue with proper overflow and underflow condition checks.","Implementation of Singly Linked List: Insertion and deletion at beginning, middle, and end.","Implementation of Doubly Linked List with bidirectional traversal.","Implementation of Binary Search Tree (BST): Insertion, node deletion, and in-order traversal.","Implementation and comparison of Quick Sort and Merge Sort algorithms."]}

subject.name: OOPs Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To implement object-oriented systems in C++ showcasing classes, constructors, operator overloading, and inheritance.","outcomes":["Students will write C++ programs verifying encapsulation, operator overloading, multiple inheritance, runtime polymorphism, and file stream I/O."],"labExperiments":["Programs demonstrating classes, object instantiation, public/private access, and member functions.","Programs on Constructor overloading: Default, parameterized, and copy constructors.","Programs using friend functions and static member variables across multiple classes.","Operator overloading: Overloading binary '+' operator to add two Complex number objects.","Operator overloading: Overloading unary '++' and '--' operators for Counter class.","Implementation of Single and Multilevel Inheritance models with base constructor invocation.","Implementation of Multiple Inheritance demonstrating virtual base classes to prevent diamond problem.","Runtime polymorphism demonstration using base class pointers and Virtual Functions.","File handling program writing and reading student class objects to binary files."]}

subject.name: Computer Organization Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To verify computer architecture concepts through microprocessor assembly programming and hardware logic simulation.","outcomes":["Students will write assembly code for arithmetic/logical manipulation, test memory block transfers, and simulate ALU operations."],"labExperiments":["Introduction to 8085/8086 microprocessor architecture and instruction set simulator.","Assembly program to perform 8-bit and 16-bit binary addition and subtraction.","Assembly program to perform multiplication of two 8-bit unsigned integers.","Assembly program to find the largest and smallest number in an array of N bytes.","Assembly program to sort an array of numbers in ascending and descending order.","Assembly program to perform block data transfer from source memory to destination memory.","Assembly program to convert BCD numbers to Binary and vice-versa.","Simulation of Booth's Multiplication Algorithm using high-level language program."]}

subject.name: E-Commerce Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To design responsive e-commerce web interfaces, shopping cart workflows, and analyze digital payment security.","outcomes":["Students will build online catalog web pages, validate customer checkout forms with JavaScript, and analyze secure payment flowcharts."],"labExperiments":["Designing an online store product catalog with responsive image galleries, pricing, and buy buttons.","Designing customer registration and login interfaces with client-side JavaScript validation.","Implementation of an interactive shopping cart table calculating subtotal, tax, discounts, and grand total.","Developing checkout order summary forms with shipping address input and credit card input masking.","Simulation and sequence analysis of Secure Electronic Transaction (SET) and SSL handshake flow.","Case study presentation analyzing security and architecture of major Indian e-commerce portals."]}

subject.name: Discipline & General Proficiency
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To evaluate student professional conduct, punctuality, teamwork, industrial visit attendance, and extracurricular involvement.","outcomes":["Demonstrated professional demeanor, group discussion capability, institutional ethics, and semester-long discipline."]}

subject.name: DBMS (Database Management Systems)
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To provide a solid understanding of database management concepts, entity-relationship modeling, relational algebra, SQL, normalization, and transaction processing.","outcomes":["Students will be able to design relational schemas, write complex SQL queries, normalize databases up to BCNF, and manage transaction ACID properties."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Basic Concepts of DBMS & Architecture)","topics":"Introduction to Database Management System (DBMS). Database approach vs traditional file-oriented approach, advantages of DBMS. DBMS architecture: 3-tier ANSI/SPARC schema architecture, physical, conceptual, and external levels. Data independence (logical and physical). Database users and administrators (DBA roles)."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Data Models & Entity-Relationship (ER) Modeling)","topics":"Data models: Hierarchical, network, relational, object-oriented models. Entity-Relationship model: Entities, entity sets, attributes (simple, composite, multivalued, derived), relationship types and sets.
