Structural constraints: Cardinality ratios, participation constraints. Keys: Super key, candidate key, primary key, foreign key, unique key. E-R diagrams and mapping ER models to relational schemas."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Relational Model & Structured Query Language (SQL))","topics":"Relational model concepts: Domains, tuples, relations, relational integrity constraints (entity integrity, referential integrity). Relational algebra operations: Select, project, union, set difference, Cartesian product, rename, joins (natural join, inner join, outer joins). SQL: Data Definition Language (DDL - CREATE, ALTER, DROP), Data Manipulation Language (DML - INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT), Data Control Language (DCL - GRANT, REVOKE). Aggregate functions, group by, having, nested subqueries, views."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Relational Database Design & Normalization)","topics":"Pitfalls in relational database design (redundancy, update anomalies, insertion and deletion anomalies). Functional dependencies: Definition, Armstrong's axioms, closure of functional dependencies, closure of attribute sets, canonical cover. Normalization: First Normal Form (1NF), Second Normal Form (2NF), Third Normal Form (3NF), Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF). Lossless-join decomposition and dependency preservation."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Transaction Processing & Concurrency Control)","topics":"Transaction concepts: Transaction states, ACID properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability). Concurrent executions, serializability (conflict and view serializability). Concurrency control techniques: Lock-based protocols (shared and exclusive locks), Two-Phase Locking (2PL), deadlock prevention and detection. Database recovery concepts: Log-based recovery, checkpoints."}],"textBooks":["Abraham Silberschatz, Henry F. Korth & S. Sudarshan, \"Database System Concepts\", McGraw-Hill.","Ramez Elmasri & Shamkant B. Navathe, \"Fundamentals of Database Systems\", Pearson Education."],"referenceBooks":["Raghu Ramakrishnan & Johannes Gehrke, \"Database Management Systems\", McGraw-Hill.","C.J. Date, \"An Introduction to Database Systems\", Addison-Wesley."]}

subject.name: JAVA
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To master Java core syntax, OOP implementations, interface architectures, multithreaded programming, exception propagation, and graphical user interfaces.","outcomes":["Students will build robust Java applications utilizing class hierarchies, packages, multithreaded concurrency, exception handling, and AWT/Swing graphical components."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Java Evolution & Language Fundamentals)","topics":"Genesis of Java, Java characteristics: Platform independent, object-oriented, robust, secure, multithreaded. Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Java Development Kit (JDK), Java Runtime Environment (JRE), bytecode. Data types, variables, type conversion, casting, operators, control flow statements (branching, looping, switch)."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Classes, Objects & Methods)","topics":"Class fundamentals: Declaring classes, creating objects, assigning object reference variables. Methods, constructors, this keyword, garbage collection, finalize() method. Method overloading, constructor overloading, objects as parameters, returning objects. Static members and static blocks, nested and inner classes."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Inheritance, Packages & Interfaces)","topics":"Inheritance basics: Member access, super keyword, creating multilevel hierarchy, method overriding, dynamic method dispatch, abstract classes, using final with variables, methods, and classes. Packages: Defining packages, CLASSPATH, access protection, importing packages. Interfaces: Defining, implementing, nested interfaces, variables in interfaces."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Exception Handling & Multithreaded Programming)","topics":"Exception handling fundamentals: Types of exceptions (checked and unchecked), try, catch, throw, throws, finally blocks, multiple catch clauses, nested try statements, creating custom exception subclasses. Multithreading: Java thread model, thread priorities, creating threads by extending Thread class and implementing Runnable interface, thread lifecycle, synchronization (synchronized methods and blocks), inter-thread communication (wait, notify, notifyAll)."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Java I/O & GUI Programming (AWT))","topics":"I/O basics: Byte streams (FileInputStream, FileOutputStream) and character streams (FileReader, FileWriter), standard input/output with BufferedReader and Scanner. Abstract Window Toolkit (AWT): AWT hierarchy, Frame, Button, Label, TextField, Checkbox, Choice, List, layout managers (FlowLayout, BorderLayout, GridLayout). Event handling: Delegation event model, event classes, listener interfaces."}],"textBooks":["Herbert Schildt, \"Java: The Complete Reference\", McGraw-Hill Education.","E. Balagurusamy, \"Programming with Java: A Primer\", Tata McGraw-Hill."],"referenceBooks":["Cay S. Horstmann & Gary Cornell, \"Core Java Volume I - Fundamentals\", Prentice Hall.","Kathy Sierra & Bert Bates, \"Head First Java\", O'Reilly Media."]}

subject.name: Management Information System
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To understand the strategic role of information systems, enterprise resource planning, decision support models, and cybersecurity governance in organizations.","outcomes":["Students will analyze enterprise business workflows, evaluate ERP/CRM/SCM systems, understand Decision Support architectures, and implement information security controls."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Introduction to Management Information Systems)","topics":"Meaning and role of MIS, definition, system approach, concepts of data and information, characteristics of quality information. Information needs of different management levels (strategic, tactical, operational). Subsystems of MIS, organizational structure and information systems."},{"title":"Unit 2 (System Development & Business Applications)","topics":"Systems Development Life Cycle (SDLC) for MIS: Requirements analysis, system design, implementation, testing, and maintenance. Structured methodologies, data flow diagrams (DFD). Business applications of IT: Financial information systems, marketing information systems, manufacturing information systems, human resource information systems."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Enterprise Systems & E-Business Applications)","topics":"Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP): Meaning, benefits, modules, ERP implementation challenges. Supply Chain Management (SCM) systems: Objectives and components. Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems: Features and business value. Knowledge Management Systems (KMS)."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Decision Support Systems & Business Intelligence)","topics":"Decision making concepts: Herbert Simon's decision-making model (Intelligence, Design, Choice, Implementation). Decision Support Systems (DSS): Characteristics, components, comparison of MIS and DSS. Executive Support Systems (ESS/EIS), Group Decision Support Systems (GDSS). Data warehousing and data mining overview in business intelligence."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Information Security & Ethical Dimensions)","topics":"Security threats to information systems: Unauthorized access, malware, denial of service, insider threats. Security management: Access control, authentication, firewalls, intrusion detection, auditing, disaster recovery planning. Ethical and social issues: Privacy, intellectual property, software copyright, accountability."}],"textBooks":["Kenneth C. Laudon & Jane P. Laudon, \"Management Information Systems: Managing the Digital Firm\", Pearson.","James A. O'Brien & George M. Marakas, \"Management Information Systems\", Tata McGraw-Hill."],"referenceBooks":["Waman S. Jawadekar, \"Management Information Systems: Text and Cases\", Tata McGraw-Hill.","Gordon B. Davis & Margrethe H. Olson, \"Management Information Systems\", McGraw-Hill."]}

subject.name: Computer Hardware and Maintenance
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To examine PC internal hardware architectures, motherboards, chipsets, power distribution, storage devices, peripheral interfacing, and diagnostic troubleshooting.","outcomes":["Students will troubleshoot motherboard and component failures, diagnose power delivery problems, replace memory/storage subsystems, and resolve operating system boot errors."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Motherboard Architecture & Processors)","topics":"Motherboard form factors: AT, ATX, microATX, ITX. Motherboard components: Processor sockets, chipset architecture (Northbridge and Southbridge / PCH), expansion slots (PCI, PCIe x1, x4, x16), memory slots. Microprocessors: Evolution from 8086 to modern multi-core CPUs, hyperthreading, clock speed, cache hierarchy (L1, L2, L3)."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Memory Systems & BIOS/UEFI)","topics":"Primary memory: RAM technologies (SRAM, DRAM, SDRAM, DDR, DDR2, DDR3, DDR4), dual-channel memory architecture, ROM types (PROM, EPROM, Flash ROM). BIOS/UEFI firmware: Functions, Power-On Self-Test (POST), beep codes, CMOS setup utility, configuring boot priority, flashing and updating BIOS."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Power Supply & Cooling Solutions)","topics":"Switched-Mode Power Supply (SMPS): Function, working principle, voltage rails (+3.3V, +5V, +12V, -12V), power connectors (24-pin ATX, 4/8-pin CPU, SATA, PCIe). Power calculation, power surge protection, UPS types. Cooling systems: Heatsinks, CPU fans, thermal paste, chassis ventilation, liquid cooling basics."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Storage Subsystems & Peripherals)","topics":"Magnetic Hard Disk Drives (HDD): Construction, platters, read/write heads, spindle motor, tracks, sectors, cylinders, SATA interfaces. Solid-State Drives (SSD): NAND flash memory, SATA SSD vs NVMe M.2 SSD. Optical storage: CD/DVD/Blu-ray. Input/Output devices: Keyboards, optical mice, touchscreens, monitor technologies (LCD, LED, OLED), display ports (VGA, DVI, HDMI, DisplayPort)."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Installation, Maintenance & Troubleshooting)","topics":"Preventive maintenance: Cleaning procedures, environmental factors (dust, temperature, humidity). System assembly and disassembly sequence. OS installation: BIOS setup, disk partitioning (MBR vs GPT), installing device drivers. Troubleshooting common hardware faults: Display failures, memory errors, blue screen of death (BSOD), hard drive failure symptoms, power issues."}],"textBooks":["Scott Mueller, \"Upgrading and Repairing PCs\", Que Publishing / Pearson.","Ron Gilster, \"PC Hardware: A Beginner's Guide\", McGraw-Hill Osborne Media."],"referenceBooks":["Craig Zacker & John Rourke, \"PC Hardware: The Complete Reference\", McGraw-Hill.","Govindarajalu, \"IBM PC and Clones: Hardware, Troubleshooting and Maintenance\", Tata McGraw-Hill."]}

subject.name: Computer Graphics
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To study display hardware, scan-conversion algorithms, 2D/3D geometric transformations, viewing and clipping pipelines, and curve generation.","outcomes":["Students will implement line/circle drawing algorithms, apply 2D/3D affine matrix transformations, execute line and polygon clipping, and understand spline representations."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Introduction & Graphics Hardware)","topics":"Overview of computer graphics and applications. Interactive vs non-interactive graphics. Video display devices: Cathode Ray Tube (CRT), raster scan displays, random scan (vector) displays, color CRT monitors (shadow mask, beam penetration), flat panel displays (LCD, LED). Video controller, frame buffer."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Scan Conversion Algorithms)","topics":"Scan conversion of primitive entities: Points and lines. Line drawing algorithms: Digital Differential Analyzer (DDA) algorithm, Bresenham's line algorithm. Circle generation algorithms: Midpoint circle algorithm, Bresenham's circle algorithm. Polygon filling algorithms: Scanline polygon fill, boundary fill, and flood fill algorithms."},{"title":"Unit 3 (2D Geometric Transformations)","topics":"Basic 2D transformations: Translation, rotation, scaling. Matrix representations and homogeneous coordinates. Composite transformations: General pivot-point rotation, fixed-point scaling, concatenated transformation matrices. Other transformations: Reflection (about x-axis, y-axis, origin, and line y=mx+c), shear (x-shear and y-shear)."},{"title":"Unit 4 (2D Viewing & Clipping)","topics":"Viewing pipeline, viewing coordinate reference frame, window-to-viewport coordinate transformation. Clipping operations: Point clipping. Line clipping algorithms: Cohen-Sutherland line clipping algorithm, Liang-Barsky line clipping algorithm. Polygon clipping: Sutherland-Hodgman polygon clipping algorithm. Text clipping."},{"title":"Unit 5 (3D Graphics & Curves)","topics":"3D display methods, 3D geometric transformations: Translation, rotation, scaling in 3D, composite 3D transformations. Projections: Parallel projections (orthographic, oblique) and Perspective projections. Visible surface detection: Back-face detection, Depth-Buffer (Z-buffer) algorithm. Introduction to curves: Spline representation, Bezier curves and B-spline curves."}],"textBooks":["Donald Hearn & M. Pauline Baker, \"Computer Graphics C Version\", Pearson Education.","Amarendra N. Sinha & Arun D. Udai, \"Computer Graphics\", Tata McGraw-Hill."],"referenceBooks":["James D. Foley, Andries van Dam, Steven K. Feiner & John F. Hughes, \"Computer Graphics: Principles and Practice\", Addison-Wesley.","Zhigang Xiang & Roy Plastock, \"Computer Graphics\", Schaum's Outline Series, McGraw-Hill."]}

subject.name: DBMS Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To provide hands-on mastery of relational database design, schema definition, SQL queries, relational operations, and PL/SQL programming.","outcomes":["Students will construct database tables with constraints, execute multi-table joins and subqueries, write PL/SQL triggers, and maintain database integrity."],"labExperiments":["Database schema definition using DDL commands (CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE) with column integrity constraints (PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK).","Data manipulation using DML commands (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) and transaction verification with COMMIT and ROLLBACK.","Data retrieval using SELECT statements with WHERE, ORDER BY, DISTINCT, and pattern matching operators (LIKE, BETWEEN, IN).","Aggregate functions (SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, COUNT) and grouping with GROUP BY and HAVING clauses.","Multi-table querying using JOIN operations (Natural Join, Inner Join, Left/Right/Full Outer Joins).","Writing nested queries, correlated subqueries, and set operations (UNION, INTERSECT, MINUS).","Creation and management of database Views, Sequences, and Indexes.","PL/SQL block programming: Control structures, Cursors (implicit and explicit), Stored Procedures, Functions, and Triggers."]}

subject.name: JAVA Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To build Java applications demonstrating object-oriented classes, inheritance, packages, multithreaded concurrency, and GUI interfaces.","outcomes":["Students will program Java classes, handle exceptions, implement multithreading, and design event-driven AWT user interfaces."],"labExperiments":["Java programs illustrating classes, objects, method overloading, and constructor overloading.","Implementation of Single, Multilevel, and Hierarchical Inheritance with 'super' keyword and method overriding.","Creating and implementing Interfaces and organizing classes into custom user-defined Packages.","Exception handling implementation using try, catch, finally blocks, and writing custom user-defined Exception classes.","Multithreaded programming: Creating threads using Thread class and Runnable interface with thread sleep and priorities.","Thread synchronization: Demonstrating synchronized methods to resolve race conditions.","Java I/O streams: Reading and writing text and binary files using FileInputStream/FileOutputStream and BufferedReader.","AWT GUI application: Creating a scientific calculator with Buttons, TextField, GridBagLayout, and ActionListener event handling."]}

subject.name: Repaired and Maintenance Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To diagnose, repair, and maintain desktop PC hardware components, power supplies, memory modules, and operating systems.","outcomes":["Students will measure SMPS voltages, troubleshoot POST error codes, partition storage drives, and perform diagnostic hardware testing."],"labExperiments":["Testing computer power supply (SMPS) output voltages on various color-coded rail wires using digital multimeter.","Motherboard inspection: Identifying capacitor leakage, testing front panel power/reset switches, and replacing CMOS battery.","Memory troubleshooting: Testing RAM modules using memory diagnostic tools and resolving memory beep error codes.","Storage maintenance: Partitioning hard drives using diskpart/GParted, sector surface scanning, and resolving bad sector warnings.","Troubleshooting common video and display adapter faults, configuring multi-monitor setups, and adjusting display resolutions.","Diagnostic software tools: Running CPU-Z, HWMonitor, and benchmarking software to monitor system temperature, voltages, and performance.","Operating System recovery: Repairing Windows Master Boot Record (MBR), creating bootable rescue media, and removing rootkit viruses."]}

subject.name: Computer Graphics Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To implement fundamental computer graphics algorithms in C/C++ graphics environment.","outcomes":["Students will program scan conversion for lines/circles, execute 2D transformations, and code line clipping routines."],"labExperiments":["Initialization of graphics mode in C/C++ using initgraph() and basic drawing functions (line, circle, rectangle).","Implementation of Digital Differential Analyzer (DDA) Line Drawing Algorithm.","Implementation of Bresenham's Line Drawing Algorithm for various slopes.","Implementation of Midpoint Circle Generation Algorithm.","Implementation of Boundary Fill and Flood Fill algorithms for polygon filling.","Implementation of 2D Geometric Transformations: Translation, Scaling, and Rotation about origin.","Implementation of 2D Rotation of a triangle about an arbitrary pivot point.","Implementation of Cohen-Sutherland Line Clipping Algorithm against a rectangular clipping window."]}

subject.name: Discipline & General Proficiency
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To assess professional ethics, student leadership, technical seminar participation, attendance regularity, and campus discipline.","outcomes":["Demonstrated professional communication, leadership in departmental initiatives, and disciplined academic participation."]}

subject.name: Web Technology
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To learn modern web standards, HTML5 markup, CSS3 styling, responsive layouts, client-side JavaScript, server scripting, and web security.","outcomes":["Students will develop responsive websites, validate client input, parse XML data structures, integrate server-side scripts, and apply web protection techniques."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Web Fundamentals & HTML5)","topics":"Internet and web overview, client-server architecture, HTTP protocol, URLs, web browsers, web servers. HTML5: Document structure, doctype, text formatting, hyperlinks, lists, tables, images, audio, video elements. HTML5 forms: Form elements, input types (text, password, email, date, number), form validation attributes."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Cascading Style Sheets - CSS3)","topics":"CSS fundamentals: Inline, internal, and external style sheets. CSS selectors: Element, class, ID, attribute, pseudo-classes, pseudo-elements. CSS Box Model: Margin, border, padding, content. Positioning: Static, relative, absolute, fixed, sticky. CSS3 styling: Colors, backgrounds, fonts, text effects, shadows, transitions, animations. Responsive design: Viewport meta tag, media queries, CSS Flexbox and Grid fundamentals."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Client-Side Scripting - JavaScript)","topics":"JavaScript introduction: Placing JavaScript in HTML, variables, data types, operators, control structures (conditional and looping). Functions: Declaration, parameters, return values, arrow functions. Document Object Model (DOM): Window and document objects, DOM element selection, modifying HTML content, styles, and attributes. Event handling: Event listeners, mouse events, keyboard events, form validation using JavaScript."},{"title":"Unit 4 (XML & Server-Side Concepts)","topics":"XML: Introduction, features, XML syntax, well-formed vs valid XML documents. Document Type Definition (DTD): Elements, attributes, internal and external DTD. XML Schema (XSD). Introduction to server-side scripting: Client-side vs server-side execution, overview of PHP/Node.js, handling GET and POST requests, session and cookie management, connecting to MySQL database."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Web Security & Cyber Laws)","topics":"Web security principles: Common threats (SQL injection, Cross-Site Scripting - XSS, Cross-Site Request Forgery - CSRF), SSL/TLS certificates, HTTPS, secure password hashing. Website deployment: Domain registration, DNS records, web hosting services, FTP upload. Cyber laws: Overview of IT Act 2000, intellectual property rights on web, digital signatures."}],"textBooks":["Achyut Godbole & Atul Kahate, \"Web Technologies: TCP/IP, Web/Java Programming, and Cloud Computing\", Tata McGraw-Hill.","Jon Duckett, \"HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites\", John Wiley & Sons."],"referenceBooks":["Jon Duckett, \"JavaScript and JQuery: Interactive Front-End Web Development\", Wiley.","Uttam K. Roy, \"Web Technologies\", Oxford University Press."]}

subject.name: Software Engineering
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To study software lifecycle models, requirements engineering, system design architectures, testing methodologies, project estimation, and quality assurance.","outcomes":["Students will produce Software Requirement Specifications (SRS), construct UML architectural diagrams, design black/white box test cases, estimate project efforts, and apply SQA standards."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Introduction & Software Process Models)","topics":"Software engineering definition, software characteristics, software crisis, software engineering principles. Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) models: Classical Waterfall model, Iterative Waterfall model, Prototyping model, Evolutionary model, Spiral model, Agile methodology principles and Scrum framework."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Software Requirements Engineering)","topics":"Requirement gathering and analysis, types of requirements (functional and non-functional). Feasibility study (technical, economic, operational). Software Requirement Specification (SRS) document: Need, characteristics of quality SRS, IEEE 830 standard format for SRS. Structured analysis: Data Flow Diagrams (DFD - Level 0, 1, 2), Data Dictionary, Decision Trees and Tables."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Software Design & Modeling)","topics":"Design concepts: Abstraction, refinement, modularity, software architecture. Cohesion (types of cohesion) and Coupling (types of coupling). Object-Oriented software design: UML modeling, Use Case diagrams, Class diagrams, Sequence diagrams, State chart diagrams. User Interface (UI) design principles."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Software Coding & Testing Methodologies)","topics":"Coding standards and guidelines, code review, code walkthrough, code inspection. Software testing fundamentals: Verification vs Validation, error, fault, failure. Testing strategies: Unit testing, integration testing (top-down, bottom-up), system testing, acceptance testing, regression testing. Test case design techniques: White-box testing (basis path testing, cyclomatic complexity, control flow graphs), Black-box testing (Equivalence Class Partitioning, Boundary Value Analysis)."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Software Maintenance, Estimation & Quality Assurance)","topics":"Software maintenance: Types of maintenance (corrective, adaptive, perfective, preventive), maintenance cost factors, software reverse engineering. Software project estimation: Empirical estimation models, COCOMO model (Basic and Intermediate). Software Quality Assurance (SQA): Software quality metrics, ISO 9000 quality standards, SEI Capability Maturity Model (CMM levels)."}],"textBooks":["Roger S. Pressman & Bruce R. Maxim, \"Software Engineering: A Practitioner's Approach\", McGraw-Hill.","Rajib Mall, \"Fundamentals of Software Engineering\", Prentice Hall of India."],"referenceBooks":["Ian Sommerville, \"Software Engineering\", Pearson Education.","Pankaj Jalote, \"An Integrated Approach to Software Engineering\", Springer."]}

subject.name: Computer Networks
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To examine network topologies, OSI and TCP/IP layered architectures, data link protocols, routing algorithms, transport mechanisms, and network security protocols.","outcomes":["Students will analyze network layer architectures, calculate subnet masks, evaluate distance vector and link state routing, contrast TCP/UDP operations, and explain cryptography standards."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Introduction & Reference Models)","topics":"Network definition, goals, and applications. Network classifications: LAN, MAN, WAN, PAN, wireless networks. Network topologies: Bus, star, ring, mesh, tree, hybrid topologies. Reference models: OSI 7-layer reference model (functions of each layer), TCP/IP reference model, comparison between OSI and TCP/IP models."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Physical & Data Link Layers)","topics":"Transmission media: Guided media (twisted pair cable, coaxial cable, optical fiber cable) and unguided media (radio waves, microwaves, infrared). Switching techniques: Circuit switching, packet switching (datagram and virtual circuit), message switching. Data Link layer functions: Framing, error detection and correction (parity check, checksum, Cyclic Redundancy Check - CRC, Hamming code). Flow control protocols: Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window (Go-Back-N, Selective Repeat). MAC sublayer: ALOHA, CSMA, CSMA/CD, IEEE 802.3 Ethernet."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Network Layer & Routing)","topics":"Network layer functions, connection-oriented vs connectionless services. IP Addressing: IPv4 addressing, address classes (Class A, B, C, D, E), subnetting, subnet mask, Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR), introduction to IPv6. Routing algorithms: Shortest path routing (Dijkstra's algorithm), Distance Vector Routing (Bellman-Ford), Link State Routing. Internetworking protocols: ARP, RARP, ICMP."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Transport Layer)","topics":"Transport layer duties: Port numbers, sockets, multiplexing and demultiplexing. User Datagram Protocol (UDP): Segment structure, connectionless characteristics, applications. Transmission Control Protocol (TCP): Segment header, connection management (3-way handshake, termination), flow control using sliding window, TCP congestion control (slow start, congestion avoidance)."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Application Layer & Network Security)","topics":"Application layer protocols: Domain Name System (DNS), Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP), Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP/HTTPS), File Transfer Protocol (FTP), Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP), Post Office Protocol (POP3/IMAP). Network security: Security goals (CIA), cryptography basics (symmetric and asymmetric encryption, DES, RSA), digital signatures, firewalls (packet filtering, proxy firewalls)."}],"textBooks":["Andrew S. Tanenbaum & David J. Wetherall, \"Computer Networks\", Pearson Education.","Behrouz A. Forouzan, \"Data Communications and Networking\", McGraw-Hill Education."],"referenceBooks":["William Stallings, \"Data and Computer Communications\", Pearson.","James F. Kurose & Keith W. Ross, \"Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach\", Pearson."]}

subject.name: Environment and Ecology
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To create awareness regarding ecological balance, environmental pollution, resource conservation, global climatic challenges, and environmental legislation.","outcomes":["Students will explain ecosystem dynamics, analyze sources and controls of pollution, describe solid waste disposal, and understand Environmental Protection regulations."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Ecosystems & Natural Resources)","topics":"Concept of ecology and ecosystem: Structure and function, producers, consumers, decomposers, food chain, food web, ecological pyramids. Natural resources: Forest resources, water resources, mineral resources, energy resources (renewable and non-renewable - solar, wind, biomass, nuclear). Conservation of natural resources."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Environmental Pollution & Solid Waste Management)","topics":"Environmental pollution: Causes, effects, and control measures of Air pollution, Water pollution, Soil pollution, and Noise pollution. Air pollutants (SOx, NOx, particulate matter, carbon monoxide). Water quality standards (BOD, COD). Solid waste management: Causes, effects, and disposal methods of urban and industrial wastes, e-waste hazards and recycling."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Social Issues & Environmental Legislation)","topics":"Sustainable development, water conservation, rainwater harvesting. Global environmental issues: Global warming and greenhouse effect, acid rain, ozone layer depletion. Environmental protection laws in India: Environmental Protection Act 1986, Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1981, Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974. Role of information technology in environment and human health."}],"textBooks":["Benny Joseph, \"Environmental Studies\", Tata McGraw-Hill.","Anubha Kaushik & C.P. Kaushik, \"Perspectives in Environmental Studies\", New Age International Publishers."],"referenceBooks":["Erach Bharucha, \"Textbook of Environmental Studies for Undergraduate Courses\", Universities Press.","R. Rajagopalan, \"Environmental Studies: From Crisis to Cure\", Oxford University Press."]}

subject.name: Introduction to Cloud Computing
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To examine cloud architecture principles, deployment/service delivery models, virtualization mechanisms, cloud security controls, and enterprise migration strategies.","outcomes":["Students will evaluate IaaS/PaaS/SaaS offerings, describe hypervisor virtualization, understand elasticity and multi-tenancy, and analyze cloud deployment risks."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1 (Fundamentals & Evolution of Cloud Computing)","topics":"Definition, origins, and historical evolution of cloud computing. Essential characteristics of cloud computing (On-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, measured service). Advantages, business drivers, and limitations of cloud computing. NIST cloud reference architecture."},{"title":"Unit 2 (Cloud Service Models)","topics":"Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS): Capabilities, virtual machines, storage, networking, providers (Amazon EC2, Google Compute Engine). Platform as a Service (PaaS): Capabilities, development environments, database services (Google App Engine, AWS Elastic Beanstalk). Software as a Service (SaaS): Capabilities, web-based applications (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Salesforce). Comparison of IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS."},{"title":"Unit 3 (Cloud Deployment Models)","topics":"Public Cloud: Architecture, features, benefits, multi-tenancy, limitations. Private Cloud: On-premises vs hosted private cloud, security advantages. Hybrid Cloud: Integration of public and private cloud, cloud bursting. Community Cloud. Criteria for choosing cloud deployment models."},{"title":"Unit 4 (Virtualization Technologies in Cloud)","topics":"Virtualization role in cloud computing. Hardware virtualization, server virtualization, storage virtualization, network virtualization. Hypervisors: Type-1 (bare-metal) and Type-2 (hosted). Virtual machine management, live migration, resource scheduling, high availability. Containerization technologies: Docker containers, comparison of containers and virtual machines."},{"title":"Unit 5 (Cloud Security & Provider Ecosystem)","topics":"Security challenges in cloud: Data privacy, data loss, shared technology vulnerabilities, identity and access management (IAM). Cloud security controls, encryption, backup, Disaster Recovery as a Service (DRaaS). Overview of major public cloud providers: Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Case study of enterprise cloud migration."}],"textBooks":["Rajkumar Buyya, Christian Vecchiola & S. Thamarai Selvi, \"Mastering Cloud Computing\", McGraw-Hill Education.","Thomas Erl, Zaigham Mahmood & Ricardo Puttini, \"Cloud Computing: Concepts, Technology & Architecture\", Prentice Hall / Pearson."],"referenceBooks":["Barrie Sosinsky, \"Cloud Computing Bible\", Wiley India.","Anthony T. Velte, Toby J. Velte & Robert Elsenpeter, \"Cloud Computing: A Practical Approach\", Tata McGraw-Hill."]}

subject.name: Web Technology Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To develop full-stack responsive web applications utilizing HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, XML, and server-side script integrations.","outcomes":["Students will build responsive websites, validate complex user input, style with CSS3 Flexbox/Grid, and create data-driven web pages."],"labExperiments":["Creating a semantic HTML5 web page structure incorporating header, nav, section, article, aside, and footer tags.","Designing responsive multi-column layouts using CSS3 Flexbox and CSS Grid with media queries.","Form validation using JavaScript: Validating username, email, phone number, password strength, and postal codes.","Interactive UI features: Image sliders, modal popups, accordion panels, and dropdown navigation menus using JavaScript DOM.","Creating well-formed XML documents, defining internal/external DTDs, and validating with XML Schema (XSD).","Server-side scripting with PHP/Node.js: Handling form submissions (GET and POST methods) and saving records to MySQL.","User authentication system: Building user registration, login, session tracking, and logout with MySQL database.","Capstone Mini-Project: Developing and deploying an interactive dynamic web application with responsive styling."]}

subject.name: Project Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To synthesize theoretical computer engineering knowledge into designing, engineering, testing, and presenting a major functional capstone project.","outcomes":["Students will formulate engineering project specifications, design database/software architecture, implement functional code, perform systematic testing, compile professional documentation, and deliver technical presentations."]}

subject.name: Industrial Training and Seminar
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To expose students to industrial workflows, professional engineering practices, software development lifecycles, and technical seminar presentation.","outcomes":["Students will present industry internship technical experience, document organizational practices, and deliver oral seminar presentations before a faculty evaluation panel."]}

subject.name: Discipline & General Proficiency
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":"To assess culminating polytechnic discipline, professional ethics, placement preparation, and institutional citizenship.","outcomes":["Demonstrated professional readiness, ethical engineering practice, teamwork, and overall institutional proficiency."]}

subject.name: English
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To develop comprehensive communication skills in English for engineering undergraduates.","To enhance vocabulary, grammatical competence, and professional writing skills.","To foster critical reading and analysis of literary and technical prose."],"outcomes":["Demonstrate proficiency in core grammar, tense consistency, and vocabulary usage.","Draft structured professional emails, formal letters, resumes, and technical reports.","Communicate effectively in group discussions, presentations, and interviews."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Prose & Poetry","topics":"A Cup of Tea by Katherine Mansfield; The Piece of String by Guy De Maupassant; Steve Jobs Commencement Address (2005); Ode to the Skylark by P.B. Shelley; Where the Mind Is Without Fear by Rabindranath Tagore; The Road Not Taken by Robert Frost."},{"title":"Unit 2: Grammar & Vocabulary","topics":"Tenses and concept of time; Verb types; Active and Passive Voice; Direct and Indirect Speech; Prepositions and Conditionals; Modal Auxiliaries; Conjunctions; Synonyms, Antonyms, and One-word substitutions."},{"title":"Unit 3: Writing Skills","topics":"Paragraph writing; Essay writing; Formal letters and applications; Technical articles for publications; Resume writing and cover letters."},{"title":"Unit 4: Reading Skills","topics":"Reading comprehension techniques; Skimming and scanning; Summarizing and note-making; Critical interpretation of technical texts."},{"title":"Unit 5: Speaking Skills","topics":"Basics of spoken communication; Public speaking and presentation delivery; Welcome and introductory speeches; Vote of thanks; Avoiding Indianisms in professional discourse."}],"textBooks":["Pushp Lata & Sanjay Kumar, 'Communication Skills', Oxford University Press.","Meenakshi Raman & Sangeeta Sharma, 'Technical Communication: Principles and Practice', Oxford University Press."],"referenceBooks":["M. Ashraf Rizvi, 'Effective Technical Communication', McGraw Hill Education.","Wren & Martin, 'High School English Grammar and Composition', S. Chand & Co."]}

subject.name: Engineering Mathematics-I
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To provide thorough analytical training in differential equations, partial differentiation, and multivariable calculus.","To introduce integral calculus applications including multiple integrals and vector calculus for engineers."],"outcomes":["Solve first-order and higher-order ordinary and partial differential equations.","Calculate maxima, minima, asymptotes, and curve tracing for functions of several variables.","Compute double and triple integrals and evaluate line, surface, and volume integrals using Gauss and Stokes theorems."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Differential Equations","topics":"First-order first-degree differential equations; Linear and reducible to linear equations; Exact and integrating factors; Second-order ODE with variable coefficients; Homogeneous equations; Series solutions; First-order PDE (Lagrange form)."},{"title":"Unit 2: Differential Calculus","topics":"Partial differentiation; Euler's theorem on homogeneous functions; Approximation of errors; Maxima and minima of multivariable functions; Lagrange's multiplier method; Asymptotes and Cartesian/Polar curve tracing."},{"title":"Unit 3: Integral Calculus","topics":"Area of curves, rectification, surface areas, and volumes of revolution; Double and triple integrals; Change of order of integration; Transformation to polar coordinates; Beta and Gamma functions."},{"title":"Unit 4: Matrices","topics":"Rank of a matrix; Reduction to normal and echelon forms; Consistency of linear system equations; Eigenvalues and eigenvectors; Cayley-Hamilton theorem; Matrix diagonalization."},{"title":"Unit 5: Vector Calculus","topics":"Scalar and vector fields; Directional derivatives; Gradient, Divergence, and Curl; Line, surface, and volume integrals; Green's theorem, Gauss Divergence theorem, and Stokes' theorem with engineering applications."}],"textBooks":["B.V. Ramana, 'Higher Engineering Mathematics', Tata McGraw Hill.","Erwin Kreyszig, 'Advanced Engineering Mathematics', 9th Edition, Wiley."],"referenceBooks":["B.S. Grewal, 'Higher Engineering Mathematics', Khanna Publishers.","Thomas & Finney, 'Calculus and Analytic Geometry', Narosa Publishing House."]}

subject.name: Physics for Engineers-I
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce fundamental wave optics, relativistic mechanics, quantum physics, and laser fundamentals essential for engineering systems."],"outcomes":["Analyze interference, diffraction, and polarization phenomena in optical devices.","Apply special relativity concepts including length contraction, time dilation, and mass-energy equivalence.","Understand laser physics, semiconductor laser operation, and fiber optic communication principles."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Optics & Wave Motion","topics":"Interference by division of wave-front and amplitude; Newton's rings; Diffraction: Fresnel and Fraunhofer diffraction; Single slit, double slit, and N-slit diffraction grating; Resolving power; Polarization by reflection and double refraction; Brewster's law; Nicol prism."},{"title":"Unit 2: Special Theory of Relativity","topics":"Inertial frames; Michelson-Morley experiment; Postulates of special relativity; Lorentz transformations; Length contraction; Time dilation; Addition of velocities; Relativistic mass and mass-energy relation."},{"title":"Unit 3: Quantum Mechanics","topics":"De Broglie hypothesis; Wave-particle duality; Davisson-Germer experiment; Heisenberg uncertainty principle; Wave function and Born interpretation; Time-dependent and time-independent Schrodinger wave equations; Particle in a 1D box."},{"title":"Unit 4: Lasers & Fiber Optics","topics":"Spontaneous and stimulated emission; Einstein's coefficients; Population inversion; Ruby laser and He-Ne laser; Semiconductor lasers; Optical fibers: Numerical aperture, acceptance angle, V-number, single-mode and multi-mode fibers, attenuation in fibers."},{"title":"Unit 5: Electromagnetism & Modern Physics","topics":"Continuity equation; Maxwell's equations in vacuum and dielectric media; Electromagnetic waves; Poynting vector; Superconductivity: Meissner effect, Type-I and Type-II superconductors, BCS theory basics."}],"textBooks":["H.K. Malik & A.K. Singh, 'Engineering Physics', Tata McGraw Hill.","Arthur Beiser, 'Concepts of Modern Physics', McGraw Hill."],"referenceBooks":["David J. Griffiths, 'Introduction to Electrodynamics', Prentice Hall.","Ghatak & Thyagarajan, 'Optics', Tata McGraw Hill."]}

subject.name: Basic Electrical and Electronics
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To impart fundamental concepts of DC and AC circuit analysis, electrical machines, semiconductor devices, and digital logic gates."],"outcomes":["Solve complex electrical networks using Kirchhoff's laws and network theorems.","Analyze single-phase and three-phase AC circuits and transformers.","Understand diode characteristics, transistor operation, and basic analog/digital circuits."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: DC Circuit Analysis","topics":"Circuit elements; Kirchhoff's laws (KCL, KVL); Mesh and Nodal analysis; Superposition theorem; Thevenin's theorem; Norton's theorem; Maximum power transfer theorem; Star-Delta transformations."},{"title":"Unit 2: AC Circuits","topics":"Sinusoidal AC quantities, peak, average, and RMS values; Form factor and peak factor; Phasor representation; Single-phase R-L, R-C, R-L-C series and parallel circuits; Resonance in electrical circuits; Three-phase balanced star and delta connections."},{"title":"Unit 3: Transformers & Electrical Machines","topics":"Single-phase transformer: Construction, principle of operation, EMF equation, equivalent circuit, losses and efficiency; Introduction to DC motors and 3-phase induction motors: Working principles and characteristics."},{"title":"Unit 4: Semiconductor Devices","topics":"P-N junction diode: VI characteristics, half-wave, full-wave and bridge rectifiers; Zener diode as voltage regulator; Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT): CB, CE, CC configurations and DC load line; Field Effect Transistor (FET) basics."},{"title":"Unit 5: Digital Electronics Basics","topics":"Number systems (Binary, Octal, Hexadecimal); Boolean algebra and De Morgan's theorems; Logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR); Half-adder and Full-adder circuits; Introduction to Operational Amplifiers (Op-Amp)."}],"textBooks":["D.P. Kothari & I.J. Nagrath, 'Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering', McGraw Hill.","V.K. Mehta & Rohit Mehta, 'Principles of Electrical Engineering & Electronics', S. Chand."],"referenceBooks":["Vincent Del Toro, 'Electrical Engineering Fundamentals', Prentice Hall.","Robert Boylestad & Louis Nashelsky, 'Electronic Devices and Circuit Theory', Pearson."]}

subject.name: Problem Solving and Programming in C
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce algorithmic problem solving, procedural programming, and ANSI C language concepts."],"outcomes":["Design flowcharts and pseudo-code to formulate algorithmic solutions.","Write, compile, and debug structured C programs utilizing arrays, strings, functions, pointers, and structures.","Perform dynamic memory allocation and file handling in C."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Introduction to Programming & C Basics","topics":"Algorithms, flowcharts, pseudocode; Compilation and execution phases; Structure of a C program; Identifiers, keywords, data types, constants, variables; Operators: Arithmetic, relational, logical, bitwise, assignment, ternary; Operator precedence and type conversion."},{"title":"Unit 2: Control Structures","topics":"Decision making statements: if, if-else, nested if-else, switch-case; Iteration statements: while, do-while, for loops; Break, continue, goto statements; Loop design patterns and nested loops."},{"title":"Unit 3: Arrays & Strings","topics":"1D and 2D arrays: Declaration, initialization, memory layout, array traversal; Matrix operations (addition, multiplication, transpose); String handling: String input/output, null terminator, string manipulation library functions (strlen, strcpy, strcat, strcmp), custom string implementations."},{"title":"Unit 4: Functions & Pointers","topics":"User-defined functions, function prototypes, parameters, call by value vs. call by reference; Recursion and call stack; Pointers: Declaration, dereferencing, pointer arithmetic; Pointers with arrays and strings; Function pointers; Dynamic memory management: malloc, calloc, realloc, free."},{"title":"Unit 5: Structures, Unions & File Handling","topics":"User-defined types: struct, union, enum, typedef; Nested structures and arrays of structures; Self-referential structures; File operations: File pointers, modes (r, w, a), formatted file I/O (fprintf, fscanf), character/string I/O (fgetc, fputc, fgets, fputs), binary I/O (fread, fwrite)."}],"textBooks":["E. Balagurusamy, 'Programming in ANSI C', 8th Edition, McGraw Hill.","Reema Thareja, 'Programming in C', Oxford University Press."],"referenceBooks":["Brian W. Kernighan & Dennis M. Ritchie, 'The C Programming Language', Prentice Hall.","Yashavant Kanetkar, 'Let Us C', BPB Publications."]}

subject.name: Fundamentals of IOT Development
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce IoT architecture, embedded microcontrollers, sensors, actuators, and cloud-connected IoT devices."],"outcomes":["Explain end-to-end Internet of Things architecture and reference models.","Interface sensors and actuators with Arduino and Raspberry Pi hardware boards.","Implement basic IoT telemetry, data acquisition, and cloud dashboards."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Introduction to Internet of Things","topics":"Definition, characteristics, physical and logical design of IoT; IoT enabling technologies; IoT levels and deployment templates; Domain-specific IoT applications (Smart Cities, Healthcare, Agriculture, Industrial IoT)."},{"title":"Unit 2: IoT Sensors & Actuators","topics":"Sensor classification: Temperature, humidity, ultrasonic, PIR, gas, accelerometer; Analog vs. digital sensors; Actuators: Relays, DC motors, servo motors, stepper motors; Signal conditioning and ADC conversion."},{"title":"Unit 3: Embedded Prototyping Platforms","topics":"Microcontroller architectures; Arduino Uno/Nano: Pinout, IDE, programming in Embedded C; Raspberry Pi: Hardware, OS installation, Python scripting for GPIO interfacing; ESP8266 and ESP32 Wi-Fi microcontrollers."},{"title":"Unit 4: IoT Communication Protocols","topics":"Network layers in IoT; WPAN protocols: Bluetooth, BLE, ZigBee, 6LoWPAN; Application layer protocols: MQTT, CoAP, HTTP, WebSockets; Gateway architecture and edge compute fundamentals."},{"title":"Unit 5: Cloud Integration & IoT Security","topics":"Connecting edge devices to IoT Cloud platforms (ThingsSpeak, Blynk, AWS IoT Core); Real-time telemetry visualization; Basic security concerns, device authentication, and encryption in IoT deployments."}],"textBooks":["Arshdeep Bahga & Vijay Madisetti, 'Internet of Things: A Hands-On Approach', Universities Press.","Raj Kamal, 'Internet of Things: Architecture and Design Principles', McGraw Hill."],"referenceBooks":["David Hanes et al., 'IoT Fundamentals: Networking Technologies, Protocols, and Use Cases for the Internet of Things', Cisco Press."]}

subject.name: Physics for Engineers Lab-I
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To verify optical and modern physical principles experimentally."],"outcomes":["Measure optical parameters using interferometers, spectrometers, and lasers."],"labExperiments":["To determine the wavelength of sodium light by Newton's Ring experiment.","To determine the wavelength of spectral lines using a diffraction grating.","To determine the specific rotation of cane sugar solution using a polarimeter.","To determine the focal length of a combination of lenses using nodal slide assembly.","To determine the bandgap of a semiconductor using a reverse-biased P-N junction diode.","To determine the wavelength of He-Ne laser beam using diffraction grating.","To determine the numerical aperture and acceptance angle of an optical fiber."]}

subject.name: Basic Electrical and Electronics Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To verify fundamental electrical network laws and characterize electronic components."],"outcomes":["Construct DC circuits, evaluate network theorems, and measure AC parameters."],"labExperiments":["Verification of Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) and Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL).","Verification of Superposition Theorem in DC resistive circuits.","Verification of Thevenin's and Norton's Theorems.","Verification of Maximum Power Transfer Theorem.","Measurement of power and power factor in single-phase R-L-C series circuit.","Open-circuit and short-circuit tests on a single-phase transformer.","V-I characteristics of P-N junction diode and Zener diode.","Input and output characteristics of Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT) in CE configuration.","Half-wave and full-wave rectifier circuit analysis using oscilloscope."]}

subject.name: Problem Solving and Programming in C Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To implement C programs covering procedural problem solving, data structures, and algorithms."],"outcomes":["Write, compile, test, and debug C programs for diverse algorithmic tasks."],"labExperiments":["Write a C program to compute simple/compound interest and temperature conversions.","Write a C program to find the largest of three numbers using nested if-else.","Write a C program to print Fibonacci series, check prime numbers, and compute factorial.","Write a C program to perform matrix addition, multiplication, and transpose.","Write a C program to check palindrome string and count vowels, consonants, and digits.","Write a C program to implement functions with call-by-value and call-by-reference.","Write a C program to implement recursive functions for GCD and Tower of Hanoi.","Write a C program using dynamic memory allocation (malloc, calloc, free) for array processing.","Write a C program to maintain student records using structures and file handling."]}

subject.name: Workshop Practice
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To impart hands-on training in basic mechanical fabrication, carpentry, fitting, and sheet metal works."],"outcomes":["Operate workshop tools safely and fabricate joints and sheet metal models."],"labExperiments":["Carpentry Shop: T-Lap joint and Cross-Lap joint fabrication.","Fitting Shop: Square fitting, V-fitting, filing, and hacksawing.","Sheet Metal Shop: Development and fabrication of rectangular tray and funnel.","Welding Shop: Preparation of Lap and Butt joints using Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW).","Foundry Shop: Preparation of sand mould using single-piece pattern."]}

subject.name: IT Workshop
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To train students in PC assembly, OS installation, shell commands, and productive office tools."],"outcomes":["Assemble computer hardware, troubleshoot OS, and automate documents and spreadsheets."],"labExperiments":["Hardware Identification: PC assembly, disassembly, motherboard components, RAM, CPU, GPU, storage.","Operating System Installation: Dual-boot setup with Windows and Linux (Ubuntu).","BIOS/UEFI Configuration: Boot order, virtualization enabling (VT-x/AMD-V), secure boot.","Linux CLI Essentials: Navigation, permissions (chmod/chown), process management, shell scripting.","Productivity Suite: Advanced LaTeX document authoring, formatting formulas, bibliography.","Spreadsheet Automation: Formulas, pivot tables, charting, and statistical functions in MS Excel / Calc.","Network Setup: Configuring LAN, IPv4 addresses, subnets, testing connectivity via ping and traceroute."]}

subject.name: Soft Skills and Self Awareness
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To cultivate emotional intelligence, interpersonal skills, personal ethics, and self-awareness."],"outcomes":["Demonstrate self-confidence, active listening, time management, and ethical decision-making."],"labExperiments":["Self-Discovery: Johari Window exercise, personal SWOT analysis.","Goal Setting: SMART goals formulation and action planning.","Active Listening & Empathy Exercises: Group dynamics and emotional intelligence role plays.","Time Management Techniques: Pomodoro technique, Eisenhower matrix prioritization.","Stress Management and Mindfulness: Breathing exercises and cognitive reframing.","Personal Grooming & Body Language: Non-verbal communication, posture, handshake, professional etiquette."]}

subject.name: Professional English
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To develop advanced corporate communication, technical reporting, and cross-cultural workplace skills."],"outcomes":["Compose professional business proposals, technical reports, and meeting minutes.","Demonstrate persuasive presentation abilities and debate skills."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Fundamentals of Professional Communication","topics":"Process of communication; Upward, downward, horizontal, and diagonal channels; Grapevine communication; Communication barriers: Physical, semantic, psychological, and organizational."},{"title":"Unit 2: Business Correspondence","topics":"Business letters: Inquiry, quotation, order, complaint, and adjustment; Memorandum, circulars, office orders, notices, agenda, and minutes of meeting."},{"title":"Unit 3: Technical Report Writing","topics":"Characteristics of technical reports; Structure and elements of a formal report: Title page, abstract, table of contents, introduction, methodology, findings, conclusion, recommendations, bibliography, appendices; Progress reports and feasibility studies."},{"title":"Unit 4: Proposal Writing & Technical Articles","topics":"Research and project proposals: Problem statement, scope, timeline, budget estimation, deliverables; Writing white papers and executive summaries."},{"title":"Unit 5: Corporate Communication & Etiquette","topics":"Cross-cultural communication; Telephone and video conferencing etiquette; Professional ethics; Negotiation strategies and handling conflicts."}],"textBooks":["Meenakshi Raman & Sangeeta Sharma, 'Technical Communication: Principles and Practice', Oxford University Press.","Herta A. Murphy et al., 'Effective Business Communication', Tata McGraw Hill."],"referenceBooks":["Raymond V. Lesikar, 'Business Communication: Connecting in a Digital World', McGraw Hill."]}

subject.name: Engineering Mathematics-II
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To provide rigorous mathematical foundations in linear algebra, Laplace transforms, Fourier series, and complex analysis."],"outcomes":["Apply Laplace transforms to solve ordinary differential equations and initial value problems.","Evaluate Fourier series expansions for periodic waveforms.","Use analytic functions, Cauchy-Riemann equations, and contour integration in complex plane."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Laplace Transforms","topics":"Definition, existence theorem; Transforms of elementary functions; Shifting theorems; Transforms of derivatives and integrals; Periodic functions; Unit step and Dirac delta functions; Inverse Laplace transforms; Convolution theorem; Applications to solving linear ODEs."},{"title":"Unit 2: Fourier Series","topics":"Periodic functions; Dirichlet conditions; Euler formulas; Fourier series for functions of arbitrary period; Even and odd functions; Half-range Fourier sine and cosine series; Parseval identity; Harmonic analysis."},{"title":"Unit 3: Complex Variables - Analytic Functions","topics":"Complex numbers and functions; Limit, continuity, and differentiability; Cauchy-Riemann equations in Cartesian and polar forms; Harmonic functions and conjugate harmonics; Conformal mapping and bilinear transformations."},{"title":"Unit 4: Complex Integration","topics":"Line integral in complex plane; Cauchy integral theorem; Cauchy integral formula for derivatives; Taylor and Laurent series expansions; Singularities, poles, and essential singularities; Residue theorem and real definite integrals evaluation."},{"title":"Unit 5: Partial Differential Equations Applications","topics":"Method of separation of variables; Solution of 1D wave equation; Solution of 1D heat conduction equation; 2D Laplace equation in Cartesian coordinates."}],"textBooks":["Erwin Kreyszig, 'Advanced Engineering Mathematics', 9th Edition, Wiley.","B.V. Ramana, 'Higher Engineering Mathematics', Tata McGraw Hill."],"referenceBooks":["B.S. Grewal, 'Higher Engineering Mathematics', Khanna Publishers.","R.K. Jain & S.R.K. Iyengar, 'Advanced Engineering Mathematics', Narosa."]}

subject.name: Physics for Engineers-II
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To explore solid-state physics, semiconductor device physics, dielectric and magnetic materials, and nanotechnology fundamentals."],"outcomes":["Describe crystal structures, Miller indices, and X-ray diffraction in solids.","Analyze intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductor band theory and carrier transport.","Classify magnetic and dielectric materials and explain nanostructure properties."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Crystal Structure & X-ray Diffraction","topics":"Space lattice, basis, unit cell; Bravais lattices; Miller indices; Interplanar spacing; Coordination number and packing fraction (SC, BCC, FCC, HCP); Bragg's law; Powder method of X-ray diffraction; Point defects and dislocations."},{"title":"Unit 2: Band Theory of Solids","topics":"Free electron theory (Drude-Lorentz, Sommerfeld); Fermi-Dirac distribution; Density of states; Kronig-Penney model and origin of energy bands; Effective mass; Distinction between metals, semiconductors, and insulators based on band gap."},{"title":"Unit 3: Semiconductor Physics","topics":"Intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors; Carrier concentration; Law of mass action; Fermi level position; Drift and diffusion currents; Hall effect and its applications; P-N junction under forward and reverse bias; Solar cell and photodetector principles."},{"title":"Unit 4: Magnetic & Dielectric Materials","topics":"Dia, para, ferro, antiferro, and ferrimagnetism; Domain theory of ferromagnetism; Hysteresis loop; Soft and hard magnetic materials; Dielectric polarization mechanisms (electronic, ionic, orientational); Clausius-Mossotti equation; Piezoelectricity, pyroelectricity, and ferroelectricity."},{"title":"Unit 5: Nanomaterials & Characterization","topics":"Introduction to nanoscience; Quantum confinement, quantum wells, wires, and dots; Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and graphene; Synthesis: Top-down and bottom-up approaches (sol-gel, CVD); Characterization techniques: SEM, TEM, and AFM basics; Engineering applications of nanomaterials."}],"textBooks":["Charles Kittel, 'Introduction to Solid State Physics', 8th Edition, Wiley.","S.O. Pillai, 'Solid State Physics', New Age International."],"referenceBooks":["Wahab M.A., 'Solid State Physics: Structure and Properties of Materials', Narosa.","H.K. Malik & A.K. Singh, 'Engineering Physics', McGraw Hill."]}

subject.name: Environmental Science
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To create environmental awareness, ecosystem understanding, pollution control methodologies, and sustainable green engineering practices."],"outcomes":["Assess environmental impacts of human activities and industrial engineering.","Propose pollution mitigation, solid waste management, and renewable energy solutions."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Environment & Natural Resources","topics":"Multidisciplinary nature of environmental studies; Renewable and non-renewable resources; Forest, water, mineral, food, and energy resources; Dams and environmental implications; Sustainable lifestyles."},{"title":"Unit 2: Ecosystems & Biodiversity","topics":"Concept of ecosystem: Structure and function; Producers, consumers, and decomposers; Energy flow and food chains/webs; Biodiversity: Genetic, species, and ecosystem diversity; Hotspots of biodiversity; Threats and conservation (In-situ & Ex-situ)."},{"title":"Unit 3: Environmental Pollution","topics":"Air pollution: Sources, greenhouse effect, ozone layer depletion, acid rain; Water pollution: Sources, eutrophication, BOD/COD; Soil pollution; Noise pollution; Marine and thermal pollution; Solid waste management: Municipal and electronic waste (e-waste) handling."},{"title":"Unit 4: Social Issues & the Environment","topics":"Sustainable development; Urban problems related to energy; Water harvesting and watershed management; Environmental ethics; Climate change and global warming; Carbon footprint and credits."},{"title":"Unit 5: Environmental Regulations & Field Work","topics":"Environment Protection Act; Air (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act; Water Act; Wildlife Protection Act; Forest Conservation Act; Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA); Field study of local polluted sites or ecosystems."}],"textBooks":["Erach Bharucha, 'Textbook of Environmental Studies for Undergraduate Courses', Universities Press.","Anubha Kaushik & C.P. Kaushik, 'Perspectives in Environmental Studies', New Age International."],"referenceBooks":["R. Rajagopalan, 'Environmental Studies: From Crisis to Cure', Oxford University Press."]}

subject.name: Design Thinking

subject.name: Industrial Communication Protocols & Connectivity
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To understand industrial automation fieldbuses, telemetry protocols, SCADA, and secure industrial cloud connectivity."],"outcomes":["Analyze industrial serial, fieldbus, and Ethernet networking protocols.","Configure Modbus, Profibus, CAN, and OPC-UA communication in automation stacks.","Design cloud telemetry pipelines for IIoT manufacturing workflows."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Industrial Automation & Network Hierarchy","topics":"Industrial automation pyramid (field, control, supervisory, enterprise levels); Requirements for industrial networks: Determinism, latency, reliability, noise immunity; Serial communication standards (RS-232, RS-422, RS-485)."},{"title":"Unit 2: Fieldbus Protocols","topics":"Modbus RTU and Modbus TCP: Message frame formats, function codes, master-slave communication; Profibus DP and PA; Foundation Fieldbus; Controller Area Network (CAN) bus: Arbitration, error handling, CANopen."},{"title":"Unit 3: Industrial Ethernet & Real-Time Networks","topics":"Industrial Ethernet standards; EtherNet/IP, Profinet, EtherCAT; Deterministic real-time Ethernet; TSN (Time-Sensitive Networking) standards; Wireless industrial protocols: WirelessHART, ISA100.11a."},{"title":"Unit 4: SCADA & OPC Unified Architecture (OPC-UA)","topics":"SCADA architecture and telemetry; RTUs and PLCs; OPC classic vs. OPC Unified Architecture (OPC-UA): Information model, security architecture, pub/sub model; Edge gateways for legacy protocol translation."},{"title":"Unit 5: Industrial Cloud Connectivity & Cyber Security","topics":"Connecting OT networks to IT cloud infrastructures; Industrial MQTT brokers; Securing industrial control systems (IEC 62443 standard); Network segmentation and demilitarized zones (DMZ); Remote monitoring dashboards."}],"textBooks":["Bogdan M. Wilamowski & J. David Irwin, 'Industrial Communication Systems', CRC Press.","Richard Zurawski, 'The Industrial Information Technology Handbook', CRC Press."],"referenceBooks":["Giacomo Veneri & Antonio Capasso, 'Hands-On Industrial Internet of Things', Packt Publishing."]}

subject.name: Statistics and Probability
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce statistical descriptive methods, discrete and continuous probability distributions, hypothesis testing, and regression analysis for computing sciences."],"outcomes":["Calculate mean, variance, moments, skewness, and kurtosis for empirical datasets.","Apply binomial, Poisson, and normal probability models to real-world engineering problems.","Perform hypothesis testing using t-test, z-test, chi-square test, and ANOVA."],"modules":[{"title":"UNIT -I: Descriptive Statistics","topics":"Measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode); Measures of dispersion (range, quartile deviation, mean deviation, standard deviation, variance, coefficient of variation); Moments, skewness, and kurtosis; Curve fitting by the method of least squares (fitting linear, parabolic, and exponential curves)."},{"title":"UNIT -II: Probability & Random Variables","topics":"Axiomatic definition of probability; Conditional probability, multiplication theorem, Bayes' theorem; Random variables: Discrete and continuous random variables; Probability Mass Function (PMF), Probability Density Function (PDF), Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF); Mathematical expectation, variance, and moment generating functions (MGF)."},{"title":"UNIT -III: Probability Distributions","topics":"Discrete distributions: Binomial distribution, Poisson distribution, Geometric distribution; Continuous distributions: Uniform distribution, Exponential distribution, Normal (Gaussian) distribution, standard normal distribution and properties, central limit theorem."},{"title":"UNIT -IV: Correlation & Regression","topics":"Bivariate data; Scatter diagram; Karl Pearson's coefficient of correlation; Spearman's rank correlation coefficient; Regression equations and regression lines; Angle between two lines of regression; Standard error of estimate."},{"title":"UNIT -V: Testing of Hypothesis & Analysis of Variance","topics":"Sampling distributions; Null and alternative hypothesis; Type-I and Type-II errors, level of significance; Large sample tests (z-test for single mean and difference of means); Small sample tests (Student's t-test for single mean, difference of means, paired t-test); Chi-square test for goodness of fit and independence of attributes; One-way and two-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA)."}],"textBooks":["S.C. Gupta & V.K. Kapoor, 'Fundamentals of Mathematical Statistics', Sultan Chand & Sons.","Sheldon M. Ross, 'Introduction to Probability and Statistics for Engineers and Scientists', Academic Press."],"referenceBooks":["Walpole, Myers, Myers & Ye, 'Probability and Statistics for Engineers and Scientists', Pearson.","B.S. Grewal, 'Higher Engineering Mathematics', Khanna Publishers."]}

subject.name: Digital Electronics
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To teach combinatorial and sequential digital logic circuit design, minimization techniques, and memory systems."],"outcomes":["Simplify Boolean expressions using Karnaugh maps and Quine-McCluskey tabulation.","Design combinational circuits like adders, subtractors, multiplexers, and decoders.","Design and analyze synchronous and asynchronous sequential circuits, flip-flops, counters, and registers."],"modules":[{"title":"UNIT -I: Boolean Algebra & Logic Simplification","topics":"Review of number systems and codes (BCD, Gray, Excess-3); Axiomatic definition of Boolean algebra and theorems; Canonical and standard forms; Karnaugh map (up to 5 variables), Don't care conditions; Prime implicants; Quine-McCluskey tabular minimization; Logic gates and universal gates implementation."},{"title":"UNIT -II: Combinational Logic Circuits","topics":"Design of adders: Half adder, Full adder, Ripple carry adder, Carry look-ahead adder; Subtractors: Half and Full subtractors; Binary parallel adder/subtractor; BCD adder; Magnitude comparator; Decoders (3:8, 4:16) and Encoders (Priority encoder); Multiplexers (4:1, 8:1) and Demultiplexers; Design of combinational circuits using MUX and Decoders; Code converters."},{"title":"UNIT -III: Sequential Logic Circuits","topics":"Latches and Flip-Flops: SR, D, JK, T and Master-Slave JK flip-flops; Triggering of flip-flops; Characteristic tables, characteristic equations, and excitation tables; Conversion between flip-flops; Timing considerations, setup and hold times."},{"title":"UNIT -IV: Registers & Counters","topics":"Registers: Shift registers (SISO, SIPO, PISO, PIPO), Universal shift register, Ring counter, Johnson counter; Counters: Asynchronous (ripple) counters (up, down, mod-N); Synchronous counters design; Up/Down synchronous counter; Sequence generators and State machine design with SM charts."},{"title":"UNIT -V: Memory & Programmable Logic","topics":"Memory hierarchy: RAM (SRAM, DRAM), ROM (PROM, EPROM, EEPROM, Flash); Memory decoding and expansion; Programmable Logic Devices (PLDs): Programmable Logic Array (PLA), Programmable Array Logic (PAL), Complex PLDs (CPLD), Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) architecture; Digital logic families (TTL, CMOS, ECL) characteristics."}],"textBooks":["M. Morris Mano & Michael D. Ciletti, 'Digital Design: With an Introduction to the Verilog HDL', Pearson.","R.P. Jain, 'Modern Digital Electronics', Tata McGraw Hill."],"referenceBooks":["Donald P. Leach & Albert Paul Malvino, 'Digital Principles and Applications', McGraw Hill.","Charles H. Roth Jr. & Larry L. Kinney, 'Fundamentals of Logic Design', Cengage Learning."]}

subject.name: Data Structures using C
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce linear and non-linear data structures, algorithm efficiency, dynamic memory operations, and sorting/searching."],"outcomes":["Analyze algorithm time and space complexity using asymptotic Big-O notations.","Implement stacks, queues, linked lists, binary search trees, and graphs in C.","Apply efficient sorting and hashing techniques to manage structured collections."],"modules":[{"title":"UNIT -I: Introduction to Data Structures & Arrays","topics":"Concept of Data Structures, Abstract Data Types (ADT); Algorithm complexity: Time and Space complexity, Asymptotic notations (Big O, Omega, Theta); Arrays: Memory representation (row-major and column-major), Operations on arrays, Sparse matrices and representation."},{"title":"UNIT -II: Stacks & Queues","topics":"Stack ADT: Array and linked representations, Push, Pop, Peek; Applications: Infix to Postfix conversion, Evaluation of Postfix expressions, Recursion simulation; Queue ADT: Array and linked representations; Circular queue, Deque (Double-ended queue), Priority queue and applications."},{"title":"UNIT -III: Linked Lists","topics":"Singly Linked List: Traversal, insertion, deletion, searching, reversing; Circular Linked List; Doubly Linked List: Operations and applications; Header linked lists; Polynomial representation and addition using linked lists."},{"title":"UNIT -IV: Trees & Binary Search Trees","topics":"Tree terminology; Binary Trees: Types, properties, array and linked representation; Binary Tree Traversals: Preorder, Inorder, Postorder, Level order; Binary Search Tree (BST): Insertion, deletion, searching; Balanced Trees: AVL trees (rotations and insertions), Introduction to B-Trees and Heaps."},{"title":"UNIT -V: Graphs, Searching & Sorting","topics":"Graph definitions and representations (Adjacency matrix, Adjacency list); Graph Traversals: Depth First Search (DFS), Breadth First Search (BFS); Spanning trees: Prim's and Kruskal's algorithms; Shortest path: Dijkstra's algorithm; Searching: Linear and Binary search; Sorting: Bubble sort, Selection sort, Insertion sort, Merge sort, Quick sort, Radix sort; Hashing: Hash functions, collision resolution techniques."}],"textBooks":["Reema Thareja, 'Data Structures Using C', Oxford University Press.","Ellis Horowitz, Sartaj Sahni & Susan Anderson-Freed, 'Fundamentals of Data Structures in C', Silicon Press."],"referenceBooks":["Aaron M. Tenenbaum et al., 'Data Structures Using C', Prentice Hall.","Seymour Lipschutz, 'Data Structures', Schaum's Outlines, McGraw Hill."]}

subject.name: Object Oriented Programming with Java
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To teach object-oriented software development using Java, including classes, inheritance, polymorphism, interfaces, multithreading, and collections."],"outcomes":["Implement OOP principles: Encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, and Abstraction in Java.","Build robust programs with Java Exception Handling and custom exceptions.","Utilize Multithreading, I/O Streams, and the Java Collections Framework."],"modules":[{"title":"UNIT -I: Java Basics & OOP Concepts","topics":"OOP paradigm vs. Procedure Oriented; Features of Java; JVM, JRE, JDK architecture; Bytecode and platform independence; Primitive types, variables, type casting; Operators and control statements; Classes, objects, methods, constructors, constructor overloading; 'this' keyword, garbage collection, and finalize method."},{"title":"UNIT -II: Inheritance, Polymorphism & Interfaces","topics":"Inheritance: Types of inheritance, 'super' keyword, method overriding, dynamic method dispatch; Abstract classes; 'final' keyword with variables, methods, and classes; Interfaces: Defining and implementing interfaces, multiple inheritance via interfaces, default and static methods in interfaces."},{"title":"UNIT -III: Packages, Exception Handling & Strings","topics":"Packages: Defining, creating, and accessing packages; Java I/O: Byte streams, Character streams, File input/output, Serialization and Deserialization."},{"title":"UNIT -V: Java Collections Framework & Generics","topics":"Generics: Generic classes, methods, and wildcards; Collections Overview: Collection interface, List (ArrayList, LinkedList, Vector), Set (HashSet, LinkedHashSet, TreeSet), Queue (PriorityQueue, ArrayDeque), Map (HashMap, TreeMap, LinkedHashMap); Iterators and for-each loop; Comparable and Comparator interfaces."}],"textBooks":["Herbert Schildt, 'Java: The Complete Reference', 12th Edition, McGraw Hill.","E. Balagurusamy, 'Programming with Java: A Primer', McGraw Hill."],"referenceBooks":["Kathy Sierra & Bert Bates, 'Head First Java', O'Reilly Media.","Joshua Bloch, 'Effective Java', Addison-Wesley."]}

subject.name: Database Management System
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To teach relational database design, entity-relationship modeling, relational algebra, SQL querying, normalization, transaction processing, and concurrency control."],"outcomes":["Design conceptual database schemas using ER and Extended ER diagrams.","Write complex SQL queries, views, constraints, triggers, and stored procedures.","Apply normalization up to BCNF and ensure ACID properties and serializability."],"modules":[{"title":"UNIT -I: Introduction to DBMS & Conceptual Modeling","topics":"Database system concepts and architecture; File system vs. DBMS; Data models, schemas, and instances; Three-schema architecture and data independence; Entity-Relationship (ER) model: Entities, attributes, entity sets, relationships, cardinalities; Strong and weak entities; Enhanced ER (EER) modeling: Specialization, generalization, and aggregation; Mapping ER models to relational schemas."},{"title":"UNIT -II: Relational Model & SQL","topics":"Relational model concepts: Domains, attributes, tuples, relations; Relational integrity constraints: Domain, key, entity, and referential integrity; Relational Algebra operations: Select, Project, Join, Set operations, Division; SQL: DDL, DML, DCL, TCL; Nested subqueries, joins (inner, outer), aggregate functions, GROUP BY, HAVING; Views, indexes, sequences."},{"title":"UNIT -III: Relational Database Design & Normalization","topics":"Informal design guidelines; Functional dependencies: Inference rules (Armstrong's axioms), closure of FD set and attributes; Normalization: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF); Multi-valued dependencies and 4NF; Lossless-join decomposition and dependency preservation."},{"title":"UNIT -IV: Transaction Management & Concurrency Control","topics":"Transaction concepts and states; ACID properties; Schedules and recoverability; Serializability: Conflict serializability and view serializability; Concurrency control protocols: Two-Phase Locking (2PL), strict and rigorous 2PL; Timestamp ordering protocol; Deadlock handling: Prevention, detection, and recovery."},{"title":"UNIT -V: Database Recovery, Security & Modern Databases","topics":"Failure classification; Recovery concepts: Log-based recovery (deferred and immediate update), Checkpoints, Shadow paging; Database security and authorization: GRANT, REVOKE; Introduction to distributed databases; Overview of NoSQL databases: Key-value, document, column-family, and graph databases."}],"textBooks":["Abraham Silberschatz, Henry F. Korth & S. Sudarshan, 'Database System Concepts', 7th Edition, McGraw Hill.","Ramez Elmasri & Shamkant B. Navathe, 'Fundamentals of Database Systems', Pearson."],"referenceBooks":["Raghu Ramakrishnan & Johannes Gehrke, 'Database Management Systems', McGraw Hill.","C.J. Date, 'An Introduction to Database Systems', Addison-Wesley."]}

subject.name: Introduction to Data Analytics
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce data science lifecycles, data wrangling, exploratory data analysis (EDA), statistical inference, and predictive modeling using Python."],"outcomes":["Clean, transform, and aggregate structured datasets using NumPy and Pandas.","Visualize data distributions, trends, and correlations using Matplotlib and Seaborn.","Build foundational regression, classification, and clustering models for business analytics."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Data Analytics Foundations & Python","topics":"Overview of data analytics lifecycle: Discovery, preparation, planning, modeling, communicating results; Importing CSV, Excel, JSON, and SQL data; Handling missing data (imputation, dropping); Data transformation: Filtering, sorting, grouping, pivoting, merging, joining, and concatenating; String and date-time operations."},{"title":"Unit 3: Exploratory Data Analysis & Visualization","topics":"Descriptive statistics;
