subject.name: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To teach algorithmic problem-solving paradigms (Divide-and-Conquer, Greedy, Dynamic Programming, Backtracking, Branch-and-Bound) and computational complexity theory."],"outcomes":["Formulate recurrence relations and solve them using Master Theorem and substitution.","Apply greedy algorithms and dynamic programming to solve optimization problems.","Differentiate between P, NP, NP-Complete, and NP-Hard complexity classes."],"modules":[{"title":"UNIT -I: Introduction & Growth of Functions","topics":"Notion of an Algorithm; Fundamentals of algorithmic problem solving; Asymptotic notations (O, Ω, Θ, o, ω); Standard complexity classes; Recurrence relations: Substitution method, Recursion tree method, Master's theorem and master theorem master cases; Analysis of non-recursive and recursive algorithms."},{"title":"UNIT -II: Divide and Conquer","topics":"Divide and conquer design paradigm; Binary Search; Merge Sort; Quick Sort and randomized quick sort analysis; Strassen's matrix multiplication; Finding maximum and minimum elements; Convex hull problem."},{"title":"UNIT -III: Greedy Method","topics":"Greedy choice property and optimal substructure; Fractional Knapsack problem; Minimum cost spanning trees (Prim's and Kruskal's algorithms); Single-source shortest paths (Dijkstra's algorithm); Huffman coding and data compression; Job sequencing with deadlines."},{"title":"UNIT -IV: Dynamic Programming","topics":"Principle of optimality; Memoization vs. Tabulation; 0/1 Knapsack problem; Matrix Chain Multiplication; Longest Common Subsequence (LCS); All-Pairs Shortest Paths (Floyd-Warshall algorithm); Bellman-Ford shortest paths algorithm; Travelling Salesperson Problem (TSP)."},{"title":"UNIT -V: Backtracking, Branch & Bound, and NP-Completeness","topics":"State space trees; Backtracking: N-Queens problem, Subset sum problem, Graph coloring, Hamiltonian cycle; Branch and Bound: Assignment problem, 0/1 Knapsack, TSP; Computational Complexity: Deterministic vs. Non-deterministic algorithms, Classes P, NP, NP-Complete, and NP-Hard; Cook's theorem; Reducibility and standard NP-Complete problems (3-SAT, Clique, Vertex Cover)."}],"textBooks":["Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest & Clifford Stein, 'Introduction to Algorithms', 4th Edition, MIT Press / PHI.","Ellis Horowitz, Sartaj Sahni & Sanguthevar Rajasekaran, 'Fundamentals of Computer Algorithms', Universities Press."],"referenceBooks":["Jon Kleinberg & Éva Tardos, 'Algorithm Design', Pearson.","Alfred V. Aho, John E. Hopcroft & Jeffrey D. Ullman, 'The Design and Analysis of Computer Algorithms', Pearson."]}

subject.name: Operating Systems
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce operating system structures, process scheduling, synchronization, deadlocks, memory management, and file storage systems."],"outcomes":["Analyze CPU scheduling algorithms (FCFS, SJF, Priority, Round Robin).","Solve race conditions and synchronization problems using semaphores and mutexes.","Evaluate paging, segmentation, and virtual memory page replacement algorithms."],"modules":[{"title":"UNIT -I: Operating System Overview & System Calls","topics":"Role and functions of operating system; Operating system operations (dual-mode operation, privileged instructions); Computing environments; OS structures: Monolithic, layered, microkernel, modular architectures; System calls: Types and mechanisms; System boot process."},{"title":"UNIT -II: Process Management & CPU Scheduling","topics":"Process concept, PCB (Process Control Block); Process states and state transitions; Process scheduling: Queues, schedulers (long-term, short-term, medium-term), context switching; Inter-Process Communication (IPC): Shared memory and message passing; Threads: User-level and kernel-level threads, multithreading models; CPU scheduling algorithms: FCFS, SJF, SRTF, Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel Queue, Multilevel Feedback Queue."},{"title":"UNIT -III: Process Synchronization & Deadlocks","topics":"Critical Section problem; Peterson's solution; Hardware support for synchronization (TestAndSet, Swap); Semaphores (counting and binary); Classical IPC problems: Producer-Consumer, Dining Philosophers, Readers-Writers; Monitors; Deadlocks: System model, deadlock characterization (necessary conditions), Resource Allocation Graph (RAG); Deadlock handling: Prevention, Avoidance (Banker's algorithm), Detection and Recovery."},{"title":"UNIT -IV: Memory Management","topics":"Logical vs. Physical address space; Swapping; Contiguous memory allocation: Fixed and dynamic partitioning, placement strategies (First-fit, Best-fit, Worst-fit), fragmentation (internal and external); Paging: Hardware implementation, TLB (Translation Lookaside Buffer), page table structures (hierarchical, hashed, inverted); Segmentation; Virtual Memory: Demand paging, page fault handling, page replacement algorithms (FIFO, Optimal, LRU, LFU), Thrashing and working-set model."},{"title":"UNIT -V: Storage Management & File Systems","topics":"File concept: Attributes, operations, types, access methods (sequential, direct); Directory structures: Single-level, two-level, tree-structured; File system mounting and sharing; Protection and access control lists; File system implementation: Directory allocation, allocation methods (contiguous, linked, indexed), free space management (bit vector, linked list); Disk scheduling: FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK; Disk formatting, boot block, bad blocks."}],"textBooks":["Abraham Silberschatz, Peter Baer Galvin & Greg Gagne, 'Operating System Concepts', 10th Edition, Wiley.","William Stallings, 'Operating Systems: Internals and Design Principles', 9th Edition, Pearson."],"referenceBooks":["Andrew S. Tanenbaum & Herbert Bos, 'Modern Operating Systems', 4th Edition, Pearson."]}

subject.name: Computer Organization and Architecture
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To impart fundamental concepts of CPU design, register transfer language, arithmetic circuits, pipelining, and memory hierarchies."],"outcomes":["Understand register transfer logic, common bus architectures, and micro-operations.","Design hardwired and microprogrammed control units and understand pipeline hazards.","Analyze cache memory mapping techniques and I/O organization with DMA."],"modules":[{"title":"UNIT -I: Register Transfer & Basic Computer Organization","topics":"Register Transfer Language; Bus and Memory transfers: Three-state bus buffers; Arithmetic, logic, and shift micro-operations; Computer registers, computer instructions, instruction cycle (fetch, decode, execute); Register-reference, memory-reference, and input-output instructions; Design of basic computer."},{"title":"UNIT -II: Central Processing Unit & Control Unit Design","topics":"General register organization, stack organization, instruction formats (three-address, two-address, one-address, zero-address); Addressing modes: Immediate, direct, indirect, register, register indirect, displacement; Data transfer and manipulation instructions; Program control; Control memory, address sequencing; Microprogram sequencer; Hardwired vs. Microprogrammed control."},{"title":"UNIT -III: Computer Arithmetic","topics":"Addition and subtraction of signed magnitude numbers and 2's complement; Multiplication algorithms: Hardware implementation, Booth's multiplication algorithm; Division algorithms: Restoring and non-restoring division; Floating-point arithmetic operations (IEEE 754 standard: single and double precision formats)."},{"title":"UNIT -IV: Pipelining & Vector Processing","topics":"Parallel processing, Flynn's classification; Pipelining: Linear pipeline processor, arithmetic pipeline, instruction pipeline; Pipeline hazards: Structural, data (RAW, WAR, WAW), and branch hazards; Hazard mitigation (forwarding, branch prediction, delayed branch); RISC vs. CISC architectures; Introduction to vector processing and array processors."},{"title":"UNIT -V: Memory Organization & Input-Output Organization","topics":"Memory hierarchy; Main memory (RAM and ROM chips), memory address map; Auxiliary memory; Associative memory; Cache memory: Locality of reference, mapping functions (direct, associative, set-associative), cache write policies (write-through, write-back), cache replacement algorithms; Virtual memory; I/O interface, asynchronous data transfer (strobe, handshaking); Modes of transfer: Programmed I/O, Interrupt-driven I/O, Direct Memory Access (DMA); Priority interrupt (daisy chaining)."}],"textBooks":["M. Morris Mano, 'Computer System Architecture', 3rd Edition, Pearson.","William Stallings, 'Computer Organization and Architecture', 10th Edition, Pearson."],"referenceBooks":["David A. Patterson & John L. Hennessy, 'Computer Organization and Design: The Hardware/Software Interface', Morgan Kaufmann."]}

subject.name: Computer Networks
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce layered network architectures (OSI and TCP/IP), physical transmission, data link protocols, IP routing, transport protocols, and application layer protocols."],"outcomes":["Compare OSI and TCP/IP protocol stacks and analyze packet encapsulation.","Implement error detection (CRC) and flow control (Sliding Window) protocols.","Calculate IPv4/IPv6 subnetting and analyze routing algorithms (OSPF, BGP, RIP)."],"modules":[{"title":"UNIT -I: Introduction & Physical Layer","topics":"Data communication components, networks, topologies (mesh, star, bus, ring); Network categories (LAN, MAN, WAN); Protocol suites: OSI 7-layer model vs. TCP/IP model; Physical layer: Transmission media (guided: twisted pair, coaxial, optical fiber; unguided: radio, microwave, infrared); Data encoding and modulation; Switching techniques: Circuit switching, message switching, packet switching (datagram vs. virtual circuit)."},{"title":"UNIT -II: Data Link Layer & Medium Access Control","topics":"Data link layer design issues: Framing, error control, flow control; Error detection and correction: Parity, Checksum, Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC), Hamming codes; Elementary flow control protocols: Stop-and-Wait; Sliding window protocols: Go-Back-N, Selective Repeat; Medium Access Control (MAC): Random access (ALOHA, Slotted ALOHA, CSMA, CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA); Controlled access; IEEE 802.3 Ethernet, IEEE 802.11 Wireless LAN; MAC addressing and switches."},{"title":"UNIT -III: Network Layer","topics":"Network layer functions; Logical addressing: IPv4 addressing (classful, classless CIDR, subnetting, supernetting), IPv6 addressing and migration; Address resolution: ARP, RARP; Internet Control protocols: ICMP, IGMP; Routing algorithms: Optimality principle, Distance Vector routing (RIP) and count-to-infinity problem, Link State routing (OSPF), Path Vector routing (BGP); Routers and NAT (Network Address Translation)."},{"title":"UNIT -IV: Transport Layer","topics":"Transport layer services and multiplexing/demultiplexing; Port numbers; User Datagram Protocol (UDP): Segment structure, checksum; Transmission Control Protocol (TCP): Segment header, connection management (3-way handshake, teardown); TCP Reliable data transfer; Flow control (sliding window buffer management); Congestion control: AIMD, slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit, fast recovery."},{"title":"UNIT -V: Application Layer & Network Security Basics","topics":"Domain Name System (DNS): Hierarchical namespace, resource records, name servers; World Wide Web and HTTP/HTTPS: Persistent and non-persistent connections, cookies, web caching; Electronic Mail: SMTP, POP3, IMAP; File transfer: FTP; Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP); Network management: SNMP; Introduction to network security: Cryptographic tools, SSL/TLS, firewalls, and VPNs."}],"textBooks":["Andrew S. Tanenbaum & David J. Wetherall, 'Computer Networks', 5th Edition, Pearson.","James F. Kurose & Keith W. Ross, 'Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach', 7th Edition, Pearson."],"referenceBooks":["Behrouz A. Forouzan, 'Data Communications and Networking', 5th Edition, McGraw Hill."]}

subject.name: Information Security
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To help students understand foundational concepts of information security.","To make it possible for students to appreciate the need for securing information from threats and risks.","To facilitate students to gain knowledge on how network infrastructure and connectivity can be secured."],"outcomes":["Explain basic concepts and importance of information security.","Identify threats to information security, analyse their impact and propose suitable countermeasures.","Describe various aspects of securing network infrastructure and importance of classifying information."],"modules":[{"title":"UNIT- I: Introduction to Information Security","topics":"Overview of Information security, Threats, Type of Vulnerabilities and Risk, Business Requirements, Information Security Definitions – Security Policies – Tier 1 (origination Level), Tier 2 (Functional Level), Tier 3 (Application or Device Level), Procedures, Standards, Guidance. Role of Governance in Information Security, Develop a Risk Management Program, Risk Management Process, Best Practices for IT Governance, Case study."},{"title":"UNIT- II: Information Asset Classification","topics":"Classification of Information, Information Assets – Owner, Custodian, User, Information Classification in terms of Secret, Confidential, Private and Public, Declassification. Retention and Disposal of Information Assets. Provide Authorization for Access – Owner, Custodian and User, Case study."},{"title":"UNIT- III: Access Control","topics":"User Identity and Access Management- Account Authorization, Access and Privilege Management, System and Network Access Control. Operating Systems Access Controls, Monitoring Systems Access Controls, Intrusion Detection System, Event logging, Cryptography. Physical Security: Identify Assets to be Protected, Perimeter Security, Firewalls, Prevention and Detection Systems, Safe Disposal of Physical Assets. Email Security: PGP, MIME, IP Security: IP security overview, Case study."},{"title":"UNIT- IV: Introduction to Cryptography","topics":"Introduction to Advanced Cryptography and Cryptanalysis, Classical Encryption Techniques – Substitution Techniques, Transposition Techniques, Permutation Method. Advanced Encryption Techniques and Security Issues – RC4, One-time Pad, RSA, DES, Triple DES, AES and Diffie Hellman, Case study."},{"title":"UNIT- V: Conventional Encryption","topics":"Confidentiality using conventional encryption – Placement of Encryption, Traffic Confidentiality, Key Distribution and Random Number Generation. Key management – Generating Keys, Nonlinear Keyspaces, Transferring Keys, Verifying Keys, Using Keys, Updating Keys, Storing keys, Backup keys, Compromised Keys, Lifetime of Keys, Destroying Keys and Public-Key Management, Case study."}],"textBooks":["Mark Stamp's Information Security: Principles and Practice (WIND), Deven N. Shah, Wiley (2009).","Cryptography and Information Security by V. K. Pachghare, Prentice-Hall of India, 2nd Revised edition (2015).","Cryptography and Network Security Principles and Practices, by William Stallings, Pearson Education; 7th edition (2017)."],"referenceBooks":["Applied Cryptanalysis – Breaking Ciphers in the Real World, Stamp, Richard M.Low.","Serious Cryptography: A Practical Introduction to Modern Encryption by Jean-Philippe Aumasson."]}

subject.name: Storage and Datacenter
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To impart the basic concepts of Storage systems and Datacenter environment.","To understand concepts about RAID techniques.","To understand basic concepts about NAS and SAN.","To understand about taking backup and restoring data with Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery concepts and tools.","To understand about Data Center Consolidation and Clustering."],"outcomes":["Describe storage architectures, direct attached storage, and RAID performance impacts.","Configure and contrast Network Attached Storage (NAS), Fibre Channel SAN, and IP-SAN/iSCSI.","Plan business continuity, backup deduplication, data center consolidation phases, and high-availability server clusters."],"modules":[{"title":"UNIT- I: Introduction to Storage System","topics":"Introduction to Information Storage: Information Storage, Evolution of Storage Architecture, Data Center Infrastructure, Virtualization and Cloud Computing. Fibre Channel Storage Area Networks: Fibre Channel Overview, The SAN and Its Evolution, Components of FC SAN, FC Connectivity, Switched Fabric Ports, Fibre Channel Architecture, Fabric Services, Switched Fabric Login Types, Zoning, FC SAN Topologies, Virtualization in SAN. IP SAN and FCoE: iSCSI, FCIP, FCoE."},{"title":"UNIT- III: Backup and Disaster Recovery","topics":"Introduction to Business Continuity: Information Availability, BC Terminology, BC Planning Life Cycle, Failure Analysis, Business Impact Analysis, BC Technology Solutions. Backup and Archive: Backup Purpose, Backup Considerations, Backup Granularity, Recovery Considerations, Backup Methods, Backup Architecture, Backup and Restore Operations, Backup Topologies, Backup in NAS Environments, Backup Targets, Data Deduplication for Backup, Backup in Virtualized Environments, Data Archive, Archiving Solution Architecture."},{"title":"UNIT- IV: Data Center Consolidation","topics":"Reasons for Data Center Consolidation: Consolidation Opportunities. subject.name: Machine Learning
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement machine learning algorithms, regularizations, ensemble models, and model evaluation techniques."],"outcomes":["Build predictive classification and regression models using scikit-learn.","Implement Decision Trees, Random Forests, Support Vector Machines, and Gradient Boosting.","Evaluate model performance, prevent overfitting, and perform hyperparameter tuning."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Foundations of Machine Learning","topics":"Overview of Machine Learning; Supervised, Unsupervised, Semi-supervised, and Reinforcement Learning; Machine learning pipeline: Data ingestion, feature engineering, train-test split, validation; Overfitting, underfitting, bias-variance tradeoff; Cross-validation techniques (K-Fold, Stratified K-Fold)."},{"title":"Unit 2: Linear & Logistic Models","topics":"Linear regression: Cost function, Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Gradient Descent (batch, stochastic, mini-batch); Ridge (L2) and Lasso (L1) regularization; Logistic regression for binary and multi-class classification (One-vs-Rest, Softmax); Maximum likelihood estimation."},{"title":"Unit 3: Tree Models & Ensemble Learning","topics":"Decision Trees: Information Gain, Entropy, Gini Impurity, CART algorithm; Mitchell, 'Machine Learning', McGraw Hill."],"referenceBooks":["Christopher M. Bishop, 'Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning', Springer."]}

subject.name: Design and Analysis of Algorithms Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To implement algorithmic design paradigms (Divide & Conquer, Greedy, Dynamic Programming, Backtracking) in C/C++."],"outcomes":["Implement and benchmark algorithmic runtime efficiency across varying dataset sizes."],"labExperiments":["Implementation and comparative empirical analysis of Merge Sort and Quick Sort.","Implementation of Strassen's Matrix Multiplication using Divide and Conquer.","Implementation of Fractional Knapsack problem using Greedy method.","Implementation of Minimum Cost Spanning Tree using Prim's algorithm and Kruskal's algorithm.","Implementation of Dijkstra's Single Source Shortest Path algorithm.","Implementation of 0/1 Knapsack problem using Dynamic Programming.","Implementation of Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) using Dynamic Programming.","Implementation of All-Pairs Shortest Path using Floyd-Warshall algorithm.","Implementation of N-Queens problem using Backtracking."]}

subject.name: Employability Skills
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To hone quantitative aptitude, logical reasoning, verbal ability, and corporate placement readiness."],"outcomes":["Solve recruitment aptitude evaluations and demonstrate professional group discussion capability."],"labExperiments":["Quantitative Aptitude: Numbers, percentages, profit and loss, ratio and proportions, time and work, time-speed-distance.","Logical Reasoning: Blood relations, seating arrangement, syllogisms, coding-decoding, series completion.","Verbal Ability: Reading comprehension, sentence correction, para-jumbles, critical reasoning.","Aptitude Mock Tests: Timed computerized test simulations covering industry recruitment patterns.","Technical Group Discussion and HR Interview simulation."]}

subject.name: Computer Networks Lab

subject.name: Operating System Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To practice Linux shell scripting, system calls, process scheduling, and page replacement simulation."],"outcomes":["Write bash scripts, utilize fork/exec system calls, and simulate OS memory/CPU scheduling algorithms."],"labExperiments":["Linux Shell Programming: Writing scripts with conditionals, loops, functions, and pattern matching (grep, sed, awk).","Process Creation: Writing C programs utilizing fork(), exec(), wait(), and exit() system calls.","Simulation of CPU Scheduling Algorithms: FCFS, SJF, Priority, and Round Robin.","Implementation of Inter-Process Communication (IPC) using Pipes and Shared Memory in C.","Simulating Process Synchronization: Producer-Consumer problem using Semaphores and Pthreads.","Implementation of Banker's Algorithm for Deadlock Avoidance.","Simulation of Page Replacement Algorithms: FIFO, LRU, and Optimal."]}

subject.name: Theory of Computation
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce formal languages, automata theory, computability, Turing machines, and undecidability."],"outcomes":["Construct DFA, NFA, and regular expressions for formal regular languages.","Design Context-Free Grammars and Pushdown Automata (PDA).","Design Turing Machines and analyze undecidable problems using halting problem and Rice's theorem."],"modules":[{"title":"MODULE -I: Regular Languages & Finite Automata","topics":"Alphabets, Strings and Languages; Deterministic finite Automata (DFA), State transition graph, Transition table, Language of DFA; Nondeterministic finite Automata (NFA), NFA with epsilon transition, Equivalence of NFA and DFA; Minimization of Finite Automata; Regular expressions (RE): Definition, Operators and precedence, Algebraic laws; Kleene's Theorem; RE to FA and DFA to RE (Arden's Theorem); Non-Regular Languages, Pumping Lemma for regular Languages and applications; Closure and Decision properties of Regular Languages; Moore and Mealy machines, Equivalence of Moore and Mealy machines."},{"title":"MODULE- II: Context Free Grammars & Pushdown Automata","topics":"Context Free Grammar (CFG) and Context Free Languages (CFL): Derivations, Derivation trees, Ambiguity in Grammar, Simplification of CFGs, Normal forms (Chomsky Normal Form - CNF, Greibach Normal Form - GNF); Variants of Turing Machine, TM as computer of integer functions; Universal Turing Machine; Church-Turing Thesis; Recursive and recursively enumerable languages; Halting problem; Introduction to Undecidability, Rice's theorem, Post Correspondence Problem (PCP), Modified PCP; Introduction to recursive function theory."}],"textBooks":["K.L.P. Mishra and N. Chandrasekaran, 'Theory of Computer Science: Automata, Languages and Computation', PHI.","John E. Hopcroft, Rajeev Motwani & Jeffrey D. Ullman, 'Introduction to Automata Theory, Languages and Computation', Pearson.","Peter Linz, 'An Introduction to Formal Languages and Automata', Narosa."],"referenceBooks":["C. Papadimitriou & C.L. Lewis, 'Elements of the Theory of Computation', PHI.","Michael Sipser, 'Introduction to the Theory of Computation', Cengage Learning."]}

subject.name: Cloud Computing

subject.name: Network Security

subject.name: Principles of Virtualization
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To provide insights into cloud virtualization architectures, hypervisors, enterprise data center optimization, and cloud migration frameworks."],"outcomes":["Differentiate full virtualization, para-virtualization, and desktop/storage/network virtualization.","Understand hypervisor technologies and Microsoft/VMware enterprise virtualization solutions.","Apply the 7-step model of migration to transition enterprise workloads into cloud platforms."],"modules":[{"title":"MODULE-I: Introduction to Virtualization","topics":"Virtualization and cloud computing; Need for virtualization: Cost, administration, rapid deployment, reduced infrastructure overhead, limitations; Types of hardware virtualization: Full virtualization, Partial virtualization, Para-virtualization; Desktop virtualization, Software virtualization, Memory virtualization, Storage virtualization, Data virtualization, Network virtualization."},{"title":"MODULE-II: Hypervisors & Virtualization Solutions","topics":"Server Virtualization: Types of server virtualization, Virtual machine basics, Types of virtual machines, Hypervisor concepts (Type-1 bare-metal, Type-2 hosted); Virtualization Solutions: Microsoft Virtualization solutions, Microsoft Infrastructure Optimization Model, Datacenter virtualization benefits, Client virtualization, Cloud virtualization integration."},{"title":"MODULE-III: Migrating into the Cloud","topics":"Challenges while migrating to Cloud; Broad approaches to cloud migration; Deciding on cloud migration; The Seven-Step Model of Migration into a Cloud; Migration risks and mitigation strategies; Enterprise cloud computing paradigm; Deployment models for enterprise cloud computing; Adoption and consumption strategies."}],"textBooks":["David Marshall & Wade A. Velte, Toby J. Velte & Robert Elsenpeter, 'Cloud Computing: A Practical Approach', Tata McGraw Hill."]}

subject.name: Humanities II / Managerial Economics

Koutsoyiannis, 'Modern Microeconomics', Macmillan / ELBS.","Maheshwari, 'Managerial Economics', Sultan Chand & Sons."]}

subject.name: Security Architecture
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To teach cloud security architectures, risk governance, cloud data protection, private cloud criteria, and operational defense-in-depth."],"outcomes":["Design cloud reference architectures incorporating defense-in-depth security controls.","Formulate encryption and data classification strategies for multitenant cloud environments.","Evaluate CSP compliance, security audit checklists, and incident response operations."],"modules":[{"title":"MODULE-I: Cloud Security Foundations & Architecture","topics":"Understanding Cloud Computing: The IT Foundation for Cloud, Overview of Security Architecture; Cloud Reference Architecture: Control over Security in Cloud Models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS); Cloud Deployment Models; Key real-world enterprise examples."},{"title":"MODULE-II: Risk Concerns & Architectural Elements","topics":"Cloud Computing Security Concerns: Risk tolerance, Legal and regulatory issues; Security Requirements for Cloud Architecture: Security patterns, Architectural building blocks, Cloud security architecture design, Key strategies for secure operation."},{"title":"MODULE-III: Data Security in Cloud Computing","topics":"Common risks with cloud data security; Data Encryption: Applications, limitations, and key management; Sensitive data categorization; Cloud Data Storage: The 'Roach Motel' syndrome; Effectively managing cloud risk; Overview of security controls and their operational boundaries; Security monitoring best practices."},{"title":"MODULE-IV: Private Clouds & Cloud Service Provider Selection","topics":"Private Clouds: Motivation and overview, Security implications of shared vs. dedicated resources; Bootstrapping secure operations: Business continuity, backup and recovery, Change management in operational environments, Vulnerability and penetration testing, Real-time security response."}],"textBooks":["Vic (J.R.) Winkler, 'Securing the Cloud: Cloud Computer Security Techniques and Tactics', Syngress / Elsevier (2011)."],"referenceBooks":["Sushil Jajodia & Krishna Kant, 'Secure Cloud Computing', Springer / Elsevier (2014).","Curtis Franklin Jr. & Brian J.S. Chee, 'Securing the Cloud: Security Strategies for the Ubiquitous Data Center', CRC Press (2019)."]}

subject.name: Database Security
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce database access control models, statistical database inference, secure DBMS design, and multi-level secure database systems."],"outcomes":["Evaluate Access Matrix, Bell-LaPadula, Biba, and Sea View database security models.","Implement user authentication, inference controls, and database intrusion detection systems.","Design multi-level security policies for object-oriented and frame-based database architectures."],"modules":[{"title":"MODULE-I: Database Security Problems & Models","topics":"Security problems in databases; Security controls overview; Access Matrix Model, Take-Grant Model, Acten Model, PN Model; Hartson and Hsiao's Model; Fernandez's Model; Bussolati and Martella's Model for distributed databases."},{"title":"MODULE-II: Mandatory Access Control Models & Security Mechanisms","topics":"Security Models: Bell and LaPadula's Model, Biba's Integrity Model, Dion's Model, Sea View Model, Jajodia and Sandhu's Model, Lattice Model for flow control; Security Mechanisms: User identification/authentication, Memory protection, Resource protection, Control flow mechanisms, Operating system isolation, TCSEC evaluation."},{"title":"MODULE-III: Secure Database Design & Intrusion Detection","topics":"Methodological approach to security software design; Secure OS and Secure DBMS design; Statistical Database Protection: Statistical attacks, Inference controls, Comparison criteria; Database Intrusion Detection Systems: IDES system, RETISS system, ASES system, Discovery."},{"title":"MODULE-IV: Private Cloud Database Considerations","topics":"Security implications of shared vs. dedicated database servers in private clouds; Network and storage segregation for private cloud databases; Regulatory compliance (HIPAA, PCI-DSS) in cloud database storage; Risk assurance."},{"title":"MODULE-V: Protection of Advanced Database Systems","topics":"Models for the protection of next-generation database systems: Protection of Frame-Based Systems; Protection of Object-Oriented Database Systems; SORION model for Object-Oriented databases."}],"textBooks":["Hassan A. Afyouni, 'Database Security and Auditing', Cengage Learning (2009).","Silvana Castano et al., 'Database Security', Pearson Education."],"referenceBooks":["Alfred Basta & Melissa Zgola, 'Database Security', Cengage Learning."]}

subject.name: Deep Learning
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To teach neural network foundations, backpropagation, deep learning architectures (CNN, RNN, LSTM), and deployment with TensorFlow/PyTorch."],"outcomes":["Design and train Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) with activation functions and optimizers.","Build Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for computer vision tasks.","Implement Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and LSTMs for sequential data and natural language."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Neural Networks Foundations","topics":"Biological neuron vs. Artificial neuron (Perceptron); Activation functions: Sigmoid, Tanh, ReLU, Leaky ReLU, Softmax; Feedforward neural networks; Loss functions: MSE, Binary Cross-Entropy, Categorical Cross-Entropy; Backpropagation algorithm and gradient computation; Optimization algorithms: SGD, Momentum, RMSprop, Adam."},{"title":"Unit 2: Training Deep Networks & Regularization","topics":"Vanishing and exploding gradient problems; Weight initialization (Xavier, He initialization); Regularization techniques: L1/L2 regularization, Dropout, Batch Normalization, Early Stopping; Hyperparameter tuning (learning rate scheduling, batch size)."},{"title":"Unit 3: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)","topics":"Convolution operation, filters/kernels, stride, padding (valid, same); Vanilla RNN and unrolling through time; Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT); Exploding/vanishing gradients in RNN; Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks: Forget, Input, Output gates; Gated Recurrent Units (GRU); Bidirectional RNNs."},{"title":"Unit 5: Modern Deep Architectures & Generative Models","topics":"Introduction to Attention Mechanism and Transformer concept; Autoencoders: Architecture, latent representations, denoising autoencoders; Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs): Generator and Discriminator game; Practical deployment using PyTorch and TensorFlow."}],"textBooks":["Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio & Aaron Courville, 'Deep Learning', MIT Press.","François Chollet, 'Deep Learning with Python', 2nd Edition, Manning Publications."],"referenceBooks":["Aurélien Géron, 'Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow', O'Reilly."]}

subject.name: Network Security Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To practice practical network security defenses, VPNs, VLAN isolation, firewall rules, and virtualization sandboxing."],"outcomes":["Configure Type-2 virtualization, ESXi bare-metal hypervisors, VLANs, and encrypted VPN tunnels.","Implement secure file sharing and remote desktop virtualization protocols."],"labExperiments":["Create Type-2 virtualization in VMware / VirtualBox: Allocate CPU, memory, and storage, and install Guest OS.","Adding and configuring dynamic virtual disks, managing virtual disk expansion and shrinkage.","Creating, managing, configuring, and scheduling VM snapshots.","Creating Spanned, Mirrored, and Striped volumes across virtual disks.","Configuring secure data transfer and folder sharing between isolated virtual machines.","Desktop Virtualization using VNC and Chrome Remote Desktop.","Configuring VMware ESXi 6.5 server on bare metal / hypervisor.","Accessing ESXi server from remote vSphere client and provisioning virtual machines.","Configuring VLANs in Cisco Packet Tracer to enforce network segmentation.","Installing and configuring KVM (Kernel-based Virtual Machine) in Linux.","Setting up an encrypted VPN tunnel between two virtual machines for secure transmission.","Creating Nested Virtual Machines (VM running inside another VM)."]}

subject.name: Principle of Virtualization Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To master hypervisor installation, virtual network configuration, live VM migration, and resource optimization."],"outcomes":["Deploy bare-metal hypervisors, configure vSwitches, and execute live virtual machine migration."],"labExperiments":["Installation and configuration of Type-1 Hypervisor (VMware ESXi / Proxmox VE).","Configuring virtual switches (vSwitch), port groups, and VLAN tagging in hypervisor environment.","Configuring shared storage (NFS / iSCSI) for virtualization cluster.","Performing Live Migration (vMotion) of virtual machines with zero downtime.","Configuring High Availability (HA) and Distributed Resource Scheduler (DRS) on hypervisor cluster.","Automating VM provisioning using command-line tools (virsh, Vagrant).","Benchmarking virtualized CPU, memory, and I/O performance against physical host."]}

subject.name: Summer Project Seminar-II
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To evaluate intermediate industrial training / summer project internship undertaken at the end of Year II."],"outcomes":["Defend technical architecture, project implementation, and software engineering deliverables before faculty committee."],"labExperiments":["Submission of comprehensive industrial internship project report and completion certificate.","Oral presentation of system architecture, technology stack, and implementation methodology.","Live software demonstration of modules and test cases developed during industrial training.","Comprehensive viva-voce examination assessing industry engineering competence."]}

subject.name: Artificial Intelligence
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce intelligent agents, informed and uninformed search strategies, knowledge representation, probabilistic reasoning, and pattern recognition."],"outcomes":["Formulate problem solving through state-space search (BFS, DFS, A*, Minimax, Alpha-Beta).","Represent domain knowledge using First-Order Logic and inference mechanisms.","Apply Bayesian reasoning, Markov models, and machine learning classifiers to intelligent systems."],"modules":[{"title":"MODULE-I: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence","topics":"Foundations and history of AI; Uninformed search: Breadth-First Search, Depth-First Search, Uniform-Cost Search, Iterative Deepening; Informed (Heuristic) search: Greedy best-first search, A* search, Heuristic admissibility; Local search: Hill-climbing, Simulated Annealing, Genetic Algorithms; Nair, 'Artificial Intelligence', 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill."],"referenceBooks":["Dan W. Patterson, 'Introduction to Artificial Intelligence and Expert Systems', PHI."]}

subject.name: Linux Administration
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To teach Linux system architecture, command-line operations, package management, disk/storage configuration, and secure user administration."],"outcomes":["Execute advanced bash shell commands, pipes, redirections, and vi editor operations.","Manage software repositories, mount filesystems, and configure Logical Volume Management (LVM).","Enforce user security permissions, Access Control Lists (ACLs), and disk quotas."],"modules":[{"title":"MODULE-I: Linux Command Line & File System","topics":"Linux filesystem hierarchy; The Shell, Linux utilities, Command line navigation; Root user vs. standard user; Managing Bash with key sequences; File system tasks: Working with directories, viewing text files, finding files (find, locate), piping and redirection; Vi/Vim editor modes, commands, editing; Getting help: man pages and info."},{"title":"MODULE-II: System & Software Administration","topics":"Software repositories and package databases; Package management: using apt, dpkg, rpm, yum; subject.name: Ethical Hacking
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce ethical penetration testing methodologies, footprinting, network scanning, system exploitation, web application attacks, and wireless hacking."],"outcomes":["Understand penetration testing phases: Reconnaissance, Scanning, Gaining Access, Maintaining Access, Covering Tracks.","Perform vulnerability scanning, OS fingerprinting, and exploitation using Kali Linux tools.","Identify and mitigate web application vulnerabilities (SQL Injection, XSS, CSRF) and wireless threats."],"modules":[{"title":"MODULE-I: Cyber Ethical Hacking Foundations","topics":"Introduction to Cyber Ethical Hacking; Simpson, Kent Backman & James E. Corley, 'Hands-On Ethical Hacking and Network Defense', Cengage Learning."],"referenceBooks":["Jon Erickson, 'Hacking: The Art of Exploitation', 2nd Edition, No Starch Press.","Dafydd Stuttard & Marcus Pinto, 'The Web Application Hacker's Handbook', Wiley."]}

subject.name: Cloud Scripting using PaaS

subject.name: Incident Response Management
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To teach Computer Security Incident Response Management (CSIRM), incident lifecycles, triage, containment, eradication, and forensic readiness."],"outcomes":["Differentiate between events, incidents, and crises in enterprise computing environments.","Implement the NIST Computer Security Incident Handling Guide lifecycle phases.","Formulate incident containment, eradication, evidence preservation, and post-incident review policies."],"modules":[{"title":"MODULE-I: Incident Response Foundations & CSIRM","topics":"Need for Computer Security Incident Response Management (CSIRM); Differences between an event, incident, and disaster; CSIRT organizational structures and charter; Incident response policies, plans, and team roles (triage, handling, escalation, forensics); Legal and regulatory reporting obligations."},{"title":"MODULE-II: Incident Handling Lifecycle","topics":"NIST SP 800-61 incident response lifecycle: Preparation, Detection & Analysis, Containment, Eradication & Recovery, Post-Incident Activity; Detection sources: SIEM alerts, IDS/IPS, anti-malware, user reports; Incident prioritization and severity scoring."},{"title":"MODULE-III: Containment, Eradication & Digital Forensics","topics":"Containment strategies: Short-term vs. long-term containment; Isolating compromised network segments; Preserving digital evidence and volatile memory; Eradication of malicious artifacts and backdoors; Secure system recovery and validation; Chain of custody."},{"title":"MODULE-IV: Post-Incident Lessons Learned & Continuous Improvement","topics":"Post-incident reviews (Lessons Learned meetings); Drafting incident closure reports; Updating defensive postures and security controls; Developing cyber incident tabletop exercises and disaster recovery drills."}],"textBooks":["Michael E. subject.name: UI/UX Fundamentals
