subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To explore advanced AI paradigms including Natural Language Processing, Transformer architectures, Generative AI, computer vision, and autonomous agent frameworks."],"outcomes":["Understand attention mechanisms, self-attention, and large language model architectures.","Implement modern Computer Vision pipelines (YOLO, object detection, segmentation).","Design autonomous agent workflows and understand AI ethics and alignment."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Natural Language Processing & Word Embeddings","topics":"Text preprocessing, tokenization, stemming, lemmatization; N-gram language models; Vector space representations: Bag-of-Words, TF-IDF; Word embeddings: Word2Vec (Skip-gram, CBOW), GloVe, FastText; Subword tokenization (BPE)."},{"title":"Unit 2: Transformer Architectures & Attention","topics":"Limitations of RNNs/LSTMs; Transformer architecture: Scaled dot-product attention, Multi-head attention, Positional encoding, Feed-forward networks; Encoder-only (BERT), Decoder-only (GPT), and Encoder-Decoder (T5) models; Transfer learning in NLP."},{"title":"Unit 3: Large Language Models & Generative AI","topics":"Pre-training and fine-tuning paradigms; Instruction tuning and RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback); Prompt engineering, zero-shot and few-shot prompting; Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG); Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT, LoRA)."},{"title":"Unit 4: Advanced Computer Vision","topics":"Object detection: Two-stage (R-CNN, Fast R-CNN, Faster R-CNN) vs. Single-stage (YOLO, SSD) detectors; Image segmentation: Semantic (U-Net) and Instance (Mask R-CNN) segmentation; Vision Transformers (ViT) overview."},{"title":"Unit 5: Autonomous Agents & AI Ethics","topics":"ReAct prompting and autonomous agent frameworks (LangChain, AutoGen); Tool-using agents and API calling; Ethical AI: Fairness, bias mitigation, transparency, copyright, safety, and responsible AI alignment guidelines."}],"textBooks":["Dan Jurafsky & James H. Martin, 'Speech and Language Processing', 3rd Edition draft.","Aurélien Géron, 'Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow', O'Reilly."],"referenceBooks":["Stuart Russell, 'Human Compatible: Artificial Intelligence and the Problem of Control', Viking."]}

subject.name: Exploring Software as a Service (SaaS) Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To explore SaaS architectures, multitenancy design patterns, SaaS billing integration, OAuth2 identity, and SaaS web application deployment."],"outcomes":["Deploy and configure multitenant SaaS applications with customer tenant isolation.","Integrate OAuth2 / SAML single-sign-on (SSO) and RESTful API webhooks."],"labExperiments":["Study of multitenancy database design patterns (Shared Database / Shared Schema vs. Isolated Database per Tenant).","Deploying a sample multitenant SaaS application on cloud hosting.","Implementing sub-domain based tenant resolution (tenant.app.com) and data isolation.","Configuring OAuth2 / OpenID Connect authentication with Google and GitHub identity providers.","Integrating a subscription billing webhook gateway (Stripe / Razorpay API sandbox).","Configuring Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with granular tenant admin and member roles.","Monitoring SaaS API usage, rate-limiting with Redis, and tenant analytics dashboards."]}

subject.name: Linux Administration Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To configure enterprise Linux servers, manage partitions, bootloaders, network services, Apache, NFS, and Samba."],"outcomes":["Install and manage Red Hat / Ubuntu enterprise server distributions.","Configure DNS, DHCP, NFS, Samba, FTP, and Apache HTTP servers on Linux."],"labExperiments":["Installation of Red Hat / Enterprise Linux OS: Partitioning drives, configuring GRUB boot loader, setting time zones and network.","Package selection, installation, and repository management using dnf/apt.","Modifying GRUB configuration: Changing timeout, default kernel, and boot parameters.","Setting up and configuring Samba Server for seamless Linux-Windows cross-platform file sharing.","Configuring DHCP server and client on Linux subnet.","Configuring BIND DNS Server with forward and reverse lookup zones for a chosen domain.","Configuring NFS (Network File System) Server and mounting on remote client machines.","Setting up Linux as a proxy server with Squid.","Configuring Postfix/Dovecot Mail Server on Linux.","Configuring VSFTPD FTP Server and verifying secure file transfers.","Using GCC and G++ compilers for compilation and debugging in Linux.","Configuring and hardening Apache HTTP Web Server (virtual hosts, SSL certificates).","Linux System Administration: sudoers configuration, changing user identities, using administrative monitoring commands (top, htop, vmstat, iostat)."]}

subject.name: Ethical Hacking Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To practice ethical penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, network reconnaissance, and exploit simulations in an isolated lab environment."],"outcomes":["Execute penetration testing steps using Kali Linux tools (Nmap, Metasploit, Wireshark, Burp Suite).","Demonstrate vulnerability assessment, web exploitation, and system hardening."],"labExperiments":["Google Hacking & OSINT: Utilizing Google Dorks, Shodan, and Maltego for reconnaissance.","Network Scanning with Nmap: Identifying open ports, service versions, and OS fingerprinting.","Network Mapping and vulnerability assessment using Nessus / OpenVAS.","Gaining and Maintaining Access using Metasploit framework in vulnerable sandbox VM.","Password Hacking & Cracking: Performing dictionary and brute-force attacks using John the Ripper and Hashcat.","Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) simulation using ARP spoofing and packet sniffing.","Web Application Security Testing: Intercepting HTTP traffic, testing for SQL Injection and XSS using Burp Suite.","Denial of Service (DoS) attack simulation and analyzing traffic spike patterns.","Covering Tracks & Log Analysis: Examining authentication logs and discussing anti-forensics counters.","Configuring Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems (Snort / Suricata) with custom alert rules."]}

subject.name: Project-I
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To initiate the capstone project lifecycle: problem definition, literature review, software requirements specification (SRS), system design, and preliminary prototyping."],"outcomes":["Formulate an engineering problem in cloud computing or cyber security.","Produce an IEEE standard Software Requirements Specification (SRS) and architecture design document.","Present prototype proof-of-concept and defend milestone deliverables before project review panel."],"labExperiments":["Identification of real-world problem domain in Cloud Computing, Cloud Security, or IoT.","Literature review of research publications and existing commercial solutions.","Preparation of IEEE-compliant Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document.","System Architecture Design: High-level design (HLD), Low-level design (LLD), ER diagrams, UML class and sequence diagrams.","Cloud Infrastructure Planning: Selection of cloud providers, service tiers, database architectures, and tech stack.","Preliminary Proof of Concept (PoC) prototype implementation.","Project-I Progress Presentation and Viva-Voce examination."]}

subject.name: Cyber Forensics
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce digital evidence handling, file system forensics (FAT, NTFS, ext, APFS), forensic imaging, and anti-forensics countermeasures."],"outcomes":["Understand electronic crime types and legal chain-of-custody protocols.","Perform forensic disk imaging and recover deleted files from slack space.","Utilize digital forensic toolkits (Autopsy, FTK Imager, EnCase) for evidence analysis."],"modules":[{"title":"Module-I: Introduction to Digital Forensics & Cybercrime","topics":"Definition and types of cybercrimes; Electronic evidence and handling; Electronic media collection, searching, and seizure of digital storage devices; Introduction to internet crimes, hacking, cracking, financial and ATM frauds; Cryptography in forensics; Emerging digital crimes and investigative challenges."},{"title":"Module-II: File Systems & Operating System Artifacts","topics":"Definition and cardinal rules of digital forensics; Data acquisition and authentication process (MD5, SHA-256 hashes); Windows file systems: FAT12, FAT16, FAT32, NTFS (MFT, attributes); UNIX and Linux file systems (ext3/ext4, inodes); Mac file systems (HFS+, APFS); Computer artifacts, browser history, registry hives, Prefetch, LNK files; Forensic applications of OS artifacts."},{"title":"Module-III: Forensic Tools, Data Recovery & Anti-Forensics","topics":"Introduction to forensic tools; Understanding and extracting data from slack space; Tools for disk imaging (dd, FTK Imager); Data carving and file header analysis; Vulnerability assessment tools; EnCase and FTK suites; Anti-forensics techniques (data wiping, encryption, steganography) and countermeasures; Retrieving deleted data from desktops, laptops, and mobile devices; Damaged SIM card data recovery; Processing multimedia evidence."}],"textBooks":["Cory Altheide & Harlan Carvey, 'Digital Forensics with Open Source Tools', Syngress / Elsevier.","Bill Nelson, Amelia Phillips & Christopher Steuart, 'Guide to Computer Forensics and Investigations', Cengage Learning."],"referenceBooks":["Eoghan Casey, 'Digital Evidence and Computer Crime: Forensic Science, Computers and the Internet', Academic Press."]}

subject.name: Web Security and SDLC
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To teach web security vulnerabilities, OWASP Top 10, cross-origin security, browser exploitation, and Secure Software Development Life Cycle (S-SDLC)."],"outcomes":["Analyze web application vulnerabilities including XSS, SQLi, and parameter pollution.","Integrate threat modeling and security checkpoints across Waterfall, Agile, and DevOps SDLC models."],"modules":[{"title":"MODULE I: Web Fundamentals & Vulnerabilities","topics":"Introduction to web security and threat landscapes; Web basics: HTML, CSS, HTTP/HTTPS request-response cycles, Cookies, Sessions; Web application vulnerabilities and classification; Building secure web architectures; Detecting and defending against third-party tracking on the web."},{"title":"MODULE II: Web Network Attacks & Injection Flaws","topics":"Network attacks and HTTPS mechanisms; Cross-Domain communication (CORS, JSONP); Limitations of HTTPS; Cross-Site Scripting (XSS: Stored, Reflected, DOM-based); SQL Injection (in-band, blind, error-based); OS Command Injection; HTTP Header Injection; Automated discovery of parameter pollution vulnerabilities in web applications."},{"title":"MODULE III: Request Authorization & Secure SDLC Models","topics":"Request authorization flaws; Insecure web logic, business logic flaws; HTTP Parameter Tampering; Cookie flaws, Session Fixation, and server misconfiguration; Attacks on user interfaces (Clickjacking); Browser and device fingerprinting; User tracking flaws; Browser caching vulnerabilities; Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) models: Waterfall, Prototyping, Spiral, Evolutionary development, and Secure SDLC (DevSecOps) integration."}],"textBooks":["Dafydd Stuttard & Marcus Pinto, 'The Web Application Hacker's Handbook: Finding and Exploiting Security Flaws', 2nd Edition, Wiley.","Gary McGraw, 'Software Security: Building Security In', Addison-Wesley."],"referenceBooks":["OWASP Top 10 Web Application Security Risks Documentation."]}

subject.name: Cloud Security
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To explore core cloud security concepts, multi-tenancy isolation, virtualization-specific attacks, hyperjacking, and cloud compliance regulations."],"outcomes":["Explain defense-in-depth, least privilege, and cryptographic mechanisms across IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS.","Analyze virtualization threats including guest-hopping, hypervisor escape, and hyperjacking.","Assess legal compliance frameworks including PCI-DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, and CSA Security Guidance."],"modules":[{"title":"MODULE I: Cloud Security Concepts & Cryptography","topics":"Security Concepts: Confidentiality, privacy, integrity, authentication, non-repudiation, availability, access control, defense-in-depth, least privilege; Application of concepts in PaaS, IaaS, and SaaS; User authentication in cloud; Cryptographic systems: Symmetric cryptography, stream/block ciphers, modes of operation, public-key crypto, hashing, digital signatures, PKI, key management, X.509 certificates, OpenSSL."},{"title":"MODULE II: Multi-Tenancy & Virtualization Vulnerabilities","topics":"Multi-tenancy issues: Isolation of users/VMs from each other; Cloud provider responsibilities; Virtualization system security: ESX and ESXi security, ESX file system security, storage considerations, backup and recovery; Virtualization vulnerabilities: Management console, management server, administrative VM, guest VM, hypervisor vulnerabilities, hypervisor escape, configuration errors, botnets in clouds."},{"title":"MODULE III: Virtualization Attacks, Defense & Compliance","topics":"Virtualization System-Specific Attacks: Guest hopping, attacks on the VM (deletion, control hijacking, code/file injection into virtualized file structure), VM migration attack, hyperjacking; Technologies for Virtualization-Based Security: Virtual server protection, virtualization-based sandboxing, storage security (HIDPS, log management, Data Loss Prevention - DLP); Legal and Compliance Issues: Data ownership, right to penetration test, jurisdictional data residency laws, examination of modern standards (PCI-DSS, ISO 27017, SOC 2), Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) guidance."}],"textBooks":["Tim Mather, Subra Kumaraswamy & Shahed Latif, 'Cloud Security and Privacy: An Enterprise Perspective on Risks and Compliance', O'Reilly Media.","Ronald L. Krutz & Russell Dean Vines, 'Cloud Security: A Comprehensive Guide to Secure Cloud Computing', Wiley."],"referenceBooks":["Cloud Security Alliance (CSA), 'Security Guidance for Critical Areas of Focus in Cloud Computing'."]}

subject.name: Hybrid Cloud Computing
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce hybrid cloud integration, private-public cloud federation, hybrid networking (VPN/Direct Connect), and enterprise workload migration."],"outcomes":["Design hybrid cloud architectures connecting on-premises data centers to AWS/Azure.","Implement hybrid data synchronization, storage tiering, and cloud bursting strategies."],"modules":[{"title":"Module I: Hybrid Cloud Architecture & Drivers","topics":"Definition and business drivers for hybrid cloud; Comparison of public, private, and hybrid cloud models; NIST definition and deployment scenarios; Workload placement strategies; Latency, data sovereignty, and regulatory compliance considerations."},{"title":"Module II: Hybrid Networking & Connectivity","topics":"Connecting on-premises environments to cloud; Site-to-Site IPSec VPN tunnels; Dedicated private connections (AWS Direct Connect, Azure ExpressRoute); Hybrid DNS resolution; BGP routing and redundant failover paths."},{"title":"Module III: Hybrid Storage & Data Integration","topics":"Hybrid storage architectures; Cloud storage gateways (file, volume, tape gateways); Data replication and synchronization; Automated storage tiering (hot, cool, archive tiers); Disaster recovery to the cloud."},{"title":"Module IV: Hybrid Management & Workload Migration","topics":"Unified hybrid cloud management (AWS Outposts, Azure Stack, Google Anthos); Workload migration tools (AWS Application Migration Service, Azure Migrate); Cloud bursting architectures; Monitoring and cost management in hybrid environments."}],"textBooks":["Rajkumar Buyya, Christian Vecchiola & S. Thamarai Selvi, 'Mastering Cloud Computing', McGraw Hill.","Michael J. Kavis, 'Architecting the Cloud', Wiley."],"referenceBooks":["Thomas Erl et al., 'Cloud Computing: Concepts, Technology & Architecture', Prentice Hall."]}

subject.name: Cloud Web Services
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To teach RESTful web services, SOAP, XML/JSON parsing, API management, and cloud web service development with AWS and Azure."],"outcomes":["Design and document enterprise REST APIs using OpenAPI/Swagger specifications.","Deploy scalable web services with API gateways, caching, and rate limiting."],"modules":[{"title":"Module I: Web Services Foundations","topics":"Evolution of distributed computing; Service Oriented Architecture (SOA) principles; Web services architecture; XML, XSD, SOAP protocol; WSDL (Web Services Description Language); REST architectural style vs. SOAP."},{"title":"Module II: RESTful Web Services & API Design","topics":"REST design constraints: Statelessness, client-server, cacheability, uniform interface; HTTP verbs (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH) and status codes; Resource URI naming conventions; JSON data interchange; Designing REST APIs with Swagger / OpenAPI specifications."},{"title":"Module III: Cloud API Gateways & Security","topics":"Role of API Gateways in microservices; Request routing, authentication, authorization (JWT, OAuth2); Rate limiting, throttling, and traffic shaping; API caching with Amazon CloudFront and ElastiCache; Securing API endpoints with AWS WAF."},{"title":"Module IV: Serverless Web Services & Microservices","topics":"Building serverless web services using AWS API Gateway and AWS Lambda; Connecting serverless backends to Amazon DynamoDB and Aurora Serverless; Async event-driven communication using AWS SNS and SQS; Monitoring API metrics with AWS CloudWatch."}],"textBooks":["Leonard Richardson & Sam Ruby, 'RESTful Web Services', O'Reilly Media.","Thomas Erl, 'Service-Oriented Architecture: Concepts, Technology, and Design', Prentice Hall."],"referenceBooks":["Mark Masse, 'REST API Design Rulebook', O'Reilly Media."]}

subject.name: Cloud Computing Solutions
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To analyze enterprise cloud solution design, well-architected frameworks, high availability, fault tolerance, and cost optimization."],"outcomes":["Architect resilient enterprise cloud solutions meeting the 5 pillars of the Well-Architected Framework.","Formulate disaster recovery, auto-scaling, and multi-region deployment topologies."],"modules":[{"title":"Module I: Cloud Architecture Fundamentals","topics":"Cloud solution architecture principles; Understanding customer requirements; AWS Well-Architected Framework pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability."},{"title":"Module II: Designing Resilient & High-Availability Topologies","topics":"Multi-AZ and Multi-Region architectures; Global traffic management with Route 53 (latency, failover, geolocation routing); Auto-scaling groups and Elastic Load Balancers (ALB, NLB); Decoupling architectures with message queues."},{"title":"Module III: Cloud Data & Storage Solutions","topics":"Choosing appropriate database solutions (RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, Redshift); Data lake architectures on Amazon S3; Big data processing pipelines with AWS EMR and Athena; Backup and archival retention strategies with S3 Glacier."},{"title":"Module IV: Cloud Migration & Cost Governance","topics":"The 6 Rs of cloud migration (Rehost, Replatform, Repurchase, Refactor, Retire, Retain); Cloud financial management (FinOps): Cost allocation tags, AWS Cost Explorer, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans; Enterprise security governance."}],"textBooks":["Joe Baron et al., 'AWS Certified Solutions Architect Official Study Guide', Sybex / Wiley.","Michael J. Kavis, 'Architecting the Cloud', Wiley."],"referenceBooks":["AWS Well-Architected Framework Whitepapers."]}

subject.name: Cloud Architectural Patterns
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce distributed cloud design patterns: Circuit Breaker, CQRS, Event Sourcing, Strangler Fig, and Ambassador patterns."],"outcomes":["Apply cloud design patterns to overcome distributed computing challenges.","Design scalable, loosely-coupled microservice architectures using event-driven patterns."],"modules":[{"title":"Module I: Scalability Primer & Compute Patterns","topics":"Scalability primer: Horizontal vs. vertical scaling; Horizontally scaling compute patterns; Stateless vs. stateful services; Auto-scaling patterns; Load balancing algorithms; Health checking and self-healing patterns."},{"title":"Module II: Resiliency & Reliability Patterns","topics":"Circuit Breaker pattern; Retry pattern with exponential backoff; Bulkhead pattern for failure isolation; Compensating Transaction pattern; Health Endpoint Monitoring pattern."},{"title":"Module III: Data Management Patterns","topics":"Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS) pattern; Event Sourcing pattern; Saga pattern for distributed transactions (orchestration vs. choreography); Materialized View pattern; Sharding pattern."},{"title":"Module IV: Modernization & Gateway Patterns","topics":"Strangler Fig pattern for legacy application migration; Ambassador pattern; Sidecar pattern; Backends for Frontends (BFF) pattern; Gateway Aggregation and Offloading patterns."}],"textBooks":["Bill Wilder, 'Cloud Architecture Patterns: Using Microsoft Azure', O'Reilly Media.","Chris Richardson, 'Microservices Patterns: With Examples in Java', Manning Publications."],"referenceBooks":["Microsoft Azure Architecture Center: 'Cloud Design Patterns'."]}

subject.name: Automation and Configuration Management
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To teach Infrastructure as Code (IaC), Ansible, Terraform, AWS Systems Manager, and continuous configuration compliance."],"outcomes":["Write Ansible playbooks to automate server provisioning and application deployments.","Deploy cloud infrastructure using Terraform declarative configurations.","Manage enterprise server fleets with AWS Systems Manager."],"modules":[{"title":"Module I: AWS Systems Manager & Fleet Management","topics":"Introduction to AWS Systems Manager (SSM); Using SSM Run Command; State Manager; Inventory management; Patch Manager for automated OS updates; Parameter Store for centralized configuration."},{"title":"Module II: Configuration Management with Ansible","topics":"Ansible architecture: Agentless communication via SSH; Ansible inventory; Modules and ad-hoc commands; Writing Ansible Playbooks (YAML syntax); Tasks, handlers, variables, templates (Jinja2); Ansible Roles and Ansible Galaxy."},{"title":"Module III: Infrastructure as Code with Terraform","topics":"Terraform core concepts: Providers, resources, variables, outputs; HCL (HashiCorp Configuration Language); Terraform state management (remote state, locking with DynamoDB); Terraform modules; Planning, applying, and destroying cloud infrastructure."},{"title":"Module IV: Continuous Compliance & Policy as Code","topics":"Policy as Code concepts; AWS Config rules for compliance auditing; Automated remediation with Lambda; GitOps workflows; Infrastructure testing and security scanning."}],"textBooks":["Lorin Hochstein & René Moser, 'Ansible: Up and Running', O'Reilly Media.","Yevgeniy Brikman, 'Terraform: Up & Running: Writing Infrastructure as Code', O'Reilly Media."],"referenceBooks":["Michael Wittig & Andreas Wittig, 'Amazon Web Services in Action', Manning Publications."]}

subject.name: Infrastructure Containers
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To teach Linux container internals (namespaces, cgroups), Docker containerization, Kubernetes cluster orchestration, and container networking."],"outcomes":["Build, optimize, and secure Docker container images using multi-stage Dockerfiles.","Deploy and orchestrate microservices on Kubernetes using Pods, Deployments, and Services."],"modules":[{"title":"Module I: Container Foundations & Docker","topics":"Evolution from VMs to Containers; Linux kernel fundamentals: cgroups, namespaces, union file systems; Installing and configuring Docker; Docker architecture: Docker Daemon, Client, Registry; Docker images and Dockerfiles (multi-stage builds); Managing container lifecycles."},{"title":"Module II: Docker Storage & Networking","topics":"Docker storage drivers; Volumes, bind mounts, and tmpfs mounts; Docker networking: Bridge, host, overlay, and macvlan networks; Multi-container orchestration using Docker Compose; Docker Swarm basics."},{"title":"Module III: Kubernetes Architecture & Workloads","topics":"Kubernetes architecture: Master nodes (API Server, etcd, Scheduler, Controller Manager) and Worker nodes (Kubelet, Kube-Proxy, Container Runtime); Core objects: Pods, ReplicaSets, Deployments; Rolling updates, rollbacks; ConfigMaps and Secrets."},{"title":"Module IV: Kubernetes Networking, Storage & Cloud Services","topics":"Kubernetes Service types: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer; Ingress controllers; Persistent Volumes (PV), Persistent Volume Claims (PVC), StorageClasses; Managed Kubernetes services: Amazon EKS, Azure AKS, Google GKE."}],"textBooks":["Nigel Poulton, 'The Kubernetes Book', Nigel Poulton.","Karl Matthias & Sean P. Kane, 'Docker: Up & Running', O'Reilly Media."],"referenceBooks":["Brendan Burns, Joe Beda & Kelsey Hightower, 'Kubernetes: Up and Running', O'Reilly Media."]}

subject.name: Artificial Intelligence (Open Elective-II)
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To provide multidisciplinary engineering students with foundational knowledge of AI concepts, search strategies, knowledge graphs, and neural systems."],"outcomes":["Understand foundational AI principles, problem formulating agents, and state-space search.","Apply knowledge engineering and modern intelligent decision frameworks to diverse engineering domains."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit I: Introduction & Intelligent Agents","topics":"Introduction to Artificial Intelligence; History and milestones; Turing test; Intelligent agents: Structure, environments, agent types; Applications in robotics, healthcare, autonomous vehicles."},{"title":"Unit II: Problem Solving & Search Methods","topics":"Formulating problems as state-space search; Uninformed search (BFS, DFS, Uniform cost); Heuristic search (A* search, Greedy search); Adversarial search and game trees."},{"title":"Unit III: Knowledge Representation","topics":"Logic fundamentals; Propositional and predicate calculus; Ontologies and semantic networks; Rule-based expert systems; Handling uncertainty with fuzzy logic and Bayesian reasoning."},{"title":"Unit IV: Learning & Neural Networks","topics":"Machine learning paradigms; Perceptron model, multilayer feedforward neural networks; Backpropagation basics; Overview of Computer Vision and Natural Language Processing applications."}],"textBooks":["Stuart Russell & Peter Norvig, 'Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach', Pearson.","Elaine Rich & Kevin Knight, 'Artificial Intelligence', McGraw Hill."],"referenceBooks":["Dan W. Patterson, 'Introduction to Artificial Intelligence and Expert Systems', PHI."]}

subject.name: Big Data Analytics (Open Elective-II)
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To teach big data characteristics (5 Vs), Hadoop ecosystem, HDFS, MapReduce, Apache Spark, and big data analytical pipelines."],"outcomes":["Explain Big Data architectures and storage mechanisms across HDFS and NoSQL stores.","Write MapReduce and Spark jobs for distributed big data processing and streaming analytics."],"modules":[{"title":"UNIT I: Introduction to Big Data and Hadoop","topics":"Types of Digital Data: Structured, Semi-structured, Unstructured; Characteristics of Big Data (Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, Value); Distributed computing challenges; Hadoop architecture: HDFS (NameNode, DataNode, secondary NameNode), HDFS blocks and replication; Hadoop MapReduce execution model."},{"title":"UNIT II: Hadoop Ecosystem Components","topics":"Hadoop YARN architecture (ResourceManager, NodeManager); Apache Pig: Pig Latin, data types, execution modes; Apache Hive: Hive QL, tables, partitions, buckets; Data ingestion tools: Apache Sqoop (RDBMS to HDFS), Apache Flume (log streaming)."},{"title":"UNIT III: Distributed Processing with Apache Spark","topics":"Limitations of MapReduce; Introduction to Apache Spark; Resilient Distributed Datasets (RDDs): Transformations and Actions; Spark SQL: DataFrames and Datasets; Spark Streaming basics."},{"title":"UNIT IV: NoSQL Databases & Analytics","topics":"NoSQL data models: Key-Value (Redis), Document (MongoDB), Column-Family (HBase, Cassandra), Graph (Neo4j); CAP Theorem and BASE properties; Big Data machine learning with Spark MLlib."}],"textBooks":["Seema Acharya & Subhashini Chellappan, 'Big Data and Analytics', Wiley India.","Tom White, 'Hadoop: The Definitive Guide', 4th Edition, O'Reilly Media."],"referenceBooks":["Bill Chambers & Matei Zaharia, 'Spark: The Definitive Guide', O'Reilly Media."]}

subject.name: Data Science (Open Elective-II)
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce data science lifecycles, statistical exploration, machine learning model building, and data communication."],"outcomes":["Apply statistical data wrangling and visualization routines to derive business insights.","Build, tune, and evaluate machine learning predictive models."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit I: Introduction to Data Science","topics":"Evolution of data science; Data science lifecycle; The role of a data scientist; Types of data; Data collection and ethics; Exploratory data analysis in Python."},{"title":"Unit II: Statistical Inference & Modeling","topics":"Probability distributions; Sampling and Central Limit Theorem; Hypothesis testing; Linear regression; Logistic regression; Measuring performance (Precision, Recall, ROC curves)."},{"title":"Unit III: Machine Learning Algorithms","topics":"Supervised learning: Decision Trees, Random Forests, Support Vector Machines; Unsupervised learning: K-Means clustering, Principal Component Analysis (PCA)."},{"title":"Unit IV: Data Visualization & Communication","topics":"Principles of effective data storytelling; Visualizing with Matplotlib, Seaborn, and interactive dashboards; Communicating model results to non-technical stakeholders."}],"textBooks":["Jake VanderPlas, 'Python Data Science Handbook', O'Reilly Media.","Joel Grus, 'Data Science from Scratch: First Principles with Python', O'Reilly Media."],"referenceBooks":["Foster Provost & Tom Fawcett, 'Data Science for Business', O'Reilly Media."]}

subject.name: Economics for Engineers
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To provide engineering undergraduates with principles of economic decision making, engineering cost estimation, cash flow analysis, depreciation, and financial statements."],"outcomes":["Evaluate engineering projects using Present Worth, Annual Cash Flow, and Rate of Return methods.","Calculate asset depreciation (Straight-Line, Declining Balance) and perform replacement analysis.","Interpret corporate balance sheets, profit-loss statements, and inflation cost indexes."],"modules":[{"title":"MODULE -I: Economic Decisions, Costs & Cash Flows","topics":"Economic Decisions Making: Overview, Problems, Role, Decision making process; Engineering Costs & Estimation: Fixed, Variable, Marginal & Average Costs, Sunk Costs, Opportunity Costs, Recurring and Non-recurring Costs, Incremental Costs, Cash Costs vs. Book Costs, Life-Cycle Costs; Estimating models (Per-unit, Segmenting, Power-sizing, Learning curve); Cash Flow Diagrams: Time value of money, Nominal & Effective interest; Present Worth Analysis: End-of-year convention, effect of inflation/deflation, taxes, multiple alternatives."},{"title":"MODULE-II: Rate of Return & Uncertainty Analysis","topics":"Cash Flow & Rate of Return Analysis: Treatment of salvage value, Annual cash flow analysis; Internal Rate of Return (IRR), Incremental analysis, Benefit-Cost Ratio analysis; Sensitivity and Break-even analysis; Public sector economic analysis; Uncertainty in Future Events: Estimates range, Probability, Expected value, Economic decision trees, Simulation, Real options."},{"title":"MODULE-III: Depreciation, Replacement & Accounting","topics":"Depreciation: Deterioration & obsolescence, Straight-line depreciation, Declining balance depreciation, Tax regulations and capital allowances; Replacement Analysis: Minimum cost life of a new asset, Marginal cost; Inflation and Price Change: Composite vs. commodity indexes, Cash flows inflating at different rates; Financial Accounting: Balance sheet, Income statement, Financial ratios, Cost accounting, Direct and indirect costs allocation."}],"textBooks":["James L. Riggs, David D. Bedworth & Sabah U. Randhawa, 'Economics for Engineers', 4th Edition, Tata McGraw-Hill.","Donald G. Newnan, Ted G. Eschenbach & Jerome P. Lavelle, 'Engineering Economic Analysis', Oxford University Press."],"referenceBooks":["Sullivan, Wicks & Koelling, 'Engineering Economy', Pearson.","R. Paneerselvam, 'Engineering Economics', PHI."]}

subject.name: Cyber Forensics Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To practice physical evidence handling, disk imaging, forensic data carving, slack space recovery, and digital investigation workflows."],"outcomes":["Create bit-stream disk images and verify cryptographic hashes using FTK Imager and dd.","Extract deleted files, browser history, and USB registry artifacts using Autopsy."],"labExperiments":["Physical collection of electronic evidence and documenting chain of custody.","Creating forensic bit-stream disk image of a flash drive using FTK Imager and verifying MD5/SHA-256 hashes.","Data carving and recovering deleted images and documents using Autopsy and Foremost.","Analyzing slack space and unallocated clusters for hidden data fragments.","Windows Registry Forensics: Examining USBSTOR keys, UserAssist, and recently opened documents.","Web Browser Forensics: Extracting browsing history, cache, cookies, and download records.","Email Forensics: Analyzing raw RFC 822 email headers, routing IP hops, and identifying spoofed emails.","Network Forensics: Reconstructing transmitted files and HTTP sessions from Wireshark PCAP captures."]}

subject.name: Web Security and SDLC Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To apply Secure SDLC documentation, threat modeling, security test cases, cryptographic implementation, and intrusion detection."],"outcomes":["Produce Software Requirement Specification, threat models, and security test plans.","Implement classical/modern encryption algorithms and demonstrate IDS alerting using Snort."],"labExperiments":["Preparation of problem statement, Software Requirement Specification (SRS) with security requirements for a target project.","Preparation of Software Configuration Management (SCM) and Risk Management security documentation.","Threat Modeling: Performing application threat modeling using Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool (STRIDE methodology).","Design Phase Architecture Review using CASE tools.","Developing unit test cases and integration security test cases for authentication and authorization.","Performing White-box static analysis (SAST) and Black-box dynamic testing (DAST) on web application code.","Implementing Caesar Cipher and Rail Fence Row/Column Transposition Ciphers.","Implementing Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange mechanism using HTML and JavaScript.","Demonstrating Intrusion Detection System (IDS) alerts using Snort on test network traffic."]}

subject.name: Cloud Security Lab
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To analyze cloud service architectures, comparative vendor security features, cloud migration risks, and cost governance."],"outcomes":["Evaluate security controls across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud platforms.","Formulate cloud migration roadmaps and implement cost governance policies."],"labExperiments":["Study of basic cloud architecture models and representing them through enterprise case studies.","Comparative security research on SaaS, PaaS, and IaaS service providers.","Research and presentation on cloud vulnerabilities and obstacles at a generic enterprise level.","Analyzing security and identity services in Amazon Web Services (AWS IAM, Security Groups, KMS).","Analyzing security and identity services in Microsoft Azure (Entra ID, Azure Key Vault).","Analyzing security and identity services in Google Cloud Platform (Cloud IAM, Cloud KMS).","Cloud Cost Management: Configuring budgets, alerts, and cost allocation tags.","Legal and compliance case study on data sovereignty and cross-border cloud storage.","Designing an end-to-end cloud migration plan for an on-premises enterprise application.","Configuring AWS CloudTrail and CloudWatch alerts for unauthorized IAM policy alterations."]}

subject.name: Project-II
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To complete the core engineering implementation, deployment, testing, and performance validation of the capstone project initiated in Semester 6."],"outcomes":["Implement production-grade cloud computing / security architectures.","Execute comprehensive testing (functional, load, security) and deploy on cloud infrastructure.","Author formal project thesis and defend project results before university evaluation board."],"labExperiments":["Implementation of core project architecture, backend services, and cloud database storage.","Deployment on cloud infrastructure (AWS / Azure / GCP / Docker / Kubernetes).","Implementation of automated test suites (unit testing, integration testing, API testing).","Performance optimization, load testing, and latency benchmarking.","Implementation of cloud security hardening, encryption, and authentication controls.","Authoring formal capstone project thesis following academic formatting standards.","Project defense presentation and live demonstration before External and Internal Examiners."]}

subject.name: Summer Project Seminar-III
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To evaluate senior summer training / pre-placement internship completed between Year III and Year IV."],"outcomes":["Present technical advancements, corporate workflows, and project outcomes from senior industrial training."],"labExperiments":["Submission of senior industrial internship certificate and technical documentation.","Slide deck presentation illustrating industrial tools, cloud technologies, and corporate engineering practices.","Live demonstration of contributions made to live corporate projects.","Oral viva-voce assessing professional engineering readiness and technical problem-solving."]}

subject.name: Industrial Training / Internship
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To provide students with intensive full-semester industrial immersion, live industry project exposure, and corporate software engineering practices."],"outcomes":["Work effectively within multidisciplinary professional engineering teams in industry.","Apply cloud engineering, software development, and quality assurance principles to production systems.","Author comprehensive industrial internship project reports and defend professional achievements."],"labExperiments":["Full-semester corporate onboarding and assignment to live engineering development team.","Participation in daily Agile stand-ups, sprint planning, and code review processes.","Contributing to production codebase: feature development, bug fixes, automated testing, and CI/CD deployment.","Bi-weekly progress monitoring and submission of mentor evaluation reports.","Authoring formal Industrial Training Dissertation detailing technical contributions.","Final industrial project defense and viva-voce before university evaluation committee."]}

subject.name: Project
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To design and deliver a comprehensive final-year capstone project or advanced research contribution in Cloud Computing / Intelligent Systems."],"outcomes":["Synthesize four years of computer science and cloud computing knowledge into an impactful software or research system.","Conduct thorough benchmarking, security validation, and deployment on production cloud infrastructure.","Defend final thesis and publish research outcomes or open-source software artifacts."],"labExperiments":["Advanced architecture realization and full-stack cloud implementation.","Automated deployment using Kubernetes or cloud serverless container architectures.","Comprehensive performance stress testing, security auditing, and penetration validation.","Preparation of final university thesis document compliant with academic publication standards.","Demonstration of working production solution, oral defense, and comprehensive viva-voce."]}

subject.name: Agile Technology
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To introduce Agile software development philosophies, Scrum framework, Extreme Programming (XP), Kanban, and DevOps continuous delivery."],"outcomes":["Contrast traditional Waterfall with Agile methodologies and apply Agile Manifesto principles.","Facilitate Scrum ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, and Retrospective.","Utilize user stories, story pointing, velocity metrics, and burndown charts in Jira."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Fundamentals of Agile Methodology","topics":"Shortcomings of traditional Waterfall models; Agile Manifesto: 4 core values and 12 principles; Agile vs. Traditional; Iterative and incremental development; Agile project management lifecycle; Overview of Agile frameworks (Scrum, Kanban, XP, Lean)."},{"title":"Unit 2: Scrum Framework","topics":"Scrum roles: Product Owner, Scrum Master, Development Team; Scrum artifacts: Product Backlog, Sprint Backlog, Increment; Scrum ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Standup, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective; Definition of Ready (DoR) and Definition of Done (DoD)."},{"title":"Unit 3: Agile Requirements & Estimation","topics":"Writing effective User Stories; INVEST criteria for user stories; Epics, Features, and Themes; Acceptance criteria; Agile estimation techniques: Planning Poker, T-shirt sizing, Bucket system; Story points vs. hours; Velocity and Burn-down / Burn-up charts."},{"title":"Unit 4: Extreme Programming & Engineering Practices","topics":"Core values of XP; Test-Driven Development (TDD): Red-Green-Refactor cycle; Pair Programming; Continuous Integration (CI); Refactoring techniques and code smells; Collective code ownership; Simple design."},{"title":"Unit 5: Kanban & Scaling Agile","topics":"Kanban principles: Visualizing workflow, Limiting Work in Progress (WIP), Managing flow, Making policies explicit; Cumulative Flow Diagrams (CFD); Scaling Agile for enterprises: Introduction to SAFe (Scaled Agile Framework) and Spotify engineering culture model."}],"textBooks":["Ken Schawber & Mike Beedle, 'Agile Software Development with Scrum', Pearson.","Mike Cohn, 'User Stories Applied: For Agile Software Development', Addison-Wesley."],"referenceBooks":["Kent Beck, 'Extreme Programming Explained: Embrace Change', Addison-Wesley."]}

subject.name: Metaverse
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To explore virtual worlds, spatial computing, augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), digital avatars, and blockchain economies in the Metaverse."],"outcomes":["Understand the technological building blocks and 7 layers of the Metaverse value chain.","Analyze spatial audio, 3D graphics rendering engines (Unity/Unreal), and HMD hardware.","Assess decentralized identity, digital asset ownership, and spatial computing ethics."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Introduction to Metaverse & Spatial Computing","topics":"Evolution of cyberspace; Defining Metaverse: Characteristics, interoperability, persistence, and synchronicity; Jon Radoff's 7 Layers of Metaverse; Extended Reality (XR) continuum: Augmented Reality (AR), Virtual Reality (VR), Mixed Reality (MR)."},{"title":"Unit 2: XR Hardware & 3D Interactive Engines","topics":"Head-Mounted Displays (HMD): Optics, refresh rate, field of view (FOV), tracking (3 DoF vs. 6 DoF, inside-out tracking); Spatial audio and haptics; 3D Game Engines: Overview of Unity 3D and Unreal Engine 5; Scene graphs, lighting, shaders, and physics simulation."},{"title":"Unit 3: Digital Avatars & Virtual Presence","topics":"Avatar creation and customization; Rigging and motion capture; Facial tracking and eye tracking; Social VR platforms (VRChat, Horizon Worlds, Decentraland); Telepresence and collaborative virtual workspaces."},{"title":"Unit 4: Metaverse Economy & Decentralized Technologies","topics":"Virtual goods economy; Role of Blockchain in Metaverse; Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) for digital asset ownership and land parcels; Smart contracts for virtual commerce; Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs) in virtual governance."},{"title":"Unit 5: Challenges & Future of Metaverse","topics":"Technical challenges: Network bandwidth, 5G/6G, low latency edge rendering; Interoperability standards (OpenXR, glTF, USD); Privacy, cybersecurity, and identity theft in virtual spaces; Ethics, digital addiction, and regulatory considerations."}],"textBooks":["Matthew Ball, 'The Metaverse: And How It Will Revolutionize Everything', Liveright Publishing.","Tony Parisi, 'Learning Virtual Reality', O'Reilly Media."],"referenceBooks":["Paul Mealy, 'Virtual & Augmented Reality For Dummies', John Wiley & Sons."]}

subject.name: Blockchain Technology
subject.syllabusDetails: {"objectives":["To teach cryptographic foundations, distributed ledgers, consensus algorithms (PoW, PoS), Ethereum smart contracts, and decentralized applications (DApps)."],"outcomes":["Explain hashing, digital signatures, and Merkle tree structures in blockchain ledgers.","Contrast consensus mechanisms: Proof of Work (PoW), Proof of Stake (PoS), and PBFT.","Author and deploy Solidity smart contracts on Ethereum test networks."],"modules":[{"title":"Unit 1: Cryptographic Foundations & Distributed Systems","topics":"Evolution of centralized vs. decentralized systems; Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT); Cryptographic primitives: Hash functions (SHA-256), cryptographic properties; Digital Signatures (ECDSA); Public/Private key pairs; Merkle Trees and Merkle Roots."},{"title":"Unit 2: Blockchain Architecture & Bitcoin","topics":"Block anatomy: Block header, previous hash, timestamp, nonce, difficulty target, transaction list; Blockchain lifecycle; Peer-to-peer network topology; Bitcoin: UTXO model, script language, transaction validation, mining process, difficulty retargeting, 51% attacks, hard and soft forks."},{"title":"Unit 3: Consensus Mechanisms","topics":"Byzantine Generals Problem; Crash fault tolerance vs. Byzantine fault tolerance; Proof of Work (PoW); Proof of Stake (PoS); Delegated Proof of Stake (DPoS); Proof of Authority (PoA); Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT); Environmental and energy considerations."},{"title":"Unit 4: Ethereum & Smart Contracts","topics":"Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM); Gas mechanism, gas price, gas limit; Accounts: Externally Owned Accounts (EOA) vs. Contract Accounts; Solidity programming language: Data types, variables, functions, modifiers, events, inheritance; Writing and compiling smart contracts with Remix IDE."},{"title":"Unit 5: DApps & Enterprise Blockchains","topics":"Decentralized Applications (DApps) architecture: Web3.js, Ethers.js, MetaMask; ERC standards: ERC-20 (fungible tokens), ERC-721 (NFTs); Enterprise blockchains: Hyperledger Fabric architecture, channels, chaincode, membership services; Real-world blockchain applications in supply chain, finance, and healthcare."}],"textBooks":["Arvind Narayanan et al., 'Bitcoin and Cryptocurrency Technologies: A Comprehensive Introduction', Princeton University Press.","Andreas M. Antonopoulos & Gavin Wood, 'Mastering Ethereum: Building Smart Contracts and DApps', O'Reilly Media."],"referenceBooks":["Imran Bashir, 'Mastering Blockchain', 3rd Edition, Packt Publishing."]}
